text: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
desc: The first promise in Scripture — Eve given a Saviour: the woman's seed shall bruise the serpent's head, and be bruised in the heel.
hebrewKey: זֶרַע (zera') — seed/offspring; שׁוּף (shuf) — crush/bruise
archaeology: Sumerian and Akkadian creation texts confirm the antiquity of the 'seed' concept, making this the earliest promise of a Deliverer in biblical literature.
trad_Jewish: Etiological narrative about human-serpent enmity. Not Messianic in mainstream Judaism.
trad_Catholic: The Protoevangelium — first promise of a Savior; Mary as 'the woman' in Marian theology.
trad_Protestant: The first gospel — points to Christ's victory over Satan at the cross.
trad_Oneness: Jesus Christ crushed Satan at the cross and resurrection.
trad_Dispensational: Ultimate fulfillment at Second Coming when Satan is cast into the lake of fire (Rev 20:10).
trad_Academic: ANE etiological narrative; Messianic reading is a later hermeneutic.

text: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.
desc: In Abraham all families of the earth blessed — the gospel preached beforehand to Abraham (Galatians 3:8).
hebrewKey: בָּרַךְ (barak) — bless; כָּל מִשְׁפְּחֹת (kol mishpechot) — all families
archaeology: The Mari Tablets (18th century BC) corroborate covenant-making customs of this patriarchal era.
trad_Jewish: God's blessing to Abraham's literal descendants — the foundational Abrahamic covenant.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Jesus, descendant of Abraham; salvation extended to all nations.
trad_Protestant: The Abrahamic covenant finds ultimate expression in Christ (Gal 3:16).
trad_Dispensational: Dual: national blessing for Israel PLUS spiritual blessing through Christ for all peoples.
trad_Academic: Part of the J-source Abrahamic cycle; universalized in later redaction.

text: The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.
desc: The sceptre not departing from Judah until Shiloh come — the Messiah arriving while Judah still held its identity.
hebrewKey: שֵׁבֶט (shevet) — scepter/tribe; שִׁילֹה (Shiloh) — 'he whose it is' (disputed)
trad_Jewish: Davidic dynasty continuation. Not clearly Messianic in mainstream Judaism.
trad_Catholic: Kingship belongs to Judah until the Messiah arrives.
trad_Protestant: Fulfilled in Jesus of the tribe of Judah — the Lion of Judah (Rev 5:5).
trad_Dispensational: Fully fulfilled when Christ rules all nations in the Millennium.
trad_Academic: Tribal blessing poem; 'Shiloh' is a textual crux with no scholarly consensus.

text: I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel, and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.
desc: A Star out of Jacob and a Sceptre out of Israel — the Messiah, foretold by a hired prophet against his employer's intent.
hebrewKey: כּוֹכָב (kokhav) — star; שֵׁבֶט (shevet) — scepter
archaeology: The Mesha Stele (840 BC) confirms Moab's historical conflicts with Israel referenced in this passage.
trad_Jewish: Applied to Bar Kokhba ('son of a star') in AD 135; also seen as referring to David.
trad_Catholic: The star of Bethlehem; the Magi followed this prophecy.
trad_Protestant: Balaam unknowingly prophesied the Star of Jacob — Christ.
trad_Dispensational: Full military fulfillment at the Second Coming.
trad_Academic: Royal oracle about a conquering Israelite king; David is the most likely original referent.

text: And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.
desc: The Davidic covenant: David's seed raised up and his kingdom established — fulfilled in Solomon's throne and finally in Christ, David's greater Son.
hebrewKey: זֶרַע (zera') — offspring; כִּסֵּא (kisse) — throne; עוֹלָם (olam) — forever/eternal
archaeology: The Tel Dan Inscription (9th century BC) — the earliest extra-biblical reference to the House of David.
trad_Jewish: Partially fulfilled in Solomon; full fulfillment awaits the Messiah ben David.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Jesus, the eternal King of the Davidic dynasty (Luke 1:32).
trad_Protestant: The Davidic Covenant — ultimately fulfilled in Christ's eternal kingdom.
trad_Dispensational: Partially now; fully in the Millennium on David's literal throne in Jerusalem.
trad_Academic: Royal theology of ancient Judah; eschatologized over centuries of transmission.

text: But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.
desc: Bethlehem Ephratah to bring forth the ruler whose goings forth are from everlasting — the verse Herod's scribes quoted when he asked where Christ should be born (Matthew 2:5-6).
hebrewKey: בֵּית-לֶחֶם (Beit Lechem) — house of bread; מִקֶּדֶם (miqqedem) — from ancient times/eternity
archaeology: Excavations at Bethlehem confirm an ancient Bronze Age settlement.
trad_Jewish: Future Davidic king; Jesus does not meet all Messianic criteria.
trad_Catholic: One of the most explicit OT Messianic prophecies. Chief priests cited it to Herod (Matt 2:5).
trad_Protestant: Named city 700 years in advance — extraordinary specificity.
trad_Oneness: "from everlasting" points to the pre-existent deity of Jesus — not a second eternal person but the one eternal God who chose to manifest in the flesh through the Incarnation. The Bethlehem birth is God himself entering human history.
trad_Academic: Some question whether Matthew's account was shaped by Micah rather than Micah predicting it.

text: Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
desc: A virgin shall conceive and bear a son called Immanuel — the sign given to Ahaz, applied by Matthew to the birth of Christ.
hebrewKey: עַלְמָה (almah) — young woman/maiden (LXX: παρθένος parthenos — virgin)
trad_Jewish: 'Almah' means young woman, not necessarily virgin. The sign was for Ahaz's time.
trad_Catholic: The LXX uses 'parthenos' (virgin). Fulfilled in the virginal conception of Jesus.
trad_Protestant: Matthew's inspired reading confirms Messianic fulfillment.
trad_Oneness: 'Immanuel' (God with us) — the Incarnation of God himself in human flesh.
trad_Academic: Original context was a sign for Ahaz. Matthew applies pesher-style interpretation.

keywords: child born|Mighty God|Everlasting Father|Prince of Peace|government|eternal|divine names
text: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.
desc: A child born, a son given, called The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace — the Messiah, and a cornerstone of the Oneness reading of the Godhead.
hebrewKey: אֵל גִּבּוֹר (El Gibbor) — Mighty God; אֲבִי עַד (Avi Ad) — Everlasting Father; שַׂר שָׁלוֹם (Sar Shalom) — Prince of Peace
trad_Jewish: Throne names for a Davidic king — hyperbolic royal titles, not literal divine attributes.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Jesus Christ; the divine names confirm his deity.
trad_Protestant: The divine titles exceed any human king — predictive of the divine Messiah.
trad_Oneness: 'Everlasting Father' — Jesus IS the Father incarnate; a foundational Oneness Christology text.
trad_Dispensational: Partially at first coming; the 'government on his shoulders' = full Millennial reign.
trad_Academic: ANE throne-name oracle; divine hyperbole common in royal texts.

text: The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.
desc: A voice crying in the wilderness to prepare the way of the LORD — John the Baptist, who claimed this verse for himself (John 1:23).
hebrewKey: פַּנּוּ (pannu) — clear/prepare; דֶּרֶךְ (derekh) — way/road
trad_Jewish: Originally about the return from Babylon.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in John the Baptist as the forerunner; cited in all four Gospels.
trad_Protestant: All four Gospels cite this of John the Baptist — unambiguous fulfillment.
trad_Oneness: John prepared the way for Jesus, who IS the LORD (YHWH) himself come in the flesh.
trad_Academic: Originally about Cyrus; NT authors apply it typologically to John the Baptist.

text: Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in: behold, he shall come, saith the LORD of hosts.
desc: A messenger sent to prepare the way, and the Lord suddenly coming to his temple — John the Baptist, named from this verse in Mark 1:2 and Matthew 11:10.
hebrewKey: מַלְאָךְ (malakh) — messenger/angel; פִּנָּה (pinna) — prepare; הֵיכָל (hekhal) — temple
trad_Jewish: Refers to Elijah returning before the Day of the LORD — not yet fulfilled.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in John the Baptist as the forerunner of Christ.
trad_Protestant: Jesus explicitly identifies John the Baptist as this messenger (Matt 11:10).
trad_Oneness: John prepared the way for Jesus, who is YHWH himself coming to his temple.
trad_Academic: John the Baptist consciously modeled himself on this prophetic role.

text: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD:
desc: Elijah sent before the great and dreadful day of the LORD — applied by Jesus to John the Baptist (Matthew 11:14).
hebrewKey: אֵלִיָּהוּ (Eliyahu) — Elijah; הַגָּדוֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא (ha-gadol ve-hanora) — great and dreadful
archaeology: This is the final verse of the Hebrew canon (Tanakh ends with Malachi). Read at every Passover Seder.
trad_Jewish: Elijah must literally return before the Messiah — he has not; so the Messiah has not yet come.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in John the Baptist (in the spirit of Elijah); literal Elijah may return before Second Coming.
trad_Protestant: Dual: John was 'the Elijah to come' but Elijah also still comes (Matt 17:11).
trad_Dispensational: John = partial; literal Elijah returns as one of the Two Witnesses (Rev 11) before Tribulation.
trad_Academic: A scribal addition linking Mosaic and Elijah traditions to close the Hebrew canon.

text: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound;
desc: The Spirit of the Lord GOD upon the anointed one to preach good tidings — the passage Jesus read in the Nazareth synagogue and claimed as fulfilled that day.
hebrewKey: מָשַׁח (mashach) — anointed (= Messiah/Christ); בָּשַׂר (basar) — proclaim good news/gospel
trad_Jewish: Refers to Isaiah himself or a future deliverer; 'day of vengeance' has not yet occurred.
trad_Catholic: Jesus explicitly claims fulfillment in Luke 4:21.
trad_Protestant: Jesus deliberately stopped before 'the day of vengeance' — announcing partial fulfillment now.
trad_Oneness: The Spirit upon the servant IS the Spirit of the Lord YHWH — not a second person anointing a third person, but God manifesting in his own anointed servant-form. The Jubilee proclamation is YHWH himself setting captives free.
trad_Dispensational: Year of favor = Church Age; vengeance = Tribulation/Second Coming.
trad_Academic: Isaiah's servant commission; Jesus adapted it for his own Messianic self-understanding.

text: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.
desc: Eyes of the blind opened, ears of the deaf unstopped, the lame man leaping — the works Jesus cites when John's disciples ask if he is the one.
hebrewKey: עֵינֵי עִוְרִים (einei ivrim) — eyes of the blind; פִּסֵּחַ (pisseyach) — lame person
trad_Jewish: Messianic age blessings; not all signs fulfilled.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Jesus' healing miracles.
trad_Protestant: Jesus used Isaiah 35 as his Messianic answer to John the Baptist (Luke 7:22).
trad_Academic: Poetic restoration vision; Jesus may have deliberately enacted these as symbolic claims.

text: Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth; I have put my spirit upon him: he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles.
desc: Behold my servant, mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth — the Messiah, and the words spoken over Jesus at his baptism.
hebrewKey: עֶבֶד (eved) — servant; בָּחִיר (bachir) — chosen one; מִשְׁפָּט (mishpat) — justice
trad_Jewish: The servant = corporate Israel or a historical individual.
trad_Catholic: Matthew explicitly cites this of Jesus at length (12:17-21).
trad_Protestant: First of four 'Servant Songs'; fulfilled in Christ's gentle, Spirit-anointed ministry.
trad_Academic: Deutero-Isaiah's servant poetry; identity debated.

text: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.
desc: Thy King cometh unto thee, lowly and riding upon an ass — the triumphal entry (Matthew 21:5).
hebrewKey: עָנִי (ani) — humble/lowly; חֲמוֹר (chamor) — donkey; עַיִר (ayir) — colt/foal
archaeology: Josephus confirms royal entries into Jerusalem. The Palm Sunday route from Bethphage down the Mount of Olives is confirmed by topography.
trad_Jewish: Future Messianic king — Jesus did not fulfill v.10 (universal peace).
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled at the Triumphal Entry; v.10 awaits the Second Coming.
trad_Protestant: Literal fulfillment — Jesus deliberately enacted this to make a Messianic claim.
trad_Oneness: The King is YHWH himself (Zech. 14:9 — "the LORD shall be king"). His entry into Jerusalem in Jesus' name fulfills Psalm 118:26 ("blessed is he who comes in the name of the LORD") — confirming Jesus IS the LORD.
trad_Academic: Jesus consciously staged a royal entry as a Messianic demonstration.

text: And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my price; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver.
desc: Thirty pieces of silver weighed for the shepherd's price — the sum paid to Judas for Jesus (Matthew 26:15).
hebrewKey: שְׁלֹשִׁים כֶּסֶף (sheloshim kesef) — thirty silver; יוֹצֵר (yotser) — potter
trad_Jewish: Historical incident in Zechariah's prophetic drama.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Judas' betrayal for 30 silver coins and the purchase of Potter's Field.
trad_Protestant: Matthew cites this as fulfilled — one of the most striking specific prophecies.
trad_Oneness: The one being betrayed is YHWH himself — "the LORD said to me" (v.13). The money is "thrown to the potter in the house of the LORD." Matthew 27:9-10 cites this as fulfilled in Judas' betrayal of Jesus. YHWH was sold for 30 pieces of silver = Jesus is YHWH.
trad_Academic: Matthew's composite citation (Jeremiah + Zechariah) reflects midrashic method.

text: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my roaring?
desc: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me — a psalm sung in Israel, and the words Jesus cried from the cross, opening a description of crucifixion written centuries before it.
hebrewKey: כָּאֲרִי/כָּארוּ (ka'ari/kaaru) — 'like a lion' (MT) vs. 'they pierced' (DSS) — the central textual debate
archaeology: The Dead Sea Scrolls reading of Psalm 22:16 (kaaru — 'they pierced') predates Jesus and supports the Messianic reading.
trad_Jewish: Personal lament of David about his own suffering.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Christ's passion; quoted or alluded to seven times in the NT Passion narratives.
trad_Protestant: The specificity — lots, piercing, mockery, Jesus' exact words — far exceeds David's experience.
trad_Oneness: Jesus quoted Ps 22:1 from the cross, fully identifying with human abandonment.
trad_Academic: The DSS supports 'pierced' reading, making Messianic coincidence remarkable even to critics.

text: He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not.
desc: Despised and rejected of men, a man of sorrows — read by Christians of Christ, and one of the most contested passages between Christian and Jewish interpreters.
hebrewKey: מְחֹלָל (mecholal) — pierced/profaned; פֶּשַׁע (pesha) — transgression
archaeology: The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a, c. 125 BC) from Qumran preserves Isaiah 53 completely unchanged — pre-Christian proof the text predates Jesus by over a century.
trad_Jewish: Corporate Israel suffering among the nations.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Jesus' passion and atoning death.
trad_Protestant: The clearest OT prediction of vicarious atonement.
trad_Oneness: Every detail fulfilled in Jesus; his death provides the foundation for New Birth salvation.
trad_Academic: The Great Isaiah Scroll proves this text is pre-Christian.

text: The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.
desc: The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand — the Old Testament verse quoted most often in the New, and Jesus' own question the Pharisees could not answer.
hebrewKey: יְהוָה (YHWH) — the LORD; אֲדֹנִי (adoni) — my lord; מַלְכִּי-צֶדֶק (Malki-Tzedek) — Melchizedek
trad_Jewish: Two human lords: YHWH and David's lord (a royal figure). Not a divine Messiah.
trad_Catholic: Most cited OT text in the NT (33+ times); fulfilled in Christ's ascension and session.
trad_Protestant: Jesus used this to show Messiah must be greater than David (Matt 22:44).
trad_Oneness: YHWH speaks to Jesus; demonstrates Jesus' exaltation.
trad_Academic: Royal enthronement Psalm; Messianic interpretation developed in Second Temple Judaism.

text: And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions:
desc: The Spirit poured out upon all flesh, sons and daughters prophesying — the passage Peter preaches at Pentecost as fulfilled that day (Acts 2:16).
hebrewKey: שָׁפַךְ (shaphak) — pour out; רוּחַ (ruach) — Spirit/breath/wind; נָבָא (nava) — prophesy
trad_Jewish: The 'great and dreadful day of the LORD' has not yet occurred — not fully fulfilled.
trad_Oneness: Fulfilled at Acts 2; continues in every Spirit baptism with tongues.
trad_Dispensational: Acts 2 is analogous/partial; full fulfillment for national Israel during the Tribulation.
trad_Academic: Joel's apocalyptic vision; Peter's citation in Acts 2 is creative contextual reapplication.

keywords: new heart|new spirit|heart of stone|heart of flesh|Holy Spirit|indwelling|regeneration
text: A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.
desc: A new heart and a new spirit, the heart of stone taken away — the new birth Jesus presses on Nicodemus and Peter preaches in Acts 2:38.
hebrewKey: לֵב חָדָשׁ (lev chadash) — new heart; לֵב הָאֶבֶן (lev ha'even) — heart of stone
trad_Jewish: Awaits the Messianic age when Israel will be fully restored.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in baptism and confirmation.
trad_Protestant: Fulfilled in the new covenant — the Spirit indwells every believer who trusts Christ.
trad_Oneness: Fulfilled in the New Birth — Spirit baptism places God's Spirit within the believer.
trad_Dispensational: Partially in the Church Age; fully for national Israel in the Millennium.
trad_Academic: Ezekiel's pastoral theology for exiles; NT writers apply it to individual regeneration.

text: For I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground: I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring:
desc: Water poured on the thirsty and God's Spirit poured upon Israel's seed — water and Spirit together, the pair Jesus makes necessary in John 3:5.
hebrewKey: יָצַק (yatsaq) — pour out; רוּחַ (ruach) — Spirit
trad_Jewish: God's promise of blessing and renewal for Israel's restoration.
trad_Catholic: The Spirit poured out through Christ on all believers.
trad_Protestant: Fulfilled at Pentecost; John 7:38-39 explicitly connects 'living water' to the Spirit.
trad_Oneness: The Spirit outpouring of Acts 2 fulfills this promise of water on dry ground.
trad_Academic: Restoration oracle using water/rain imagery; applied to Pentecost by NT writers.

fulfillmentRefs: 1948 State of Israel|Return from Babylon 538 BC|Acts 2
text: The hand of the LORD was upon me, and carried me out in the spirit of the LORD, and set me down in the midst of the valley which was full of bones,
desc: The valley of dry bones: a nation shown as a graveyard, then brought together and made to live — Israel's prophesied return.
hebrewKey: עֲצָמוֹת (atsamot) — bones; נָשַׁב (nashav) — breathe/blow; חָיָה (chayah) — live/revive
archaeology: The State of Israel was declared on May 14, 1948 — cited by Dispensationalists as a remarkable modern fulfillment.
trad_Jewish: Full regathering of all twelve tribes under a Davidic king — still future.
trad_Oneness: The breath = Holy Spirit (Acts 2); national fulfillment still future.
trad_Dispensational: 1948 = bones coming together without the Spirit yet; Second Coming = Spirit breathed in.
trad_Academic: Vision of national restoration for Babylonian exiles.

keywords: new covenant|law in hearts|Israel|Judah|forgiveness|know the LORD|mind|not like Moses
text: Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah:
desc: A new covenant with Israel and Judah, not like the one their fathers broke — quoted in full in Hebrews 8.
hebrewKey: בְּרִית חֲדָשָׁה (berit chadashah) — new covenant; תּוֹרָה (torah) — law/instruction
trad_Jewish: Still future; fulfilled when literal national Israel keeps Torah perfectly in the Messianic age.
trad_Catholic: Inaugurated by Christ at the Last Supper; fulfilled in the Church through the sacraments.
trad_Protestant: Fulfilled in the New Testament — Hebrews quotes this as the basis of the new covenant.
trad_Oneness: Fulfilled in Acts 2 — the Spirit writes God's law on hearts through the New Birth.
trad_Dispensational: Partially fulfilled with the Church; fully with national Israel in the Millennium.
trad_Academic: Jeremiah's vision of inner transformation; appropriated by the NT.

fulfillmentRefs: 539 BC Cyrus conquest|Modern Babylon ruins Iraq
text: And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees' excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.
desc: Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, to be as Sodom and Gomorrah — a desolation whose completeness is still argued over.
hebrewKey: צְבִי (tsvi) — jewel/glory; נֶהְפַּךְ (nehpak) — overthrown; לְנֵצַח (le-netsach) — forever/perpetually
archaeology: Modern excavations near Hillah, Iraq confirm permanent desolation. Unlike Damascus (still inhabited), Babylon has never been continuously occupied since late antiquity.
trad_Jewish: Fulfilled in Babylon's fall to Cyrus (539 BC) and permanent desolation.
trad_Catholic: Historically verified — Babylon became permanently desolate exactly as Isaiah said.
trad_Protestant: Babylon's permanent desolation while ancient Damascus still stands is remarkable.
trad_Dispensational: Some see a future 'Mystery Babylon' (Rev 17-18) requiring a literal re-founded Babylon.
trad_Academic: Possibly composed after Babylon's decline; the permanent desolation detail is striking.

text: And this whole land shall be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.
desc: Seventy years of service to Babylon — the span Daniel later counts (Daniel 9:2).
hebrewKey: שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה (shivim shanah) — seventy years; שָׁמֵם (shamem) — desolate
archaeology: The Cyrus Cylinder (539 BC, British Museum) records Cyrus' policy of releasing exiled peoples.
trad_Jewish: Fulfilled exactly — Daniel read Jeremiah and calculated the exile's end (Dan 9:2).
trad_Catholic: One of the most precisely fulfilled prophecies; confirmed by the Cyrus Cylinder.
trad_Protestant: The 70-year exactness is remarkable.
trad_Academic: The 70 years may be symbolic; the return under Cyrus is historically confirmed.

text: Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I am against thee, O Tyrus, and will cause many nations to come up against thee, as the sea causeth his waves to come up.
desc: Many nations brought against Tyre as the sea casteth up its waves — a city broken by empire after empire, and the most closely contested fulfillment in the catalogue.
hebrewKey: סֶלַע (sela) — bare rock; גָּרַד (garad) — scrape clean
archaeology: Alexander literally scraped Tyre's rubble into the sea to build a causeway — confirmed by Arrian's Anabasis Alexandri and modern marine archaeology.
trad_Jewish: Historical multi-stage fulfillment over centuries.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled by Nebuchadnezzar (mainland) and Alexander the Great (island) — scraped literally bare.
trad_Protestant: One of the most detailed and remarkably fulfilled prophecies in Scripture.
trad_Academic: v.14 ('never rebuilt') is complicated by Tyre's partial survival as a city.

fulfillmentRefs: 612 BC Fall of Nineveh to Babylon and Medes
text: Woe to the bloody city! it is all full of lies and robbery; the prey departeth not;
desc: Woe to the bloody city, full of lies and robbery — Nineveh, which fell in 612 BC.
hebrewKey: עִיר הַדָּמִים (ir ha-damim) — city of blood; שֶׁקֶר (sheqer) — lies
archaeology: The fall of Nineveh (612 BC) is confirmed by the Babylonian Chronicle (British Museum, BM 21901). Destroyed by fire and flood exactly as Nahum predicted.
trad_Jewish: Historical prophecy; Nineveh's fall in 612 BC matches the description remarkably.
trad_Protestant: The joy at Nineveh's fall — historically noted — matches Nahum 3:19 precisely.
trad_Academic: May have been written close to events; the Babylonian Chronicle confirms the broad accuracy.

text: That saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure: even saying to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be built; and to the temple, Thy foundation shall be laid.
desc: Cyrus named as God's shepherd who would order Jerusalem rebuilt — a king named roughly 150 years before his birth.
hebrewKey: כּוֹרֶשׁ (Koresh) — Cyrus; רֹעִי (ro'i) — my shepherd; מָשִׁיחַ (mashiach) — anointed
archaeology: The Cyrus Cylinder (539 BC, British Museum) explicitly confirms Cyrus' policy of restoring temples. Cyrus is named in Isaiah approximately 150 years before his birth.
trad_Jewish: Josephus reports Cyrus read this text and was moved to act.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled precisely — Cyrus named 150 years before birth.
trad_Protestant: The naming of Cyrus 150 years in advance is one of the strongest evidences for predictive prophecy.
trad_Dispensational: Cyrus as a type of Christ — the deliverer of God's people from captivity.
trad_Academic: Critical scholars argue Deutero-Isaiah wrote this section after Cyrus appeared (~550 BC).

text: I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.
desc: One like the Son of man coming with the clouds to the Ancient of days — the title Jesus took for himself, and the verse he quoted at his trial (Mark 14:62).
hebrewKey: בַּר אֱנָשׁ (bar enash) — son of man (Aramaic); עֲנָנֵי שְׁמַיָּא (ananei shemaya) — clouds of heaven
trad_Jewish: 'Son of man' = angelic representative of Israel or the Jewish people collectively.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Christ's ascension (receiving authority) and future Second Coming.
trad_Protestant: Jesus claimed to be this Son of Man before the Sanhedrin (Matt 26:64).
trad_Dispensational: The receiving of the kingdom = Second Coming; fully established in the Millennium.
trad_Academic: Apocalyptic vision from the Maccabean period (c. 165 BC).

text: Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.
desc: Seventy weeks to finish transgression and bring in everlasting righteousness — the timetable to Messiah, and the most debated chronology in Scripture.
hebrewKey: שָׁבֻעִים (shabuim) — sevens/weeks; חָתַךְ (chatak) — decreed/cut; מָשִׁיחַ (mashiach) — anointed/Messiah
archaeology: The Elephantine Papyri (5th century BC) confirm Persian-period Jewish chronology relevant to calculating the 70 weeks.
trad_Jewish: Future events; some rabbis see a Maccabean partial fulfillment.
trad_Oneness: The "Anointed One" (Messiah) who is "cut off" (v.26) is the one God dying in human flesh, and by that death He ends the sacrificial system, bearing it personally. The "he" who confirms the covenant and breaks it in the midst of the week (v.27) is not Christ but the antichrist — the seventieth week is his, not the Saviour's.
trad_Dispensational: 69 weeks fulfilled at Palm Sunday; gap; Week 70 = future 7-year Tribulation.
trad_Academic: Written during the Maccabean crisis (~165 BC).

fulfillmentRefs: AD 70 Roman destruction|Josephus Wars of the Jews 6.4-10
text: And Jesus said unto them, See ye not all these things? verily I say unto you, There shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.
desc: Not one stone left upon another — the temple's destruction, fulfilled in AD 70.
hebrewKey: N/A — Greek: λίθος (lithos) — stone; καταλυθήσεται (kataluthesetai) — thrown down/destroyed
archaeology: Josephus details the complete destruction of Herod's Temple by Titus in AD 70. Roman soldiers dismantled stones to retrieve melted gold.
trad_Jewish: Historically confirmed — the Temple was completely destroyed in AD 70.
trad_Catholic: Literally fulfilled in AD 70 — one of Jesus' most verifiably accurate predictions.
trad_Protestant: The precision of this prediction is extraordinary.
trad_Dispensational: Partially fulfilled in AD 70; the 'Great Tribulation' referenced in Matt 24:21 is still future.
trad_Academic: May be a vaticinium ex eventu, or Jesus was aware of Roman military tactics.

text: And he said, It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.
desc: Too light a thing to restore Israel only — the servant, Jesus, given for a light to the Gentiles and salvation unto the end of the earth.
hebrewKey: אוֹר גּוֹיִם (or goyim) — light of the nations; קְצֵה הָאָרֶץ (qetse ha-arets) — ends of the earth
trad_Jewish: The servant = Israel, commissioned to be a light to the nations.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Jesus and the Church's mission to all peoples.
trad_Protestant: Paul and Barnabas explicitly cite this as their mandate for Gentile mission (Acts 13:47).
trad_Oneness: Jesus, the servant, fulfilled this by sending the apostles to all nations.
trad_Academic: Deutero-Isaiah's universalist vision.

text: For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first:
desc: The Lord descending with a shout and the trump of God, the dead in Christ rising first — the catching-away of the church.
hebrewKey: N/A — Greek: ἁρπαγησόμεθα (harpagesometha) — caught up/seized; ἀπάντησιν (apantesin) — meeting
trad_Catholic: The general resurrection at the Last Day; no separate pre-Tribulation rapture.
trad_Dispensational: Pre-Tribulation Rapture — the Church removed before the 7-year Tribulation.
trad_Academic: Paul adapting imperial παρουσία (parousia) — royal arrival language.

text: And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand.
desc: An angel with the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain — the binding of Satan at the Millennium's beginning.
hebrewKey: N/A — Greek: χίλια ἔτη (chilia ete) — thousand years; δεσμός (desmos) — chain/bond
trad_Catholic: Official position (Catechism 676) is amillennial.
trad_Dispensational: Literal 1,000-year reign of Christ on earth after the Tribulation.

text: For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.
desc: New heavens and a new earth created, the former not remembered nor come into mind — God's promise of a remade creation.
hebrewKey: בָּרָא (bara) — create (same word as Genesis 1:1); חָדָשׁ (chadash) — new
trad_Jewish: Describes the coming Messianic age — wolves and lambs together — still future.
trad_Dispensational: New heavens and earth follow the Millennium and final judgment (Rev 21).
trad_Academic: Eschatological vision of restored creation borrowing from Genesis theology.

keywords: new heaven|new earth|new Jerusalem|sea no more|God dwells|tears|death no more|Holy City|bride
text: And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea.
desc: A new heaven and a new earth, the first passed away and no more sea — Isaiah's new heavens and new earth, seen arriving.
hebrewKey: N/A — Greek: καινὸς (kainos) — new/renewed; νύμφη (nymphe) — bride
trad_Catholic: The eschaton — the final state of redeemed creation dwelling with God.
trad_Dispensational: Future literal reality after Millennium and Great White Throne judgment.
trad_Academic: Apocalyptic vision drawing on Isaiah 65 and Jewish heavenly Jerusalem traditions.

text: In one house shall it be eaten; thou shalt not carry forth ought of the flesh abroad out of the house; neither shall ye break a bone thereof.
desc: Not a bone of the Passover lamb to be broken — kept at the cross, where the soldiers brake no bone of Jesus (John 19:36).
hebrewKey: עֶצֶם (etsem) — bone; שָׁבַר (shavar) — break; פֶּסַח (pesach) — Passover/pass over
archaeology: The Passover Seder has been continuously practiced for 3,400 years — the oldest continuously observed religious ceremony in history.
trad_Jewish: A legal requirement for the Passover lamb — not a Messianic prediction.
trad_Catholic: Typologically fulfilled in Christ — the Lamb of God whose bones were not broken (John 19:36).
trad_Protestant: Jesus is the true Passover Lamb (1 Cor 5:7).
trad_Oneness: Jesus is the Passover Lamb; the feast typology perfectly fulfilled in his sacrificial death.
trad_Academic: John's symbolic typology is deliberate; the historical detail may be accurate.

keywords: Pentecost|fifty days|Feast of Weeks|Shavuot|harvest|wave offering|new grain|firstfruits
text: And ye shall count unto you from the morrow after the sabbath, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering; seven sabbaths shall be complete:
desc: Fifty days counted from the sheaf to the feast of weeks — the calendar that sets Pentecost, the day the Spirit fell.
hebrewKey: חֲמִשִּׁים יוֹם (chamishim yom) — fifty days; שָׁבֻעוֹת (Shavuot) — Feast of Weeks
archaeology: The Qumran community placed great emphasis on the Feast of Weeks as the covenant renewal festival.
trad_Jewish: Shavuot celebrates the giving of Torah at Sinai; also a harvest festival.
trad_Catholic: Typologically fulfilled in the Spirit outpouring 50 days after Passover.
trad_Protestant: The feast foreshadows the Spirit outpouring at Pentecost.
trad_Oneness: Acts 2 occurs exactly on the Feast of Weeks — confirming it as the prophetic fulfillment.
trad_Academic: The timing of Acts 2 on the feast day is historically noted by scholars.

keywords: resurrection|everlasting life|shame|contempt|dust|awake|two destinations|wise shine like stars
text: And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
desc: Many that sleep in the dust shall awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame — the clearest statement of bodily resurrection in the Hebrew Bible.
hebrewKey: יָשֵׁן (yashen) — sleep; עָפָר (aphar) — dust; עוֹלָם (olam) — everlasting
trad_Jewish: Future general resurrection — confirms Jewish belief in bodily resurrection.
trad_Catholic: Confirms the two-destination resurrection doctrine.
trad_Protestant: The clearest OT statement of bodily resurrection and two-outcome final judgment.
trad_Dispensational: Two literal resurrections 1,000 years apart (Rev 20:4-5).
trad_Academic: Late Jewish apocalyptic (2nd century BC).

keywords: believed message|arm of the LORD|no beauty|no majesty|rejected|appearance|Israel disbelief
text: Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the LORD revealed?
desc: Who hath believed our report? — the Servant song's opening, quoted by John and Paul of Israel's unbelief.
hebrewKey: מִי הֶאֱמִין (mi he'emin) — who has believed; שֹׁרֶשׁ (shoresh) — root
trad_Jewish: The disbelief of the nations in Israel's message during exile.
trad_Catholic: John quotes this (12:38) to explain Israel's disbelief in Jesus.
trad_Protestant: Both John and Paul quote Isaiah 53:1 to explain the rejection of Jesus.
trad_Academic: John 12:38 explicitly cites this as the reason for disbelief.

keywords: Israel|many days|no king|no sacrifice|no ephod|no temple|dispersion|Diaspora|long exile
fulfillmentRefs: AD 70 onwards|Loss of Temple sacrifice|Jewish Diaspora
text: For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim:
desc: Israel to abide many days without king, prince, sacrifice or ephod — the long dispersion.
hebrewKey: יָמִים רַבִּים (yamim rabbim) — many days; מֶלֶךְ (melekh) — king; זֶבַח (zevach) — sacrifice
archaeology: The destruction of the Second Temple (AD 70) ended the Jewish sacrificial system. The Jewish people have lived without a king, sacrifice, or temple for nearly 2,000 years.
trad_Jewish: Describes the current state of the Jewish people — without Temple, sacrifice, or Davidic king.
trad_Catholic: The long Jewish dispersion without Temple worship is fulfilled.
trad_Protestant: One of the most remarkably specific prophecies — the Jewish people have lived exactly as Hosea described for 2,000 years.
trad_Dispensational: The next verse (Hos 3:5) promises the return — 1948 is the beginning of the restoration.
trad_Academic: Hosea's description of the Northern Kingdom's exile; broadly accurate in describing the Diaspora.

text: And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots:
desc: A rod out of the stem of Jesse, a Branch from his roots — a coming Davidic Saviour springing from a felled dynasty.
hebrewKey: חֹטֶר (choter) — shoot; נֵצֶר (netser) — Branch (also root of 'Nazareth'); גֵּזַע (geza) — stump/root
trad_Jewish: Future Davidic king in the Messianic age when peace reigns among animals (v.6). Not yet fulfilled.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Jesus, the Branch from Jesse's line (Matt 1:6), anointed with the Spirit at baptism.
trad_Protestant: The sevenfold Spirit resting on Jesus is explicitly shown at his baptism.
trad_Oneness: The Spirit resting on the Branch is not a third person given to a second person but the Spirit of YHWH (God's own presence and power) fully expressed in Jesus. "The Spirit of wisdom and understanding" describes the full divine nature dwelling in the Messiah — the one God in human manifestation.
trad_Dispensational: The peaceable kingdom of v.6-9 is the Millennial reign — only partially fulfilled at First Coming.
trad_Academic: Royal oracle about a future ideal Davidic king; the animal peace imagery is poetic/hyperbolic.

keywords: Branch|David|righteous|King|reign wisely|Judah saved|Israel safe|YHWH our Righteousness
text: Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.
desc: A righteous Branch raised unto David, a King reigning in judgment and justice — the Messiah of David's line.
hebrewKey: צֶמַח צַדִּיק (tsemach tsadiq) — righteous Branch; יְהוָה צִדְקֵנוּ (YHWH Tsidqenu) — The LORD Our Righteousness
trad_Jewish: A future Davidic king who brings national security — not yet fulfilled (Judah and Israel not yet unified under this king).
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Jesus, the righteous descendant of David who IS our righteousness.
trad_Protestant: Jesus fulfills the title 'The LORD Our Righteousness' (1 Cor 1:30).
trad_Dispensational: National salvation of 'Judah and Israel' awaits the Millennial reign.
trad_Academic: Jeremiah contrasts this ideal king with the unjust kings of his day, especially Jehoiakim.

keywords: Branch|servant|stone|seven eyes|Joshua|high priest|iniquity removed in single day
text: Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, thou, and thy fellows that sit before thee: for they are men wondered at: for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.
desc: My servant the BRANCH brought forth — the Messianic title given as a sign to Joshua the high priest and his fellows.
hebrewKey: עַבְדִּי צֶמַח (avdi tsemach) — my servant the Branch; אֶבֶן (even) — stone; עֵינַיִם (einayim) — eyes
trad_Jewish: This Branch is a future royal-priestly figure; Joshua the priest is a symbol. Not yet fulfilled.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Jesus who is both priest and king — the Branch who removes iniquity in one day (the cross).
trad_Protestant: Christ's priestly and kingly roles perfectly fulfill the Branch imagery.
trad_Dispensational: The Branch who builds the temple (Zech 6:12-13) = Christ building his Millennial temple.
trad_Academic: Post-exilic priestly-royal theology; 'the Branch' was likely Zerubbabel.

text: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre.
desc: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever — addressed to the king, and applied to the Son in Hebrews 1:8.
hebrewKey: כִּסְאֲךָ אֱלֹהִים (kiss'acha Elohim) — your throne, O God; עוֹלָם וָעֶד (olam va'ed) — forever and ever
trad_Jewish: A royal wedding song addressing the king with courtly hyperbole; the king is called 'god' as a title.
trad_Catholic: Hebrews 1:8 applies this directly to the Son — 'Your throne, O God, is forever and ever.'
trad_Protestant: The author of Hebrews explicitly interprets v.6 as addressed to Christ, confirming his deity.
trad_Oneness: This Psalm directly addresses Jesus as God — supports the full deity of Christ.
trad_Academic: ANE royal hyperbole; the king is called 'god' as a stylistic convention.

text: Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste.
desc: A tried stone, a precious corner stone laid in Zion — Christ the sure foundation, applied to him by both Peter and Paul.
hebrewKey: אֶבֶן בֹּחַן (even bochan) — tested stone; פִּנַּת יִקְרַת (pinnat yiqrat) — precious cornerstone
trad_Jewish: God's sure foundation for Zion against the 'covenant with death' made by faithless leaders.
trad_Catholic: Paul and Peter apply this to Christ as the cornerstone of the Church.
trad_Protestant: The New Testament applies this to Christ with consistent unanimity.
trad_Academic: Isaiah's polemic against the foreign-alliance policy of Ahaz's court.

keywords: bronze serpent|pole|look and live|Nehushtan|typology|lifted up|John 3:14|salvation by looking
text: And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.
desc: The brass serpent lifted on a pole that the bitten might look and live — the type Jesus applies to his own crucifixion (John 3:14).
hebrewKey: נְחַשׁ הַנְּחֹשֶׁת (nachash hanechoshet) — bronze serpent; נֵס (nes) — pole/standard
archaeology: The Nehushtan was preserved in the Temple until Hezekiah destroyed it (2 Kings 18:4). Similar pole-serpent symbols found in ANE medicine traditions.
trad_Jewish: A historical incident demonstrating faith-healing in the wilderness; not Messianic.
trad_Catholic: Jesus explicitly cites this as a type of his crucifixion (John 3:14).
trad_Protestant: The typology is authoritative because Jesus himself draws it.
trad_Oneness: Looking in faith to the crucified Christ for salvation perfectly mirrors the typology.
trad_Academic: An aetiological narrative explaining the Nehushtan artifact; John applies it Christologically.

text: Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and ye perish from the way, when his wrath is kindled but a little. Blessed are all they that put their trust in him.
desc: Kiss the Son, lest he be angry — the second psalm, which Paul preaches of the risen Christ (Acts 13:33).
hebrewKey: נַשְּׁקוּ-בַר (nashqu-var) — kiss the son (Aramaic loan word 'bar'); אַפּוֹ (appo) — his wrath
trad_Jewish: Addressed to Gentile kings who resist YHWH's anointed (Davidic) king.
trad_Catholic: 'The Son' = Christ; submission to him is required of all nations.
trad_Protestant: 'Bar' (son) in Aramaic within a Hebrew Psalm is unusual — suggests a very elevated figure.
trad_Dispensational: Full submission of all nations to Christ occurs at Second Coming.
trad_Academic: Royal enthronement Psalm; 'bar' may be a scribal variant. Its use of Aramaic 'son' is debated.

keywords: one shepherd|servant David|prince|flock|covenant of peace|tender|true shepherd
text: And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.
desc: One shepherd set over the flock, 'my servant David' — the Messiah, who said 'I am the good shepherd' (John 10:11).
hebrewKey: רֹעֶה אֶחָד (ro'eh echad) — one shepherd; עַבְדִּי דָוִד (avdi David) — my servant David
trad_Jewish: The Messiah (a future David-like figure) who gathers and tends scattered Israel.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Jesus, the Good Shepherd — a Davidic descendant who is the one shepherd.
trad_Protestant: Jesus claims to be the Good Shepherd (John 10:11) fulfilling this Ezekiel prophecy.
trad_Dispensational: The 'covenant of peace' and physical flourishing (v.25-29) point to the Millennial Kingdom.
trad_Academic: Ezekiel's critique of bad shepherds (corrupt leaders) and promise of a good one.

keywords: last days|mountain|temple|highest|peoples stream|nations come|Zion|swords into plowshares|law from Jerusalem
text: But in the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of the LORD shall be established in the top of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills; and people shall flow unto it.
desc: The mountain of the LORD's house established in the last days, all nations flowing unto it — the Millennial reign.
hebrewKey: בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים (be'acharit hayamim) — in the last days; נָהֲרוּ (naharu) — stream (like a river)
trad_Jewish: The Messianic age — not yet fulfilled.
trad_Catholic: Inaugurated in the Church (heavenly Zion) and consummated in the new creation.
trad_Protestant: Partially fulfilled in the global spread of the Gospel from Jerusalem.
trad_Dispensational: The Millennial Kingdom centered in Jerusalem.
trad_Academic: Identical text also in Isaiah 2:2-4; shared oracle between the two prophetic traditions.

keywords: return|seek the LORD|David their king|last days|trembling|blessings|Israel restored|Davidic king
text: Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the LORD their God, and David their king; and shall fear the LORD and his goodness in the latter days.
desc: Afterward Israel returns and seeks the LORD and David their king in the latter days — the regathering that answers the dispersion before it.
hebrewKey: אַחַר כֵּן (achar ken) — afterward; דָּוִד מַלְכָּם (David malcham) — David their king; יָרְאוּ (yare'u) — trembling/in awe
trad_Jewish: Israel's future return to YHWH and a Davidic king — still future.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled partially in Jewish conversions; fully at the end of time.
trad_Protestant: The national salvation of Israel (Romans 11:26) fulfills the 'afterward.'
trad_Dispensational: Fulfilled at the Second Coming when Israel nationally accepts Jesus as Messiah.
trad_Academic: Hosea 3 is his personal story of reconciliation used as an allegory for Israel.

text: I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.
desc: All nations gathered into the valley of Jehoshaphat — the nations answering at the end of the age for scattering Israel and parting his land.
hebrewKey: עֵמֶק יְהוֹשָׁפָט (Emek Yehoshafat) — Valley of Jehoshaphat; שָׁפַט (shaphat) — judge
archaeology: The 'Valley of Jehoshaphat' is traditionally identified with the Kidron Valley, though its prophetic geography is debated.
trad_Jewish: An end-time judgment of the nations for mistreating Israel.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in the final judgment at Christ's return.
trad_Protestant: The Great White Throne Judgment / Armageddon fulfills this.
trad_Dispensational: The Battle of Armageddon and subsequent Millennial judgment of nations (Matt 25:31-46).
trad_Academic: Apocalyptic poetry; the valley name likely coined from Jehoshaphat's victory in 2 Chronicles 20.

keywords: great multitude|every nation|white robes|palm branches|throne|Lamb|worship|Tribulation saints
text: After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands;
desc: A great multitude which no man could number, of all nations and kindreds and tongues, standing before the throne — washed in the blood of the Lamb and saved out of the great tribulation, serving day and night in his temple (Revelation 7:14-15).
hebrewKey: N/A — Greek: ὄχλος πολύς (ochlos polys) — great crowd; πᾶν ἔθνος (pan ethnos) — every nation
trad_Catholic: The saints in heaven — the elect from every people worshipping the Lamb.
trad_Dispensational: Tribulation martyrs from the 7-year Tribulation period.
trad_Academic: John's universal vision of salvation drawing on the Jewish Feast of Tabernacles imagery.

text: And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, … Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold I am against thee, O Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal: And I will turn thee back, and put hooks into thy jaws, and I will bring thee forth, and all thine army, horses and horsemen, all of them clothed with all sorts of armour, even a great company with bucklers and shields, all of them handling swords:
desc: The opening of the Gog oracle. The LORD sets Himself against Gog of the land of Magog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, turns him back with hooks in his jaws, and brings him with all his army against the mountains of Israel — where God Himself destroys him, and the nations learn who He is.
hebrewKey: גּוֹג (Gog) — Gog; מָגוֹג (Magog) — Magog; רֹאשׁ (rosh) — head/chief (disputed as 'Russia')
trad_Jewish: A future northern confederacy that invades Israel in the end times.
trad_Catholic: The final assault of evil upon the Church consummated at Christ's return.
trad_Dispensational: Likely Russia leading a coalition against Israel in the Tribulation.
trad_Academic: Gog may be Gyges of Lydia; Magog is a geographic/ethnic designation from Scythian tradition.

text: In that day shall there be an altar to the LORD in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof to the LORD.
desc: An altar to the LORD in the midst of Egypt — worship established among a nation that had enslaved Israel.
hebrewKey: מִזְבֵּחַ (mizbeyach) — altar; מַצֵּבָה (matsevah) — monument/pillar; לַיהוָה (la-YHWH) — to the LORD
archaeology: The Jewish temple at Elephantine (5th century BC), where Jews worshipped YHWH in Egypt, is archaeologically confirmed. The Coptic Christian church has been in Egypt since the 1st century AD.
trad_Jewish: Awaits the future Messianic age when Egypt worships YHWH.
trad_Catholic: The Coptic Church of Egypt partially fulfills this.
trad_Protestant: The Egyptian Christian community fulfills the spirit of this promise.
trad_Dispensational: Full national conversion of Egypt in the Millennium.
trad_Academic: Isaiah's universalist oracle; the Elephantine papyri show a historical Jewish-Egyptian temple.

keywords: abomination of desolation|temple desecrated|sacrifice abolished|Antiochus Epiphanes|Maccabees|altar|pig|Zeus
text: And arms shall stand on his part, and they shall pollute the sanctuary of strength, and shall take away the daily sacrifice, and they shall place the abomination that maketh desolate.
desc: The daily sacrifice taken away and the abomination that maketh desolate set up — enacted by Antiochus IV, and named by Jesus as still ahead (Matthew 24:15).
hebrewKey: שִׁקּוּץ מְשׁוֹמֵם (shiquts meshomem) — abomination of desolation; תָּמִיד (tamid) — the daily sacrifice
archaeology: The desecration of the Temple by Antiochus IV Epiphanes in 167 BC is confirmed by 1 Maccabees, 2 Maccabees, and Josephus. A pig was sacrificed on the altar of Zeus set up in the Holy of Holies.
trad_Jewish: Fulfilled in 167 BC by Antiochus IV Epiphanes — Hanukkah celebrates the Maccabean response.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled historically; Jesus' citation in Matthew 24 adds a future eschatological dimension.
trad_Protestant: Dual fulfillment — Antiochus was a type; the final 'abomination' is still future.
trad_Dispensational: The future Antichrist sets up an abomination in a rebuilt Jerusalem temple.
trad_Academic: Critical scholars see Daniel 11 as detailed history written after 167 BC, not predictive prophecy.

text: They gave me also gall for my meat; and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
desc: Gall for meat and vinegar to drink — offered to Jesus at the crucifixion.
hebrewKey: רֹאשׁ (rosh) — gall/bitterness; חֹמֶץ (chomets) — vinegar/sour wine
trad_Jewish: David's personal lament in persecution.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled at the crucifixion — gall offered before, vinegar offered at the moment of death.
trad_Protestant: Two distinct fulfillments — Matthew 27:34 (gall before) and John 19:29 (vinegar at death).
trad_Academic: The crucifixion narrative may have been shaped partly by Psalm 69.

text: He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken.
desc: Not one of his bones broken — kept at the cross, where the soldiers brake not Jesus' legs (John 19:36).
hebrewKey: עֶצֶם (etsem) — bone; שָׁמַר (shamar) — protect/keep; אַחַת (achat) — one
trad_Jewish: God protects the righteous person — a general promise.
trad_Catholic: John explicitly cites this alongside Exodus 12:46 to show its fulfillment at the crucifixion.
trad_Protestant: The combination of Psalm 34:20 and Exodus 12:46 creates a double typological fulfillment.
trad_Academic: John deliberately crafts the crucifixion narrative around these texts.

keywords: everlasting covenant|David|faithful love|holy and sure|witness to peoples|nations run to you
text: Incline your ear, and come unto me: hear, and your soul shall live; and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David.
desc: The sure mercies of David in an everlasting covenant — cited by Paul at Antioch as fulfilled in the resurrection (Acts 13:34).
hebrewKey: בְּרִית עוֹלָם (berit olam) — everlasting covenant; חַסְדֵי דָוִד (chasdei David) — faithful mercies of David
trad_Jewish: God's enduring covenant mercies toward Israel through David's line.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Christ — Paul cites this (Acts 13:34) to proclaim the resurrection.
trad_Protestant: Paul connects the 'holy and sure mercies of David' to the resurrection of Christ.
trad_Academic: Deutero-Isaiah democratizing the Davidic covenant to all the exiles.

keywords: strike shepherd|scatter sheep|sword|close to me|disciples fled|Gethsemane|two thirds|one third purified
text: Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith the LORD of hosts: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones.
desc: Smite the shepherd and the sheep shall be scattered — quoted by Jesus on the night of his arrest (Matthew 26:31).
hebrewKey: עַמִּיתִי (amiti) — my associate/close to me (a fellow of God!); רֹעֶה (ro'eh) — shepherd
trad_Jewish: Historical judgment oracle about a future shepherd figure.
trad_Catholic: Jesus explicitly cites this in Gethsemane (Matt 26:31) to predict the disciples' flight.
trad_Protestant: Jesus' use makes this an intentional prophecy of his arrest and the disciples' scattering.
trad_Academic: Jesus may have seen his situation through the lens of this oracle; the disciples' flight is historically plausible.

keywords: beat|beard pulled|mocking|spitting|cheeks|suffering servant|face set like flint|not ashamed
text: I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair: I hid not my face from shame and spitting.
desc: The back given to the smiters and the face not hidden from shame and spitting — Jesus scourged and mocked before the crucifixion.
hebrewKey: גֵּו (gev) — back; לְמַכִּים (le-makkim) — those who beat; לְחָיַי (lechayay) — my cheeks
trad_Jewish: The suffering prophet-servant — Isaiah himself or corporate Israel.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Jesus' trial and scourging — beard pulled, spit upon, beaten.
trad_Protestant: The specific detail of beard-pulling and spitting is remarkable.
trad_Academic: ANE lamentation style; the passion narrative develops this imagery.

text: Behold, the LORD hath proclaimed unto the end of the world, Say ye to the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy salvation cometh; behold, his reward is with him, and his work before him.
desc: Say ye to the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy salvation cometh — words taken up at the triumphal entry.
hebrewKey: יִשְׁעֵךְ (yish'ekh) — your salvation/Savior; שָׂכָר (sakhar) — reward
trad_Jewish: God's salvation coming to Zion — the Messianic age.
trad_Catholic: Matthew combines Isaiah 62:11 and Zechariah 9:9 for the Triumphal Entry account.
trad_Protestant: Jesus intentionally enacted both prophecies simultaneously.
trad_Academic: Matthew's composite citation is a literary technique showing prophetic fulfillment.

text: And in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because thou hast obeyed my voice.
desc: In thy seed shall all nations be blessed — the promise Paul reads as singular: 'thy seed, which is Christ' (Galatians 3:16).
hebrewKey: זַרְעֲךָ (zarecha) — your offspring/seed; הִתְבָּרֲכוּ (hitbareku) — will be blessed
archaeology: Mount Moriah is identified with the Temple Mount in Jerusalem (2 Chr 3:1). The Binding of Isaac (Aqedah) is one of the most analyzed typological narratives in biblical scholarship.
trad_Jewish: The Aqedah (binding of Isaac) is the supreme act of faithfulness; the blessing comes through Abraham's seed = Israel.
trad_Catholic: Paul argues 'seed' is singular, referring to Christ (Gal 3:16).
trad_Protestant: The typology — father offering only son on Mount Moriah — foreshadows the cross.
trad_Oneness: Jesus, the seed of Abraham, brings blessing to all nations through the gospel.
trad_Academic: Aqedah is a founding narrative; Paul's singular 'seed' argument is a novel interpretive move.

keywords: purify lips|all peoples|call on name of LORD|one accord|shoulder to shoulder|pure speech|Babel reversed|nations worship|lips|purify|peoples|name|serve
text: For then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the LORD, to serve him with one consent.
desc: A pure language turned to the people, that they may all call upon the name of the LORD with one consent — the Gentiles brought in.
hebrewKey: שָׂפָה בְרוּרָה (safah berurah) — pure/purified lips; שֶׁכֶם אֶחָד (shekhem echad) — one shoulder/one accord
trad_Jewish: The reversal of Babel — all nations will one day call on YHWH in one language.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled partially in the Church; fully at the end when all nations worship together.
trad_Protestant: Pentecost reverses Babel — all tongues now call on the name of the LORD.
trad_Oneness: All who call on the name of Jesus (Acts 2:21) and receive the Spirit are fulfilling this.
trad_Academic: Zephaniah's eschatological reversal of the Babel narrative is a sophisticated literary inversion.

keywords: swords into plowshares|spears into pruning hooks|no more war|judge nations|settle disputes|Jerusalem|peace|Micah 4
text: And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.
desc: Swords beaten into plowshares and nations learning war no more — the peace of Messiah's reign, read of the Millennium.
hebrewKey: כִּתְּתוּ חַרְבוֹתָם (kitetu charvotam) — they will beat their swords; אֵתִים (etim) — plowshares
trad_Jewish: The Messianic age — not yet fulfilled; the nations still war.
trad_Catholic: The Church advances this vision; full realization at the end of time.
trad_Protestant: This is the goal of the Messianic kingdom — not yet fully realized.
trad_Dispensational: Fulfilled in the Millennial Kingdom when Christ rules with a rod of iron.
trad_Academic: The identical text in Micah 4:3 suggests a shared tradition. The UN has this verse inscribed on its wall.

text: Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will perform that good thing which I have promised unto the house of Israel and to the house of Judah.
desc: The good thing promised to Israel and Judah to be performed — the Davidic pledge renewed in the Messiah.
hebrewKey: אָקִים (aqim) — I will raise up; צֶמַח צְדָקָה (tsemach tsedaqah) — righteous/saving Branch
trad_Jewish: Awaits Davidic king who establishes justice in the land of Israel.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Jesus the righteous Branch.
trad_Protestant: Parallel to Jeremiah 23:5 — the righteous Branch = Christ.
trad_Dispensational: Dual: Church Age partial fulfillment; Millennial full fulfillment.
trad_Academic: Many scholars think this section (Jeremiah 33) is a later addition, absent in the LXX.

keywords: desert blooms|wilderness|crocus|joy|glory of Lebanon|Carmel|Sharon|healing miracles|return of exiles
text: The wilderness and the solitary place shall be glad for them; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose.
desc: The wilderness made glad and the desert blossoming as the rose — the restoration under Messiah's reign.
hebrewKey: יְשֻׂשׂוּם (yeshusum) — rejoice; תִּפְרַח (tifrach) — blossom; כַּחֲבַצֶּלֶת (kachavatselet) — like a crocus/narcissus
archaeology: Modern Israel's transformation of the Negev desert through irrigation is sometimes cited as partial fulfillment.
trad_Jewish: The Messianic age of restoration — still future.
trad_Catholic: Partially fulfilled in Jesus' healing miracles; fully in the new creation.
trad_Protestant: Jesus' miracles inaugurate this Messianic renewal.
trad_Dispensational: The Millennium brings ecological and physical restoration.
trad_Academic: Restoration poetry for exiles returning from Babylon.

text: The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall bring presents: the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts.
desc: Kings of Tarshish and of the isles bringing presents — the Messiah's reign honoured by the nations.
hebrewKey: מַלְכֵי תַרְשִׁישׁ (malkei Tarshish) — kings of Tarshish; שְׁבָא וּסְבָא (Sheva u-Seva) — Sheba and Seba
archaeology: Sheba (modern Yemen) was renowned for gold, frankincense, and myrrh in the ancient world. The Queen of Sheba narrative confirms trading relationships.
trad_Jewish: Royal Psalm for Solomon's golden age; the Messianic age will surpass even Solomon's glory.
trad_Catholic: The Magi bringing gold and incense partially fulfills this (Matthew 2).
trad_Protestant: Typological fulfillment in the Magi; full fulfillment at Christ's return.
trad_Dispensational: All nations paying homage in the Millennial Kingdom.
trad_Academic: A coronation Psalm idealizing the king's international recognition.

keywords: great name|nations|sun rises|sun sets|pure offerings|incense|Gentiles worship|global worship
text: For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the LORD of hosts.
desc: From the rising of the sun to its going down, incense and a pure offering among the Gentiles — worship carried beyond Israel.
hebrewKey: גָּדוֹל שְׁמִי (gadol shemi) — great is my name; מִמִּזְרַח-שֶׁמֶשׁ (mimizrach-shemesh) — from the rising of the sun
trad_Jewish: Awaits the Messianic age when all nations truly worship YHWH.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in the global Church offering the Eucharist 'in every place.'
trad_Protestant: The global spread of Christian worship from every nation fulfills this.
trad_Academic: Malachi's critique of corrupt temple worship; the global vision is his theological corrective.

text: Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father's children shall bow down before thee.
desc: Judah praised by his brethren, his hand on the neck of his enemies — the tribe the Messiah comes from.
hebrewKey: יְהוּדָה (Yehudah) — Judah/praise; יוֹדוּךָ (yoducha) — will praise you; אֲרִי (ari) — lion
trad_Jewish: Judah receives royal preeminence among the twelve tribes.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Jesus of the tribe of Judah — the Lion of Judah.
trad_Protestant: The tribe of Judah produced both David and Jesus.
trad_Dispensational: The Lion of Judah rules in the Millennium (Rev 5:5).
trad_Academic: Tribal blessing poem reflecting historical Judah's dominance.

keywords: undivided heart|new spirit|heart of stone|heart of flesh|indwelling|new covenant|obedience
text: And I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them an heart of flesh:
desc: One heart and a new spirit given, the stony heart replaced with a heart of flesh — the new birth, received in Acts 2:38.
hebrewKey: לֵב אַחַד (lev echad) — undivided/one heart; רוּחַ חֲדָשָׁה (ruach chadashah) — new spirit
trad_Jewish: Promise to the exiles of spiritual renewal in the land.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in baptism and the indwelling of the Holy Spirit.
trad_Protestant: Parallels Ezekiel 36:26 — both describe the regenerating work of the Spirit.
trad_Oneness: Fulfilled in the New Birth experience — Spirit baptism transforms the heart.
trad_Academic: Ezekiel's pastoral theology; parallel passage in 36:26.

keywords: deaf hear|blind see|scroll|day|healing|Messianic credentials|gloom darkness|poor rejoice
text: And in that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity, and out of darkness.
desc: The deaf hearing and the blind seeing out of darkness — Messianic signs, the works Jesus points to as his credentials.
hebrewKey: חֵרְשִׁים (chereshim) — deaf; עֵינֵי עִוְרִים (einei ivrim) — eyes of the blind; יִרְאוּ (yiru) — will see
trad_Jewish: The Messianic age when God's intervention heals the disabled.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Jesus' healing miracles.
trad_Protestant: Jesus cites Isaiah 29:18 (alongside 35:5) as his Messianic credentials to John (Luke 7:22).
trad_Academic: Isaiah's Messianic healing vision; Jesus deliberately enacted these miracles.

keywords: strengthen Judah|Joseph|restore|compassion|as if not rejected|Ephraim|regather|Signal|return from exile
text: And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will bring them again to place them; for I have mercy upon them: and they shall be as though I had not cast them off: for I am the LORD their God, and will hear them.
desc: The house of Judah strengthened and the house of Joseph saved, brought back as though they had never been cast off — Israel's restoration.
hebrewKey: גָּבַרְתִּי (gavanti) — I will strengthen; הֲשִׁיבֹתִים (hashivotim) — I will restore/return them
trad_Jewish: The future reunion of all twelve tribes — still awaited.
trad_Catholic: The spiritual fulfillment in the Church where Jew and Gentile are unified.
trad_Protestant: Points to the future restoration of Israel.
trad_Dispensational: Literally fulfilled when the twelve tribes return in the Tribulation/Millennial period.
trad_Academic: Zechariah's post-exilic restoration oracle.

text: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace; that bringeth good tidings of good, that publisheth salvation; that saith unto Zion, Thy God reigneth!
desc: Beautiful upon the mountains the feet of him that bringeth good tidings — applied by Paul to those who preach the gospel.
hebrewKey: מְבַשֵּׂר (mevaser) — gospel-herald/one who brings good news; שָׁלוֹם (shalom) — peace; יָשַׁע (yasha) — salvation
trad_Jewish: The herald announcing the end of Babylonian exile and God's return to Zion.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Jesus' proclamation of the Kingdom and the Church's evangelism.
trad_Protestant: Paul cites this of the Christian missionary (Romans 10:15) — the gospel spreads like the herald's feet.
trad_Oneness: The Apostolic mission fulfills these beautiful feet of gospel proclamation.
trad_Academic: Deutero-Isaiah's great herald announcement; Paul democratizes it for all evangelists.

text: Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou ordained strength because of thine enemies, that thou mightest still the enemy and the avenger.
desc: Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou ordained strength — quoted by Jesus in the temple when the children cried Hosanna (Matthew 21:16).
hebrewKey: עֹלְלִים (olelim) — infants; יֹנְקִים (yoneqim) — nursing children; עֹז (oz) — strength/stronghold
trad_Jewish: Children's praise honoring God; the Psalm celebrates human dignity in creation.
trad_Catholic: Jesus cites this (Matt 21:16) when defending the children's 'Hosanna!' in the temple.
trad_Protestant: Jesus' direct citation makes this a Messianic fulfillment.
trad_Academic: Jesus uses this as a counterargument to the chief priests — an effective proof-text from the Psalter.

keywords: covenant for the people|light for Gentiles|righteousness|called|keep|open blind eyes|free captives|darkness
text: I the LORD have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thine hand, and will keep thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles;
desc: The servant given for a covenant of the people and a light of the Gentiles — Messianic: Christ for Israel and the nations both.
hebrewKey: בְּרִית עָם (berit am) — covenant for the people; אוֹר גּוֹיִם (or goyim) — light of the nations
trad_Jewish: Israel as God's servant called to be a light to the nations.
trad_Catholic: Simeon quotes this at Jesus' dedication (Luke 2:32): 'a light for revelation to the Gentiles.'
trad_Protestant: Simeon's citation makes this an authoritative Messianic fulfillment.
trad_Oneness: Jesus is the Light of the world and the covenant — fulfilled in him alone.
trad_Academic: First Servant Song's universalist vision.

keywords: name endure|sun|all nations blessed|Abraham's promise|call him blessed|forever|global renown
text: His name shall endure for ever: his name shall be continued as long as the sun: and men shall be blessed in him: all nations shall call him blessed.
desc: His name enduring for ever, all nations calling him blessed — the Messiah's everlasting kingdom.
hebrewKey: שְׁמוֹ לְעוֹלָם (shemo le'olam) — his name forever; כָּל-גּוֹיִם (kol-goyim) — all nations
trad_Jewish: The ideal Davidic king whose fame outlasts the sun — Messianic hope.
trad_Catholic: Jesus' name is the only name by which people are saved (Acts 4:12); all nations call him blessed.
trad_Protestant: The global spread of the name 'Jesus' fulfills this universally.
trad_Dispensational: Full global recognition in the Millennial Kingdom.
trad_Academic: Connects the Abrahamic blessing formula to the Davidic king.

keywords: glory of Second Temple|greater than Solomon's|peace|Shalom|Messiah visits temple|Zerubbabel|desired of nations|shake nations|glory|temple|house
text: The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith the LORD of hosts: and in this place will I give peace, saith the LORD of hosts.
desc: The glory of the latter house greater than the former — Christ entering the second temple, whose stones were poorer than Solomon's.
hebrewKey: כָּבוֹד (kavod) — glory; בַּיִת הַזֶּה (bayit hazeh) — this house; שָׁלוֹם (shalom) — peace
archaeology: Herod's Temple (the expanded Second Temple) was considered by the Romans to be one of the wonders of the world. Jesus visited and taught there.
trad_Jewish: Haggai encourages the returned exiles — the Second Temple's glory still debated as greater than Solomon's.
trad_Catholic: Greater glory was the Messiah himself who entered and taught in the Second Temple.
trad_Protestant: The second temple's glory surpassed the first because Jesus the Glory of God walked in it.
trad_Dispensational: A future Millennial temple will exceed both previous temples.
trad_Academic: Haggai's encouraging oracle for the discouraged post-exilic community.

keywords: river of life|temple threshold|east|everything lives|fish|heal|Dead Sea|new creation|flowing water
text: Afterward he brought me again unto the door of the house; and, behold, waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward: for the forefront of the house stood toward the east, and the waters came down from under from the right side of the house, at the south side of the altar.
desc: Waters issuing from under the threshold, deepening as they run until they heal the sea — taken up in Revelation's river of life.
hebrewKey: מַיִם (mayim) — water; יָצָא (yatsa) — goes out/flows; חָיָה (chayah) — live/be healed
trad_Jewish: The Millennial temple from which life-giving water flows — still future.
trad_Catholic: Typologically fulfilled in the Spirit flowing from Christ; fully in Revelation 22.
trad_Protestant: Revelation 22:1-2 draws directly on this imagery for the New Jerusalem.
trad_Dispensational: Literal river from the Millennial temple in Jerusalem healing the Dead Sea.
trad_Academic: Part of Ezekiel's utopian temple vision (chapters 40-48).

keywords: worms not die|fire not quenched|dead bodies|rebels|loathsome|final judgment|Gehenna|hell|outer darkness
text: And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.
desc: The carcases of the transgressors, their worm not dying and their fire not quenched — the verse Jesus quotes of Gehenna, and Isaiah's deliberate last word.
hebrewKey: תּוֹלַעְתָּם (tolaatam) — their worm; תִּכְבֶּה (tikhbeh) — be quenched; גֵּיהִנֹּם (Gehinnom) — Gehenna

trad_Jewish: Physical description of the dead bodies of God's enemies; Gehenna as a concept develops from this.
trad_Catholic: The eternal punishment of hell; the fire and worm language is used by Jesus himself.
trad_Protestant: Jesus cites this (Mark 9:44,48) as a description of hell/Gehenna.
trad_Academic: The Hinnom Valley had a long history as a site of fire; Jesus drew on this geography metaphorically.

keywords: famine|hearing the word|not food|not water|stagger|seek the word|not find|post-exile|silence of prophets
fulfillmentRefs: Lamentations 2:9|1 Samuel 3:1|Between Testaments — 400 years of prophetic silence
text: Behold, the days come, saith the Lord GOD, that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD:
desc: A famine not of bread but of hearing the words of the LORD — judgment by God's silence, the withdrawal of prophecy itself.
hebrewKey: רָעָב (ra'av) — famine; שָׁמֹעַ (shamo'a) — hearing; דְּבַר-יְהוָה (devar YHWH) — word of the LORD
archaeology: The period between Malachi (c. 450 BC) and John the Baptist (c. AD 28) — approximately 400 years — is described by Jewish tradition as a period of prophetic silence.
trad_Jewish: The Intertestamental period of 400 years without a prophet fulfills this.
trad_Catholic: The 400 years of silence ended with John the Baptist.
trad_Protestant: The silent centuries between Malachi and Matthew demonstrate the famine of prophecy.
trad_Dispensational: The Church Age could be seen as another such 'famine' for Israel as the Gentiles receive the Word.
trad_Academic: Amos refers to the removal of prophetic guidance from the Northern Kingdom.

keywords: Root of Jesse|banner|nations rally|Gentiles seek him|resting place|glory|signal|gather|second time
text: And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious.
desc: The root of Jesse standing as an ensign, to whom the Gentiles shall seek — the Davidic Saviour drawing the nations.
hebrewKey: שֹׁרֶשׁ יִשַׁי (shoresh Yishai) — Root of Jesse; נֵס (nes) — banner/signal; גּוֹיִם (goyim) — nations
trad_Jewish: The Messiah as a rallying point for all nations in the Messianic age.
trad_Catholic: Paul explicitly cites this of Christ's acceptance by the Gentiles (Romans 15:12).
trad_Protestant: Paul's citation in Romans 15:12 makes this a clear Messianic fulfillment.
trad_Dispensational: The second regathering (v.11) points to the end-time return of Israel.
trad_Academic: Part of the great Isaianic vision of the Messianic king.

keywords: path of life|joy in presence|eternal pleasures|right hand|resurrection|no decay|Holy One|fullness of joy
text: Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.
desc: The path of life shown, fulness of joy in God's presence — quoted by Peter at Pentecost as proof of the resurrection (Acts 2:25-28).
hebrewKey: אֹרַח חַיִּים (orach chayyim) — path of life; שְׂמָחוֹת (semachot) — joys; נְעִמוֹת (ne'imot) — pleasures
trad_Jewish: David's personal trust in God through life and death.
trad_Catholic: Fulfilled in Christ's resurrection and exaltation to the Father's right hand.
trad_Protestant: Peter cites Psalm 16:10-11 as a unit in his Pentecost sermon (Acts 2:25-28).
trad_Oneness: The joy at the Father's right hand is the joy of Christ's exalted position after the resurrection.
trad_Academic: Peter's midrashic interpretation of David's personal confidence as pointing to Christ.

keywords: coming soon|Maranatha|Amen|testimony|alpha omega|bride|Spirit|promise of return|final verse
text: He which testifieth these things saith, Surely I come quickly. Amen. Even so, come, Lord Jesus.
desc: Surely I come quickly — the last promise in Scripture, and the church's answer to it.
hebrewKey: מָרַנָּא תָּא (Maranatha) — Our Lord, come! (Aramaic, preserved in 1 Cor 16:22)
trad_Catholic: The final prayer of Scripture — 'Come, Lord Jesus' — the Church's eschatological hope.
trad_Protestant: The last prophetic promise in Scripture — the definitive Second Coming promise.
trad_Oneness: Every believer lives in anticipation of the imminent return of Jesus Christ.
