text: And I will harden Pharaoh's heart, that he shall follow after them; and I will be honoured upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host; that the Egyptians may know that I am the LORD. And they did so.
desc: God predicting Pharaoh's pursuit and his own glorification at the Red Sea, fulfilled in the drowning of Egypt's army.

text: And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.
desc: Moses predicting Israel would never see the Egyptian army again, fulfilled when the sea closed over Pharaoh's forces.

text: Thou shalt bring them in, and plant them in the mountain of thine inheritance, in the place, O LORD, which thou hast made for thee to dwell in, in the Sanctuary, O Lord, which thy hands have established.
desc: Moses's song predicting Israel would be planted in God's holy mountain, pointing to both the temple and the heavenly Zion.

text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.
desc: The total destruction of Amalek predicted after their attack on Israel, progressively fulfilled through Saul and David.

sub: The Angel who bears the Name
text: Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared. Beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not; for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him.
desc: God sends His Angel before Israel — One who can pardon transgression and 'in whom is my name' — read by many as a pre-incarnate appearance of the Son.

text: I will send my fear before thee, and will destroy all the people to whom thou shalt come, and I will make all thine enemies turn their backs unto thee. And I will send hornets before thee, which shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee.
desc: God promising supernatural terror before Israel's armies as they entered Canaan, fulfilled in the Conquest.

text: Observe thou that which I command thee this day: behold, I drive out before thee the Amorite, and the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
desc: God's covenant promise to drive out the six Canaanite nations before Israel, fulfilled under Joshua.

text: For I will cast out the nations before thee, and enlarge thy borders: neither shall any man desire thy land, when thou shalt go up to appear before the LORD thy God thrice in the year.
desc: God promising to protect Israel's borders during the three annual pilgrimage feasts, fulfilled throughout the monarchy period.

text: Defile not ye yourselves in any of these things: for in all these the nations are defiled which I cast out before you: And the land is defiled: therefore I do visit the iniquity thereof upon it, and the land itself vomiteth out her inhabitants.
desc: Warning that Canaanite moral corruption would bring judgment as it had on those nations Israel was displacing.

text: Ye shall therefore keep all my statutes, and all my judgments, and do them: that the land, whither I bring you to dwell therein, spue you not out. And ye shall not walk in the manners of the nation, which I cast out before you: for they committed all these things, and therefore I abhorred them.
desc: God's promise of Canaan as a fertile inheritance, fulfilled in Israel's settlement of the Promised Land.

text: If ye walk in my statutes, and keep my commandments, and do them; Then I will give you rain in due season, and the land shall yield her increase, and the trees of the field shall yield their fruit.
desc: God's covenant promise to dwell and walk among His people as their God — a thread running to the incarnation and the new creation.

text: But if ye will not hearken unto me, and will not do all these commandments; And if ye shall despise my statutes, or if your soul abhor my judgments, so that ye will not do all my commandments, but that ye break my covenant:
desc: Covenant curses for disobedience including disease, drought, defeat, and exile, fulfilled progressively over Israel's history.

text: Then shall the land enjoy her sabbaths, as long as it lieth desolate, and ye be in your enemies' land; even then shall the land rest, and enjoy her sabbaths. As long as it lieth desolate it shall rest; because it did not rest in your sabbaths, when ye dwelt upon it.
desc: The land resting during Israel's exile to make up missed Sabbath years, fulfilled in the 70-year Babylonian captivity.

text: And upon them that are left alive of you I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies; and the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them; and they shall flee, as fleeing from a sword; and they shall fall when none pursueth.
desc: The psychological terror and vulnerability of the exiled remnant, fulfilled in the exile's disorientation and fear.

text: If they shall confess their iniquity, and the iniquity of their fathers, with their trespass which they trespassed against me, and that also they have walked contrary unto me;
desc: Before Israel ever entered the land, the Torah wrote the whole cycle in advance: sin, exile among enemies — then 'if they shall confess their iniquity… I will remember my covenant.' Every later restoration prophecy is an appeal to this clause; Daniel's exile prayer (Dan. 9:4-19) executes it verbatim.

text: Have I conceived all this people? have I begotten them, that thou shouldest say unto me, Carry them in thy bosom, as a nursing father beareth the sucking child, unto the land which thou swarest unto their fathers?
desc: God as a mother eagle bearing Israel, a metaphor extended to the Messiah who gathers and bears his people.

text: Surely they shall not see the land which I sware unto their fathers, neither shall any of them that provoked me see it:
desc: God judging the unbelieving exodus generation to die in the wilderness, fulfilled over 40 years of wandering.

text: Say unto them, As truly as I live, saith the LORD, as ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you: Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness; and all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward, which have murmured against me,
desc: The specific judgment that those 20 years and older would die in the wilderness, fulfilled in the 40-year wandering.

text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live.
desc: The bronze serpent lifted up bringing healing to those who look in faith, cited by Jesus as a type of his crucifixion.

text: God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?
desc: Balaam's oracle declaring God's unchanging faithfulness — He cannot lie or revoke His blessing on His people.

sub: Balaam's oracles — no enchantment against Jacob
text: Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Israel: according to this time it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel, What hath God wrought!
desc: Balaam, hired to curse Israel, can only bless: 'Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob… according to this time it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel, What hath God wrought!' — Israel's God-guarded destiny declared by a pagan prophet.

sub: A Star and a Sceptre from Jacob
text: And now, behold, I go unto my people: come therefore, and I will advertise thee what this people shall do to thy people in the latter days. And he took up his parable, and said, Balaam the son of Beor hath said, and the man whose eyes are open hath said:
desc: Balaam's final oracle of the Star and Sceptre rising from Jacob — a royal Messianic figure with dominion, awaited 'but not now.'

text: And when he looked on Amalek, he took up his parable, and said, Amalek was the first of the nations; but his latter end shall be that he perish for ever.
desc: Amalek, once the first among nations, predicted to perish forever, fulfilled in their complete destruction.

text: And he looked on the Kenites, and took up his parable, and said, Strong is thy dwellingplace, and thou puttest thy nest in a rock. Nevertheless the Kenite shall be wasted, until Asshur shall carry thee away captive.
desc: The Kenites dwelling securely in rocks but eventually being conquered by Assyria, fulfilled in the Assyrian campaigns.

text: And he took up his parable, and said, Alas, who shall live when God doeth this! And ships shall come from the coast of Chittim, and shall afflict Asshur, and shall afflict Eber, and he also shall perish for ever.
desc: Western ships afflicting Assyria and Eber (Hebrews), understood as Rome's eventual dominance over the Near East.

sub: Seek the LORD and find Him
text: When thou shalt beget children, and children's children, and ye shall have remained long in the land, and shall corrupt yourselves, and make a graven image, or the likeness of any thing, and shall do evil in the sight of the LORD thy God, to provoke him to anger:
desc: Moses foretells exile for idolatry, and the promise that a repentant, seeking Israel will find God, who will not forget His covenant.

text: Wherefore it shall come to pass, if ye hearken to these judgments, and keep, and do them, that the LORD thy God shall keep unto thee the covenant and the mercy which he sware unto thy fathers:
desc: Conditional blessings for faithfulness including military victories and fruitfulness, fulfilled in David's and Solomon's reigns.

text: For if ye shall diligently keep all these commandments which I command you, to do them, to love the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, and to cleave unto him;
desc: God's promise that no enemy would stand before Israel as they took the land — fulfilled in the conquest under Joshua.

text: The LORD thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me; unto him ye shall hearken;
desc: Moses' promise of a coming Prophet like himself, to whom Israel must listen — applied by Peter and Stephen to Jesus.

sub: Whoever will not hear that Prophet
text: And it shall come to pass, that whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him.
desc: The warning that whoever refuses to hear the coming Prophet will answer to God — applied by Peter to those who reject Jesus.

text: But the prophet, which shall presume to speak a word in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die.
desc: The test of a true prophet, ensuring that false prophets who presume to speak for God face judgment.

text: And it shall come to pass, if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the LORD thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments which I command thee this day, that the LORD thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth:
desc: The covenant blessings promised for obedience — prosperity, victory, and preeminence among the nations.

text: But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the LORD thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee:
desc: The covenant curses for disobedience — siege, exile, and dispersion among all nations — read as foretelling Israel's Diaspora.

sub: The nations ask why the land lies waste
text: So that the generation to come of your children that shall rise up after you, and the stranger that shall come from a far land, shall say, when they see the plagues of that land, and the sicknesses which the LORD hath laid upon it;
desc: The nations asking why the land lies desolate — Israel rooted out for forsaking the covenant.

sub: Gathered from all nations; the heart circumcised
text: And it shall come to pass, when all these things are come upon thee, the blessing and the curse, which I have set before thee, and thou shalt call them to mind among all the nations, whither the LORD thy God hath driven thee,
desc: After the scattering, God promises to regather Israel from all nations and circumcise their hearts to love Him — a restoration and new-covenant hope.

sub: They will forsake me; the Song as witness
text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Behold, thou shalt sleep with thy fathers; and this people will rise up, and go a whoring after the gods of the strangers of the land, whither they go to be among them, and will forsake me, and break my covenant which I have made with them.
desc: God foretells to Moses that Israel will forsake the covenant after his death, giving the Song (ch. 32) as a witness against them.

sub: A foolish nation to provoke them
text: And when the LORD saw it, he abhorred them, because of the provoking of his sons, and of his daughters. And he said, I will hide my face from them, I will see what their end shall be: for they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith.
desc: From the Song of Moses — God will provoke unfaithful Israel to jealousy by 'a foolish nation,' which Paul applies to the Gentiles.

sub: Vengeance is mine; rejoice, O nations
text: To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time: for the day of their calamity is at hand, and the things that shall come upon them make haste.
desc: The Song's close — God's vengeance and recompense, and the call for the nations to rejoice with His people — cited across the NT.

sub: The everlasting arms; a people saved by the LORD
text: And this is the blessing, wherewith Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel before his death. And he said, The LORD came from Sinai, and rose up from Seir unto them; he shined forth from mount Paran, and he came with ten thousands of saints: from his right hand went a fiery law for them.
desc: Moses' deathbed blessing on the tribes of Israel — foretelling their destinies and resting in the eternal God their refuge.

text: Moses my servant is dead; now therefore arise, go over this Jordan, thou, and all this people, unto the land which I do give to them, even to the children of Israel.
desc: God commissioning Joshua to lead Israel into the Promised Land, the fulfillment of the land promise to Abraham.

text: And Joshua said, Hereby ye shall know that the living God is among you, and that he will without fail drive out from before you the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Hivites, and the Perizzites, and the Girgashites, and the Amorites, and the Jebusites.
desc: God guaranteeing to drive out all seven Canaanite nations as Israel crossed the Jordan, fulfilled under Joshua.

sub: Jericho — a curse with a 500-year fuse
text: And Joshua adjured them at that time, saying, Cursed be the man before the LORD, that riseth up and buildeth this city Jericho: he shall lay the foundation thereof in his firstborn, and in his youngest son shall he set up the gates of it.
desc: Joshua's oath over the ruins: whoever rebuilds Jericho will lay its foundation at the cost of his firstborn and set up its gates at the cost of his youngest. Five centuries later, 'in his days did Hiel the Bethelite build Jericho: he laid the foundation thereof in Abiram his firstborn, and set up the gates thereof in his youngest son Segub, according to the word of the LORD' (1 Kgs. 16:34).

text: And the LORD said unto Joshua, Stretch out the spear that is in thy hand toward Ai; for I will give it into thine hand. And Joshua stretched out the spear that he had in his hand toward the city.
desc: God's command and promise to deliver Ai to Joshua, fulfilled when the city was taken by Israel's ambush.

text: All the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon unto Misrephothmaim, and all the Sidonians, them will I drive out from before the children of Israel: only divide thou it by lot unto the Israelites for an inheritance, as I have commanded thee.
desc: God promising the remaining Canaanites would be driven out by the LORD before Israel, fulfilled in later conquest.

text: And Moses sware on that day, saying, Surely the land whereon thy feet have trodden shall be thine inheritance, and thy children's for ever, because thou hast wholly followed the LORD my God.
desc: Caleb's land inheritance at Hebron promised by Moses and fulfilled 45 years later as Caleb claimed it in old age.

text: And the LORD your God, he shall expel them from before you, and drive them from out of your sight; and ye shall possess their land, as the LORD your God hath promised unto you.
desc: God's final promise to Joshua that he would complete the expulsion of Canaanites if Israel remained faithful.

text: Know for a certainty that the LORD your God will no more drive out any of these nations from before you; but they shall be snares and traps unto you, and scourges in your sides, and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off this good land which the LORD your God hath given you.
desc: Joshua's warning that remaining Canaanites would become traps for unfaithful Israel, fulfilled repeatedly in Judges.

text: And an angel of the LORD came up from Gilgal to Bochim, and said, I made you to go up out of Egypt, and have brought you unto the land which I sware unto your fathers; and I said, I will never break my covenant with you.
desc: God rebuking Israel for making covenants with Canaanites, warning the remaining nations would be thorns.

text: And the anger of the LORD was hot against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of spoilers that spoiled them, and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies.
desc: The cycle of judgment in Judges predicted and fulfilled repeatedly: disobedience brings oppression until Israel cries out.

text: And I will draw unto thee to the river Kishon Sisera, the captain of Jabin's army, with his chariots and his multitude; and I will deliver him into thine hand.
desc: God promising Deborah and Barak a specific victory over Sisera at the Kishon River, fulfilled when the army was swept away.

text: And she said, I will surely go with thee: notwithstanding the journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honour; for the LORD shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman. And Deborah arose, and went with Barak to Kedesh.
desc: Deborah's prediction that a woman would get credit for Sisera's death, fulfilled when Jael drove a peg through Sisera's head.

text: And the LORD looked upon him, and said, Go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites: have not I sent thee? And he said unto him, Oh my Lord, wherewith shall I save Israel? behold, my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house.
desc: God promising Gideon victory over all Midian with a vastly reduced army, fulfilled when 300 men routed a vast host.

text: And the LORD said unto Gideon, By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you, and deliver the Midianites into thine hand: and let all the other people go every man unto his place.
desc: God specifying that only 300 men would defeat Midian so Israel could not boast, fulfilled in Gideon's night raid.

text: And the bramble said unto the trees, If in truth ye anoint me king over you, then come and put your trust in my shadow: and if not, let fire come out of the bramble, and devour the cedars of Lebanon.
desc: Jotham's parable-curse predicting that Abimelech and the men of Shechem would destroy each other, fulfilled three years later.

text: For, lo, thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and no razor shall come on his head: for the child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb: and he shall begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.
desc: The miraculous birth of Samson as a Nazirite deliverer predicted by the Angel of the LORD, fulfilled in Samson's birth and ministry.

text: The adversaries of the LORD shall be broken to pieces; out of heaven shall he thunder upon them: the LORD shall judge the ends of the earth; and he shall give strength unto his king, and exalt the horn of his anointed.
desc: Hannah's prophetic song of reversal, the first use of 'anointed' (Messiah/Christ) in relation to God's coming King.

text: And there came a man of God unto Eli, and said unto him, Thus saith the LORD, Did I plainly appear unto the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt in Pharaoh's house?
desc: God's announcement of judgment on Eli's house for his sons' corruption, fulfilled in the deaths at Aphek and loss of the ark.

text: And the LORD said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle. In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house: when I begin, I will also make an end.
desc: God's judgment on Eli's priestly line declared in advance, fulfilled when Eli's sons died and the priesthood passed from his house.

text: And he said, This will be the manner of the king that shall reign over you: He will take your sons, and appoint them for himself, for his chariots, and to be his horsemen; and some shall run before his chariots.
desc: Samuel warning Israel of the abuses a human king would bring, fulfilled throughout the monarchy period.

text: Then Samuel took a vial of oil, and poured it upon his head, and kissed him, and said, Is it not because the LORD hath anointed thee to be captain over his inheritance?
desc: Saul anointed as Israel's first king exactly as God instructed Samuel, the first fulfillment of Israel's request for a king.

text: If ye will fear the LORD, and serve him, and obey his voice, and not rebel against the commandment of the LORD, then shall both ye and also the king that reigneth over you continue following the LORD your God:
desc: Samuel's conditional promise of covenant blessing for the new monarchy, requiring continued obedience.

text: And Samuel said to Saul, Thou hast done foolishly: thou hast not kept the commandment of the LORD thy God, which he commanded thee: for now would the LORD have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever.
desc: Samuel declaring Saul's dynasty would not endure because of his disobedience, fulfilled as the kingdom passed to David.

text: And Samuel said unto Saul, I will not return with thee: for thou hast rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD hath rejected thee from being king over Israel.
desc: God declaring Saul's kingdom given to another after the Amalek disobedience, fulfilled in David's anointing.

text: And he sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, and withal of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look to. And the LORD said, Arise, anoint him: for this is he.
desc: Samuel, sent to Bethlehem past seven older brothers, anoints the shepherd boy: 'Arise, anoint him: for this is he.' Every Messianic lineage prophecy on this site runs through this moment — the covenant line, the city, and the office all begin converging at Bethlehem a millennium before the manger.

text: This day will the LORD deliver thee into mine hand; and I will smite thee, and take thine head from thee; and I will give the carcases of the host of the Philistines this day unto the fowls of the air, and to the wild beasts of the earth; that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel.
desc: David's bold prediction of Goliath's defeat before the battle, fulfilled when David killed him with a stone.

text: Then said David, O LORD God of Israel, thy servant hath certainly heard that Saul seeketh to come to Keilah, to destroy the city for my sake. Will the men of Keilah deliver me up into his hand? will Saul come down, as thy servant hath heard? O LORD God of Israel, I beseech thee, tell thy servant. And the LORD said, He will come down.
desc: God warning David that the men of Keilah would betray him to Saul, causing David to escape before it happened.

text: And now, behold, I know well that thou shalt surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel shall be established in thine hand.
desc: Even Saul acknowledging David's destiny to reign and prevail, inadvertently prophesying what God had decreed.

text: And the LORD hath done to him, as he spake by me: for the LORD hath rent the kingdom out of thine hand, and given it to thy neighbour, even to David: Because thou obeyedst not the voice of the LORD, nor executedst his fierce wrath upon Amalek, therefore hath the LORD done this thing unto thee this day.
desc: Samuel's ghost (or God through the medium) predicting Saul's death the next day at Jezreel, fulfilled exactly at Gilboa.

text: So do God to Abner, and more also, except, as the LORD hath sworn to David, even so I do to him; To translate the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beersheba.
desc: Abner formally acknowledging the divine decree that David would reign over all Israel, the transition of the kingdom.

text: Also in time past, when Saul was king over us, thou wast he that leddest out and broughtest in Israel: and the LORD said to thee, Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be a captain over Israel.
desc: God's word to David that he would shepherd all Israel recalled at his coronation, fulfilled when all Israel came to David.

text: He shall build an house for my name, and I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever.
desc: God promising through Nathan that David's son would build the temple and have an everlasting kingdom.

text: And thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.
desc: The Davidic covenant's eternal throne, the most directly messianic promise in the OT historical books.

text: Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thine house; because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife. Thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thine own house, and I will take thy wives before thine eyes, and give them unto thy neighbour, and he shall lie with thy wives in the sight of this sun.
desc: God's judgment on David for the Bathsheba-Uriah sin, fulfilled in Amnon's murder, Absalom's rebellion, and Adonijah's death.

text: And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the LORD. And Nathan said unto David, The LORD also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die. Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die.
desc: David forgiven of murder and adultery, his life spared but consequences remaining, a model of God's mercy and discipline.

sub: David's song — head of the heathen
text: Thou also hast delivered me from the strivings of my people, thou hast kept me to be head of the heathen: a people which I knew not shall serve me. Strangers shall submit themselves unto me: as soon as they hear, they shall be obedient unto me.
desc: David's victory song (parallel to Psalm 18) climaxes: 'thou hast kept me to be head of the heathen: a people which I knew not shall serve me' — words Paul quotes (v.50 = Ps. 18:49) as prophecy of the Gentiles praising God in Christ (Rom. 15:9).

text: Now these be the last words of David. David the son of Jesse said, and the man who was raised up on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel, said,
desc: David's last words describing the ideal just ruler who is like the morning sun, a messianic portrait.

text: That the LORD may continue his word which he spake concerning me, saying, If thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail thee (said he) a man on the throne of Israel.
desc: God's conditional promise to maintain David's dynasty if his sons remain faithful, setting up the tension the Messiah resolves.

text: Concerning this house which thou art in building, if thou wilt walk in my statutes, and execute my judgments, and keep all my commandments to walk in them; then will I perform my word with thee, which I spake unto David thy father:
desc: God's conditional promise to dwell in the temple if Solomon remains faithful, the terms eventually broken.

text: And if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked, in integrity of heart, and in uprightness, to do according to all that I have commanded thee, and wilt keep my statutes and my judgments:
desc: God warning of temple destruction and exile for covenant unfaithfulness, fulfilled in 586 BC when Babylon destroyed Jerusalem.

text: Wherefore the LORD said unto Solomon, Forasmuch as this is done of thee, and thou hast not kept my covenant and my statutes, which I have commanded thee, I will surely rend the kingdom from thee, and will give it to thy servant.
desc: God announcing the division of the kingdom as judgment on Solomon's idolatry, fulfilled at Rehoboam's accession.

sub: Kingline — the kingdom torn in twelve pieces
text: … And Ahijah caught the new garment that was on him, and rent it in twelve pieces: And he said to Jeroboam, Take thee ten pieces: for thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel, Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee:
desc: Ahijah tears a new garment into twelve pieces and hands Jeroboam ten: the kingdom will split, ten tribes north, the Davidic line keeping Judah 'that David my servant may have a light alway before me in Jerusalem.' It happened at Rehoboam's accession, exactly along the announced seam.

text: And he cried against the altar in the word of the LORD, and said, O altar, altar, thus saith the LORD; Behold, a child shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name; and upon thee shall he offer the priests of the high places that burn incense upon thee, and men's bones shall be burnt upon thee.
desc: An unnamed prophet confronts Jeroboam's altar at Bethel and names the king who will defile it — 'a child shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name' — roughly three centuries before Josiah did exactly that (2 Kgs. 23:15-16).

text: And he gave a sign the same day, saying, This is the sign which the LORD hath spoken; Behold, the altar shall be rent, and the ashes that are upon it shall be poured out.
desc: The long-range Josiah prophecy is sealed with a same-day sign: 'Behold, the altar shall be rent, and the ashes... poured out' — which happens as Jeroboam stretches out his hand (1 Kgs. 13:5).

text: And it was so, when Ahijah heard the sound of her feet, as she came in at the door, that he said, Come in, thou wife of Jeroboam; why feignest thou thyself to be another? for I am sent to thee with heavy tidings.
desc: Total destruction of Jeroboam's dynasty predicted, fulfilled when Baasha killed all of Jeroboam's house.

text: Then the word of the LORD came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha, saying, Forasmuch as I exalted thee out of the dust, and made thee prince over my people Israel; and thou hast walked in the way of Jeroboam, and hast made my people Israel to sin, to provoke me to anger with their sins;
desc: Baasha's entire house condemned for following Jeroboam's sins, fulfilled when Zimri killed all of Baasha's house.

text: And Elijah the Tishbite, who was of the inhabitants of Gilead, said unto Ahab, As the LORD God of Israel liveth, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word.
desc: Elijah predicting a total drought in Israel as judgment, fulfilled in 3.5 years of drought that devastated the land.

text: For thus saith the LORD God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the LORD sendeth rain upon the earth.
desc: Elijah's prediction of miraculous provision for the widow of Zarephath, fulfilled throughout the drought period.

text: And it came to pass after many days, that the word of the LORD came to Elijah in the third year, saying, Go, shew thyself unto Ahab; and I will send rain upon the earth.
desc: The Carmel confrontation where Elijah predicted God would answer by fire, ending the drought as rain came.

text: And, behold, there came a prophet unto Ahab king of Israel, saying, Thus saith the LORD, Hast thou seen all this great multitude? behold, I will deliver it into thine hand this day; and thou shalt know that I am the LORD.
desc: God promising Ahab victory over Ben-Hadad through an unnamed prophet at Samaria, fulfilled in the great battle.

text: And there came a man of God, and spake unto the king of Israel, and said, Thus saith the LORD, Because the Syrians have said, The LORD is God of the hills, but he is not God of the valleys, therefore will I deliver all this great multitude into thine hand, and ye shall know that I am the LORD.
desc: God promising victory over Syria to vindicate his universal sovereignty, fulfilled in the massive Israelite victory at Aphek.

text: Then said he unto him, Because thou hast not obeyed the voice of the LORD, behold, as soon as thou art departed from me, a lion shall slay thee. And as soon as he was departed from him, a lion found him, and slew him.
desc: A disobedient prophet killed by a lion for breaking God's command, fulfilled immediately as a warning to all prophets.

text: And he said unto him, Thus saith the LORD, Because thou hast let go out of thy hand a man whom I appointed to utter destruction, therefore thy life shall go for his life, and thy people for his people.
desc: Ahab's premature sparing of Ben-Hadad condemned, fulfilled when Ahab was killed in battle against Syria.

sub: Ahab — dogs at the pool of Samaria
text: And thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus saith the LORD, Hast thou killed, and also taken possession? And thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus saith the LORD, In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick thy blood, even thine.
desc: After the judicial murder of Naboth, Elijah pronounces: 'In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick thy blood, even thine.' Three years later Ahab's chariot is washed at the pool of Samaria, 'and the dogs licked up his blood' (1 Kgs. 22:38).

sub: The house of Ahab cut off
text: Behold, I will bring evil upon thee, and will take away thy posterity, and will cut off from Ahab him that pisseth against the wall, and him that is shut up and left in Israel,
desc: Elijah's full sentence: Ahab's male line will be swept away like Jeroboam's, and 'the dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.' Jehu's coup (2 Kgs. 9-10) fulfills every clause — Joram shot in Naboth's field, Jezebel thrown from the window at Jezreel, the seventy sons destroyed.

text: … Seest thou how Ahab humbleth himself before me? because he humbleth himself before me, I will not bring the evil in his days: but in his son’s days will I bring the evil upon his house.
desc: When Ahab humbles himself in sackcloth, God amends the timetable through Elijah: 'I will not bring the evil in his days: but in his son's days will I bring the evil upon his house' — fulfilled when Jehu destroys Joram, not Ahab, in Naboth's field (2 Kgs. 9:25-26).

text: And he said, I saw all Israel scattered upon the hills, as sheep that have not a shepherd: and the LORD said, These have no master: let them return every man to his house in peace.
desc: Micaiah's vision predicting Ahab's death and Israel's scattering, fulfilled when Ahab died and Israel fled.

text: Now therefore thus saith the LORD, Thou shalt not come down from that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die. And Elijah departed.
desc: Elijah predicting Ahaziah's death from his bed-fall injury for consulting Baal, fulfilled when Ahaziah died.

text: And he said, Thus saith the LORD, Make this valley full of ditches. For thus saith the LORD, Ye shall not see wind, neither shall ye see rain; yet that valley shall be filled with water, that ye may drink, both ye, and your cattle, and your beasts.
desc: Elisha predicting water without rain and victory over Moab, fulfilled the next morning with both.

text: And he said, About this season, according to the time of life, thou shalt embrace a son. And she said, Nay, my lord, thou man of God, do not lie unto thine handmaid.
desc: Elisha predicting the Shunammite woman would have a son, fulfilled the following year.

text: And when they came down to him, Elisha prayed unto the LORD, and said, Smite this people, I pray thee, with blindness. And he smote them with blindness according to the word of Elisha.
desc: Elisha predicting the Syrian army would be struck blind, fulfilled when they were led into Samaria.

text: Then Elisha said, Hear ye the word of the LORD; Thus saith the LORD, To morrow about this time shall a measure of fine flour be sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, in the gate of Samaria.
desc: In besieged, starving Samaria — donkey heads selling for silver — Elisha names tomorrow's commodity prices: 'To morrow about this time shall a measure of fine flour be sold for a shekel... in the gate of Samaria.' The Syrian army flees in the night and the prices land exactly (2 Kgs. 7:16).

text: Then a lord on whose hand the king leaned answered the man of God, and said, Behold, if the LORD would make windows in heaven, might this thing be? And he said, Behold, thou shalt see it with thine eyes, but shalt not eat thereof.
desc: The royal officer scoffs — 'if the LORD would make windows in heaven, might this thing be?' Elisha answers: 'Thou shalt see it with thine eyes, but shalt not eat thereof.' Next day he is appointed gatekeeper, sees the plenty, and is trampled in the stampede (2 Kgs. 7:17-20).

text: And Elisha said unto him, Go, say unto him, Thou mayest certainly recover: howbeit the LORD hath shewed me that he shall surely die.
desc: Elisha predicting both that Hazael would recover from illness but Benhadad would die, fulfilled when Hazael smothered him.

text: And Hazael said, Why weepeth my lord? And he answered, Because I know the evil that thou wilt do unto the children of Israel: their strong holds wilt thou set on fire, and their young men wilt thou slay with the sword, and wilt dash their children, and rip up their women with child.
desc: Elisha predicting Hazael would become king and would massacre Israel, fulfilled in Hazael's brutal campaigns.

text: And thou shalt smite the house of Ahab thy master, that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of the LORD, at the hand of Jezebel.
desc: God commanding Jehu's anointing as king to destroy Ahab's house, fulfilled in Jehu's violent revolution.

text: Wherefore they came again, and told him. And he said, This is the word of the LORD, which he spake by his servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, In the portion of Jezreel shall dogs eat the flesh of Jezebel:
desc: Elijah's prediction of Jezebel's gruesome end by dogs at Jezreel, fulfilled literally when she was thrown from a window.

text: And the LORD said unto Jehu, Because thou hast done well in executing that which is right in mine eyes, and hast done unto the house of Ahab according to all that was in mine heart, thy children of the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.
desc: Jehu's dynasty limited to four generations as reward for destroying Ahab's house, fulfilled exactly in Zechariah.

text: Now Elisha was fallen sick of his sickness whereof he died. And Joash the king of Israel came down unto him, and wept over his face, and said, O my father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof.
desc: Elisha's sign-prophecy limiting Israel's victories over Syria to three, fulfilled in three battles under Joash.

text: And Isaiah said unto them, Thus shall ye say to your master, Thus saith the LORD, Be not afraid of the words which thou hast heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
desc: Isaiah's first answer to the Assyrian ultimatum is a three-part prediction: Sennacherib will hear a rumor, return to his own land, and fall by the sword there. All three happened — the army withdrew, and twenty years later his own sons cut him down in his god's temple (19:37).

text: Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, That which thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria I have heard.
desc: God's full answer to Sennacherib's letter: the virgin daughter of Zion despises him; the hook goes in his nose and he returns the way he came; Jerusalem will not see so much as an arrow shot into it — 'I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David's sake.'

sub: Sennacherib — the angel and the morning
text: And it came to pass that night, that the angel of the LORD went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.
desc: 'And it came to pass that night, that the angel of the LORD went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.' The empire's unstoppable army, ended between dusk and dawn.

text: In those days was Hezekiah sick unto death. And the prophet Isaiah the son of Amoz came to him, and said unto him, Thus saith the LORD, Set thine house in order; for thou shalt die, and not live.
desc: Isaiah predicting Hezekiah's recovery from his terminal illness after his prayer, fulfilled within three days.

text: Turn again, and tell Hezekiah the captain of my people, Thus saith the LORD, the God of David thy father, I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tears: behold, I will heal thee: on the third day thou shalt go up unto the house of the LORD.
desc: Hezekiah, dying, receives the most personal dated prophecy in Scripture: 'I will heal thee… I will add unto thy days fifteen years.' The regnal arithmetic of Kings checks out — Hezekiah reigns exactly the promised span beyond the crisis — and the sign given was a shadow moving backward.

text: Behold, the days come, that all that is in thine house, and that which thy fathers have laid up in store unto this day, shall be carried into Babylon: nothing shall be left, saith the LORD.
desc: Isaiah predicting the Babylonian exile of all Hezekiah's treasures and sons, fulfilled a century later under Nebuchadnezzar.

text: And the LORD spake by his servants the prophets, saying, Because Manasseh king of Judah hath done these abominations, and hath done wickedly above all that the Amorites did, which were before him, and hath made Judah also to sin with his idols:
desc: God declaring catastrophic judgment on Jerusalem for Manasseh's sins, fulfilled in the Babylonian destruction.

text: Because thine heart was tender, and thou hast humbled thyself before the LORD, when thou heardest what I spake against this place, and against the inhabitants thereof, that they should become a desolation and a curse, and hast rent thy clothes, and wept before me; I also have heard thee, saith the LORD.
desc: Huldah the prophetess promising Josiah he would die in peace before Jerusalem's destruction, fulfilled at Megiddo before Babylon came.

text: And the LORD said, I will remove Judah also out of my sight, as I have removed Israel, and will cast off this city Jerusalem which I have chosen, and the house of which I said, My name shall be there.
desc: God confirming through Huldah that all the curses of Deuteronomy would fall on Judah for its idolatry.

text: Surely at the commandment of the LORD came this upon Judah, to remove them out of his sight, for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he did; And also for the innocent blood that he shed: for he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood; which the LORD would not pardon.
desc: The Babylonian exile attributed to Manasseh's extreme sin, the culmination of centuries of accumulated judgment.

text: And it shall come to pass, when thy days be expired that thou must go to be with thy fathers, that I will raise up thy seed after thee, which shall be of thy sons; and I will establish his kingdom.
desc: The Chronicler's record of Nathan's oracle. Notably, Chronicles omits the 'if he commit iniquity' clause of 2 Samuel 7:14 and says God will settle the coming king 'in mine house and in my kingdom for ever' — sharpening the profile beyond Solomon.

text: Behold, a son shall be born to thee, who shall be a man of rest; and I will give him rest from all his enemies round about: for his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quietness unto Israel in his days.
desc: Solomon named before birth and promised peaceful reign, fulfilled in Israel's golden age under Solomon.

text: And he said unto me, Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father. Moreover I will establish his kingdom for ever, if he be constant to do my commandments and my judgments, as at this day.
desc: God confirming through David the Solomonic temple-building promise, with the eternal throne pointing beyond Solomon to Christ.

text: If I shut up heaven that there be no rain, or if I command the locusts to devour the land, or if I send pestilence among my people; If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.
desc: God's night answer to Solomon's temple dedication: when drought, locusts, or pestilence come, 'if my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray… then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.' The covenant's standing repair procedure — invoked by every revival since.

text: And as for thee, if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked, and do according to all that I have commanded thee, and shalt observe my statutes and my judgments;
desc: God's warning that persistent idolatry would result in being plucked from the land and the temple becoming a ruin.

text: Then came Shemaiah the prophet to Rehoboam, and to the princes of Judah, that were gathered together to Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said unto them, Thus saith the LORD, Ye have forsaken me, and therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak.
desc: Shemaiah's explanation of Shishak's invasion as God's judgment, prompting Rehoboam's humbling and partial deliverance.

text: And he went out to meet Asa, and said unto him, Hear ye me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin; The LORD is with you, while ye be with him; and if ye seek him, he will be found of you; but if ye forsake him, he will forsake you.
desc: Azariah the prophet declaring the covenant principle of mutual faithfulness, foundational to understanding Israel's cycles.

text: And at that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah, and said unto him, Because thou hast relied on the king of Syria, and not relied on the LORD thy God, therefore is the host of the king of Syria escaped out of thine hand.
desc: Hanani rebuking Asa for trusting Syria instead of God, warning that wars would follow his faithlessness.

text: Then he said, I did see all Israel scattered upon the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd: and the LORD said, These have no master; let them return therefore every man to his house in peace.
desc: Micaiah's vision of Israel without a king after Ahab's death, fulfilled when Ahab died and Israel scattered.

text: And he said, Hearken ye, all Judah, and ye inhabitants of Jerusalem, and thou king Jehoshaphat, Thus saith the LORD unto you, Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God's.
desc: Jahaziel's prediction of Jehoshaphat's bloodless victory over Moab, Ammon, and Edom, fulfilled when enemies turned on each other.

text: And there came a writing to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, Thus saith the LORD God of David thy father, Because thou hast not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat thy father, nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah,
desc: Elijah's letter predicting Jehoram's horrible death by intestinal disease for his wickedness, fulfilled exactly.

text: And it came to pass, as he talked with him, that the king said unto him, Art thou made of the king's counsel? forbear; why shouldest thou be smitten? Then the prophet forbare, and said, I know that God hath determined to destroy thee, because thou hast done this, and hast not hearkened unto my counsel.
desc: A prophet warning Amaziah that his doom was sealed for adopting Edomite idols, fulfilled when Joash of Israel defeated him.

sub: Kingline — gathered to thy grave in peace
text: And she answered them, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Tell ye the man that sent you to me, Thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will bring evil upon this place, and upon the inhabitants thereof, even all the curses that are written in the book which they have read before the king of Judah:
desc: The prophetess Huldah authenticates the rediscovered Book of the Law: the written curses will fall on Jerusalem — but not in Josiah's days; because his heart was tender, 'thou shalt be gathered to thy grave in peace, neither shall thine eyes see all the evil.' Jerusalem fell twenty-three years after his burial.

text: Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the LORD spoken by the mouth of Jeremiah might be accomplished, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and put it also in writing, saying,
desc: The Hebrew Bible's canonical last words: 'that the word of the LORD spoken by the mouth of Jeremiah might be accomplished, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia' — the seventy-years clock striking, recorded as fulfillment by name, prophet cited, king named, decree quoted.

text: Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and put it also in writing, saying,
desc: Ezra opens by quoting the proclamation itself: Cyrus, 'that the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled,' authorizes any of God's people to go up to Jerusalem 'and build the house of the LORD God of Israel' — with imperial funding for the journey.

text: Remember, I beseech thee, the word that thou commandedst thy servant Moses, saying, If ye transgress, I will scatter you abroad among the nations: But if ye turn unto me, and keep my commandments, and do them; though there were of you cast out unto the uttermost part of the heaven, yet will I gather them from thence, and will bring them unto the place that I have chosen to set my name there.
desc: A millennium after Moses, Nehemiah quotes him back to God: 'Remember… the word that thou commandedst thy servant Moses, saying, If ye transgress, I will scatter you… but if ye turn unto me… yet will I gather them.' The scatter-clause had happened; Nehemiah stands on the gather-clause — and the walls go up.

text: And said unto the king, Let the king live for ever: why should not my countenance be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers' sepulchres, lieth waste, and the gates thereof are consumed with fire?
desc: Nehemiah's prayer and the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls, partially fulfilling Daniel's 70-weeks prophecy timeline.

text: For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth: And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God:
desc: Job's confession of a living Redeemer who will stand on earth, and his own bodily resurrection to see God in the flesh.

text: If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to shew unto man his uprightness: Then he is gracious unto him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit: I have found a ransom.
desc: Job's vision of a heavenly messenger-interpreter who pays a ransom to deliver the sinner from death, a portrait of Christ's intercession.

sub: I have set my King on Zion
text: He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh: the Lord shall have them in derision. Then shall he speak unto them in his wrath, and vex them in his sore displeasure.
desc: God's answer to the raging nations — He installs His King on Zion, the decree behind the Messiah's enthronement.

text: Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession. Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel.
desc: The LORD's word to His Anointed Son — the nations as His inheritance, to be ruled with a rod of iron — applied to Christ throughout Revelation.

sub: The Son of Man given dominion
text: What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him? For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour.
desc: The psalm of humanity's God-given dominion, applied in Hebrews and 1 Corinthians to Jesus, the Son of Man, under whose feet all things are placed.

text: The wicked shall be turned into hell, and all the nations that forget God.
desc: God's judgment on the God-forgetting wicked, a warning of eschatological consequence pointing to the final judgment.

text: Oh that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion! when the LORD bringeth back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.
desc: David's longing for the Deliverer who comes from Zion, quoted by Paul in context of Israel's end-times salvation.

text: I have set the LORD always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved. Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth: my flesh also shall rest in hope.
desc: David's confidence that God will not abandon him to the grave — cited by Peter at Pentecost as a prophecy of Christ's resurrection.

text: As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.
desc: David's expectation of seeing God's face after death, a personal resurrection hope fulfilled in Christ's risen appearance.

text: Now know I that the LORD saveth his anointed; he will hear him from his holy heaven with the saving strength of his right hand.
desc: Confidence in God saving his anointed king, fulfilled in Christ's resurrection from the right hand of the Father.

text: The king shall joy in thy strength, O LORD; and in thy salvation how greatly shall he rejoice! Thou hast given him his heart's desire, and hast not withholden the request of his lips. Selah.
desc: Psalm 21's royal celebration of the Anointed King crowned with gold, prophetically describing Christ's eternal coronation.

text: But I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised of the people. All they that see me laugh me to scorn: they shoot out the lip, they shake the head, saying,
desc: The Sufferer mocked by onlookers who shake their heads and taunt his trust in God — words echoed almost exactly at the crucifixion.

text: But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother's breasts. I was cast upon thee from the womb: thou art my God from my mother's belly.
desc: The Messiah's trust in God from birth, fulfilled in Christ who was consecrated from the womb.

text: Be not far from me; for trouble is near; for there is none to help. Many bulls have compassed me: strong bulls of Bashan have beset me round.
desc: The graphic description of the Sufferer — pierced hands and feet, bones out of joint, garments divided by lot — fulfilled in detail at the crucifixion.

sub: I will declare thy name unto my brethren
text: I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee. Ye that fear the LORD, praise him; all ye the seed of Jacob, glorify him; and fear him, all ye the seed of Israel.
desc: After the sufferings of Psalm 22, the vindicated sufferer praises God among His 'brethren' and the ends of the earth turn to the LORD — applied to Christ in Hebrews.

text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
desc: The beloved confession of the LORD as shepherd — which Jesus claims as 'the good shepherd' who gives His life for the sheep.

sub: Lift up your heads; the King of glory
text: Lift up your heads, O ye gates; and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors; and the King of glory shall come in. Who is this King of glory? The LORD strong and mighty, the LORD mighty in battle.
desc: The triumphal entry of the King of glory — the LORD of hosts — into His gates, read of Christ's ascension and royal advent.

sub: The last words from the cross
text: Into thine hand I commit my spirit: thou hast redeemed me, O LORD God of truth.
desc: David's prayer of trust, spoken by Jesus as His final words from the cross.

text: False witnesses did rise up; they laid to my charge things that I knew not.
desc: The suffering servant accused by false witnesses, fulfilled in the false testimony at Jesus's trial before the Sanhedrin.

text: Let not them that are mine enemies wrongfully rejoice over me: neither let them wink with the eye that hate me without a cause.
desc: Being hated without cause predicted, cited by Jesus as scripture fulfilled in his own experience with the Jewish leaders.

text: My lovers and my friends stand aloof from my sore; and my kinsmen stand afar off.
desc: Friends and loved ones standing at a distance during suffering, fulfilled when the disciples watched from afar at Calvary.

text: Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required. Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me,
desc: The declaration that God desires obedience over sacrifice — 'Lo, I come to do thy will' — applied in Hebrews to Christ's incarnation and self-offering.

text: I have preached righteousness in the great congregation: lo, I have not refrained my lips, O LORD, thou knowest. I have not hid thy righteousness within my heart; I have declared thy faithfulness and thy salvation: I have not concealed thy lovingkindness and thy truth from the great congregation.
desc: The Messiah publicly proclaiming righteousness, fulfilled in Jesus's bold temple teaching and synagogue preaching.

text: Thou art fairer than the children of men: grace is poured into thy lips: therefore God hath blessed thee for ever.
desc: The King more beautiful than all men with grace-filled lips, Messianic portrait of Christ's divine excellence.

text: Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, O most mighty, with thy glory and thy majesty. And in thy majesty ride prosperously because of truth and meekness and righteousness; and thy right hand shall teach thee terrible things.
desc: The Warrior-King riding in truth to judge and make war, to be fulfilled at Christ's return in power.

sub: The King anointed above His fellows
text: Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows. All thy garments smell of myrrh, and aloes, and cassia, out of the ivory palaces, whereby they have made thee glad.
desc: The royal wedding psalm's praise of the King anointed by God above His fellows — applied in Hebrews to the Son.

text: I will make thy name to be remembered in all generations: therefore shall the people praise thee for ever and ever.
desc: The Messiah-King's name remembered across all generations, fulfilled in the universal spread of Jesus's name.

text: God is gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet.
desc: God ascending 'with a shout' — read by the church as a foreshadowing of Christ's ascension and enthronement.

text: Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.
desc: Jerusalem as the joy of the earth and city of the great King, fulfilled in Christ's Millennial and eternal reign from Zion.

text: Our God shall come, and shall not keep silence: a fire shall devour before him, and it shall be very tempestuous round about him. He shall call to the heavens from above, and to the earth, that he may judge his people.
desc: Asaph's psalm of God coming as Judge with fire and tempest, summoning heaven and earth and gathering His covenant saints.

text: But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth? Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.
desc: God rebuking hypocritical worship without transformed lives, pointing to the final reckoning for the unrepentant.

text: Oh that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion! When God bringeth back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.
desc: Longing for Israel's salvation from Zion, pointing to the end-times restoration when all Israel shall be saved.

text: For it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it: neither was it he that hated me that did magnify himself against me; then I would have hid myself from him:
desc: The anguish of betrayal by a close friend — read of Christ's betrayal by one of His own, Judas.

text: He hath put forth his hands against such as be at peace with him: he hath broken his covenant. The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.
desc: The betrayer's deceptive smooth words masking treachery, fulfilled in Judas's hypocritical kiss of greeting in Gethsemane.

text: The Lord gave the word: great was the company of those that published it.
desc: God's word proclaimed by a great army of heralds, fulfilled in the rapid spread of the gospel by the apostolic church.

sub: The ascension and gifts to men
text: The chariots of God are twenty thousand, even thousands of angels: the Lord is among them, as in Sinai, in the holy place. Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive: thou hast received gifts for men; yea, for the rebellious also, that the LORD God might dwell among them.
desc: The LORD's triumphant ascent, leading captives and receiving gifts — applied by Paul to Christ's ascension and the gifts given to the Church.

text: They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of mine head: they that would destroy me, being mine enemies wrongfully, are mighty: then I restored that which I took not away.
desc: The Messiah hated without cause, the very words Jesus cited when explaining the world's hatred of him.

text: I am become a stranger unto my brethren, and an alien unto my mother's children.
desc: The sufferer estranged from his own brothers — read of Jesus, whose own brothers did not believe in Him.

sub: Zeal for God's house; bearing reproach
text: For the zeal of thine house hath eaten me up; and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.
desc: The Sufferer consumed by zeal for God's house, bearing the reproaches meant for God — cited of Jesus cleansing the temple and bearing reproach.

text: Let their habitation be desolate; and let none dwell in their tents.
desc: The imprecation that the betrayer's dwelling be left desolate — applied by Peter to Judas and the choosing of his replacement.

text: The mountains shall bring peace to the people, and the little hills, by righteousness. He shall judge the poor of the people, he shall save the children of the needy, and shall break in pieces the oppressor.
desc: Nature itself bringing peace in the messianic age, a portrait of the coming Kingdom when the earth is renewed.

text: He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth. They that dwell in the wilderness shall bow before him; and his enemies shall lick the dust.
desc: The King's universal dominion from sea to sea, to be fully realized in Christ's millennial and eternal kingdom.

text: For he shall deliver the needy when he crieth; the poor also, and him that hath no helper. He shall spare the poor and needy, and shall save the souls of the needy.
desc: The King as deliverer of the needy and poor, fulfilled in Christ's ministry to the outcast and poor throughout his earthly ministry.

text: And he shall live, and to him shall be given of the gold of Sheba: prayer also shall be made for him continually; and daily shall he be praised. There shall be an handful of corn in the earth upon the top of the mountains; the fruit thereof shall shake like Lebanon: and they of the city shall flourish like grass of the earth.
desc: The eternal name of the messianic King, fulfilled in Jesus's name proclaimed across every nation and generation.

text: Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who only doeth wondrous things. And blessed be his glorious name for ever: and let the whole earth be filled with his glory; Amen, and Amen.
desc: Solomon's doxology of universal blessing in God's name, the closing prayer that Christ will fulfill globally.

text: Give ear, O my people, to my law: incline your ears to the words of my mouth. I will open my mouth in a parable: I will utter dark sayings of old:
desc: Asaph's words 'I will open my mouth in a parable' — which Matthew sees fulfilled in Jesus' teaching in parables.

text: Let thy hand be upon the man of thy right hand, upon the son of man whom thou madest strong for thyself.
desc: Prayer for the man at God's right hand to be strengthened, pointing to the Messiah's exaltation and intercession.

text: All nations whom thou hast made shall come and worship before thee, O Lord; and shall glorify thy name.
desc: All nations coming to worship God, to be fulfilled when every knee bows at Christ's return.

text: I will make mention of Rahab and Babylon to them that know me: behold Philistia, and Tyre, with Ethiopia; this man was born there. And of Zion it shall be said, This and that man was born in her: and the highest himself shall establish her.
desc: The nations' peoples counted as born in Zion, a prophetic image of spiritual citizenship in God's city.

sub: An everlasting throne for David's seed
text: Then thou spakest in vision to thy holy one, and saidst, I have laid help upon one that is mighty; I have exalted one chosen out of the people. I have found David my servant; with my holy oil have I anointed him:
desc: God's covenant oath to David — an everlasting throne and seed — the 'sure mercies' fulfilled in the Son of David, Christ.

text: But thou hast cast off and abhorred, thou hast been wroth with thine anointed. Thou hast made void the covenant of thy servant: thou hast profaned his crown by casting it to the ground.
desc: The Psalmist's lament over the apparent abandonment of the Davidic covenant, fulfilled temporarily in exile but reversed in Christ.

text: O sing unto the LORD a new song: sing unto the LORD, all the earth. Sing unto the LORD, bless his name; shew forth his salvation from day to day.
desc: The new song of universal worship, fulfilled in the church's global worship and to be consummated in heaven's eternal praise.

text: The LORD reigneth; let the earth rejoice; let the multitude of isles be glad thereof. Clouds and darkness are round about him: righteousness and judgment are the habitation of his throne.
desc: An enthronement psalm celebrating the LORD's universal reign in righteousness, before whom all peoples see His glory.

text: O sing unto the LORD a new song; for he hath done marvellous things: his right hand, and his holy arm, hath gotten him the victory. The LORD hath made known his salvation: his righteousness hath he openly shewed in the sight of the heathen.
desc: God winning salvation by his own power, the new song of redemption fulfilled in Christ's resurrection victory.

text: The LORD reigneth; let the people tremble: he sitteth between the cherubims; let the earth be moved. The LORD is great in Zion; and he is high above all the people.
desc: The LORD enthroned between the cherubim, applied to Christ's exaltation to the Father's right hand.

text: Thou shalt arise, and have mercy upon Zion: for the time to favour her, yea, the set time, is come. For thy servants take pleasure in her stones, and favour the dust thereof.
desc: God arising to rebuild Zion at the appointed time, pointing to Israel's end-times restoration.

sub: Thou art the same; thy years have no end
text: Of old hast thou laid the foundation of the earth: and the heavens are the work of thy hands. They shall perish, but thou shalt endure: yea, all of them shall wax old like a garment; as a vesture shalt thou change them, and they shall be changed:
desc: Words addressed to the LORD the Creator — which Hebrews applies directly to the Son, Christ, the unchanging Creator.

text: The LORD hath prepared his throne in the heavens; and his kingdom ruleth over all.
desc: God's heavenly throne and universal dominion established, fulfilled in Christ's ascension and session at the Father's right hand.

text: Thou sendest forth thy spirit, they are created: and thou renewest the face of the earth.
desc: The Spirit as the power of creation and renewal, pointing to the new creation God will bring through the Spirit.

text: He hath remembered his covenant for ever, the word which he commanded to a thousand generations. Which covenant he made with Abraham, and his oath unto Isaac;
desc: God's eternal memory of the Abrahamic covenant, affirmed throughout Israel's history and fulfilled in Christ the promised seed.

text: To overthrow their seed also among the nations, and to scatter them in the lands.
desc: God's judgment stayed by an intercessor standing in the breach, a pattern fulfilled in Christ's eternal intercession.

text: O give thanks unto the LORD, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever. Let the redeemed of the LORD say so, whom he hath redeemed from the hand of the enemy;
desc: God gathering the redeemed from all four compass points, fulfilled in Pentecost's universal gathering and Israel's regathering.

text: Set thou a wicked man over him: and let Satan stand at his right hand. When he shall be judged, let him be condemned: and let his prayer become sin.
desc: An imprecatory prayer against the betrayer, interpreted as fulfilled in Judas Iscariot and Satan entering him.

sub: The betrayer's office given to another
text: Let his days be few; and let another take his office.
desc: An imprecation on the treacherous adversary — which Peter applied to Judas and the choosing of his replacement.

text: The LORD shall send the rod of thy strength out of Zion: rule thou in the midst of thine enemies. Thy people shall be willing in the day of thy power, in the beauties of holiness from the womb of the morning: thou hast the dew of thy youth.
desc: The Messiah's scepter going forth from Zion to rule even among adversaries, the progressive expansion of Christ's reign.

text: The Lord at thy right hand shall strike through kings in the day of his wrath. He shall judge among the heathen, he shall fill the places with the dead bodies; he shall wound the heads over many countries.
desc: The LORD striking down kings in the day of wrath, fulfilled in Christ's final battle at Armageddon.

text: O praise the LORD, all ye nations: praise him, all ye people. For his merciful kindness is great toward us: and the truth of the LORD endureth for ever. Praise ye the LORD.
desc: The shortest Psalm calling all nations to praise, quoted by Paul as a prophecy of Gentile praise fulfilled in the church.

text: I shall not die, but live, and declare the works of the LORD. The LORD hath chastened me sore: but he hath not given me over unto death.
desc: Deliverance from death to declare God's works, cited as a prophecy of Christ's resurrection triumph.

text: Save now, I beseech thee, O LORD: O LORD, I beseech thee, send now prosperity. Blessed be he that cometh in the name of the LORD: we have blessed you out of the house of the LORD.
desc: The 'Hosanna' ('save now') and 'Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the LORD' — the crowd's cry at Jesus' Triumphal Entry.

text: For ever, O LORD, thy word is settled in heaven.
desc: The eternal permanence of God's word, the foundation for all prophecy being trustworthy and ultimately fulfilled.

sub: The fruit of thy body upon thy throne
text: The LORD hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne. If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony that I shall teach them, their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore.
desc: God's sworn oath to set David's offspring on his throne — which Peter cites at Pentecost as fulfilled in the risen Christ.

text: For the LORD hath chosen Zion; he hath desired it for his habitation. This is my rest for ever: here will I dwell; for I have desired it.
desc: God's eternal choice of Zion as his dwelling, pointing to the New Jerusalem as the eternal home of God with man.

text: All the kings of the earth shall praise thee, O LORD, when they hear the words of thy mouth. Yea, they shall sing in the ways of the LORD: for great is the glory of the LORD.
desc: All kings praising God for his words, to be fulfilled when every ruler acknowledges Christ's kingship at his return.

text: Thy kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and thy dominion endureth throughout all generations.
desc: God's kingdom declared everlasting, fulfilled in Christ's eternal reign that has no end.

text: The LORD possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old. I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was.
desc: Wisdom speaking as the first of God's creative acts, interpreted as a portrait of the pre-existent Word/Christ.

text: Who hath ascended up into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment? who hath established all the ends of the earth? what is his name, and what is his son's name, if thou canst tell?
desc: Agur's mysterious question about who has ascended and whose Son can do these things, pointing toward the Father-Son relationship.

text: And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the LORD'S house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it.
desc: The elevation of Jerusalem as the spiritual center of the world in the messianic age, nations streaming to learn God's Torah.

text: Enter into the rock, and hide thee in the dust, for fear of the LORD, and for the glory of his majesty. The lofty looks of man shall be humbled, and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down, and the LORD alone shall be exalted in that day.
desc: Human pride brought utterly low before God's majesty at the Day of the LORD, eschatological judgment on all arrogance.

sub: The Branch of the LORD; Zion cleansed
text: In that day shall the branch of the LORD be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the earth shall be excellent and comely for them that are escaped of Israel.
desc: The 'Branch of the LORD' beautifying the remnant, with Zion cleansed by the Spirit of judgment and burning — read of the Messiah and the purifying Spirit.

text: And he will lift up an ensign to the nations from far, and will hiss unto them from the end of the earth: and, behold, they shall come with speed swiftly: None shall be weary nor stumble among them; none shall slumber nor sleep; neither shall the girdle of their loins be loosed, nor the latchet of their shoes be broken:
desc: God summoning distant nations as instruments of judgment, fulfilled in Assyria and Babylon's swift campaigns against Israel.

text: And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.
desc: God's judicial blinding of Israel for rejecting his message, explicitly fulfilled in Jesus's explanation of why he spoke in parables.

text: Then said I, Lord, how long? And he answered, Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate, And the LORD have removed men far away, and there be a great forsaking in the midst of the land.
desc: Isaiah's commissioning to preach until total desolation, fulfilled in the Babylonian exile and the long Diaspora.

text: And he shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
desc: The LORD Himself becomes a sanctuary to some but a stone of stumbling and rock of offence to others — applied by Paul and Peter to Christ.

sub: I and the children, for signs
text: And I will wait upon the LORD, that hideth his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him. Behold, I and the children whom the LORD hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from the LORD of hosts, which dwelleth in mount Zion.
desc: Isaiah and his children as 'signs' — words Hebrews places on the lips of Christ, who shares flesh with 'the children God has given.'

text: O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger, and the staff in their hand is mine indignation. I will send him against an hypocritical nation, and against the people of my wrath will I give him a charge, to take the spoil, and to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets.
desc: Assyria as God's instrument of judgment against Israel, with Assyria's own pride eventually punished.

text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the remnant of Israel, and such as are escaped of the house of Jacob, shall no more again stay upon him that smote them; but shall stay upon the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.
desc: The surviving remnant of Israel finally trusting God alone, fulfilled partially in the return from Babylon.

text: Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD of hosts, O my people that dwellest in Zion, be not afraid of the Assyrian: he shall smite thee with a rod, and shall lift up his staff against thee, after the manner of Egypt.
desc: God promising that Assyria's yoke over Israel would be broken just as Egypt's was, fulfilled in Sennacherib's defeat.

text: And the spirit of the LORD shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the LORD;
desc: The sevenfold Spirit resting on the shoot of Jesse — the Messianic King who judges with righteousness for the poor and slays the wicked with the breath of His mouth.

text: The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them.
desc: Isaiah's vision of restored creation under the Branch of Jesse — universal peace and the earth filled with the knowledge of the LORD.

text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.
