desc: The Root of Jesse as a banner for the nations, gathering both Jewish exiles and Gentiles to himself.

sub: Restoration — the song for that day
text: And in that day thou shalt say, O LORD, I will praise thee: though thou wast angry with me, thine anger is turned away, and thou comfortedst me. Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid: for the LORD JEHOVAH is my strength and my song; he also is become my salvation.
desc: Isaiah writes the worship service in advance: 'In that day thou shalt say, O LORD, I will praise thee… with joy shall ye draw water out of the wells of salvation.' A pre-composed hymn for a future deliverance — Israel still sings it at the close of every Sabbath (Havdalah), and 'salvation' here is the Hebrew yeshuah.

text: For the LORD will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.
desc: God's mercy restoring Israel to their land with foreigners joining them, fulfilled in the return from Babylon and again in modern Israel.

text: That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased! The LORD hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers.
desc: Babylon's sudden fall predicted in a taunt-song, fulfilled when Cyrus conquered Babylon in 539 BC without a battle.

text: The LORD of hosts hath sworn, saying, Surely as I have thought, so shall it come to pass; and as I have purposed, so shall it stand: That I will break the Assyrian in my land, and upon my mountains tread him under foot: then shall his yoke depart from off them, and his burden depart from off their shoulders.
desc: God swears with an oath: 'I will break the Assyrian in my land, and upon my mountains tread him under foot.' In 701 BC Sennacherib's army — having flattened 46 Judean cities — disintegrates at Jerusalem's doorstep overnight (2 Kgs. 19:35), and Assyria never threatens Jerusalem again.

text: In the year that king Ahaz died was this burden. Rejoice not thou, whole Palestina, because the rod of him that smote thee is broken: for out of the serpent's root shall come forth a cockatrice, and his fruit shall be a fiery flying serpent.
desc: Warning to Philistia not to celebrate Assyrian setbacks, since a worse power (Babylon) would follow.

sub: Moab — cities fallen in a night
text: The burden of Moab. Because in the night Ar of Moab is laid waste, and brought to silence; because in the night Kir of Moab is laid waste, and brought to silence;
desc: 'In the night Ar of Moab is laid waste... in the night Kir of Moab is laid waste' — a lament-oracle over Moab's cities, sanctuaries, and refugees, delivered with tears rather than triumph (v.5: 'My heart shall cry out for Moab').

text: Send ye the lamb to the ruler of the land from Sela to the wilderness, unto the mount of the daughter of Zion. For it shall be, that, as a wandering bird cast out of the nest, so the daughters of Moab shall be at the fords of Arnon.
desc: The Moab oracle closes with a signed timestamp: 'Within three years, as the years of an hireling, and the glory of Moab shall be contemned' — a dated, short-range prediction appended to the longer lament, with a messianic gleam at its center: the throne established 'in mercy... in the tabernacle of David' (16:5).

sub: Damascus — the burden fulfilled in 732 BC
text: The burden of Damascus. Behold, Damascus is taken away from being a city, and it shall be a ruinous heap.
desc: 'Behold, Damascus is taken away from being a city, and it shall be a ruinous heap.' Within three years of the oracle's setting, Tiglath-pileser III stormed Damascus (732 BC), executed King Rezin, deported the population, and ended the Aramean kingdom forever.

text: The cities of Aroer are forsaken: they shall be for flocks, which shall lie down, and none shall make them afraid. The fortress also shall cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus, and the remnant of Syria: they shall be as the glory of the children of Israel, saith the LORD of hosts.
desc: Israel's fortified cities left desolate, fulfilled in the Assyrian devastation of the northern kingdom.

text: Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!
desc: The roaring nations compared to surging seas, suddenly rebuked by God and fleeing like chaff.

text: Woe to the land shadowing with wings, which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia: That sendeth ambassadors by the sea, even in vessels of bulrushes upon the waters, saying, Go, ye swift messengers, to a nation scattered and peeled, to a people terrible from their beginning hitherto; a nation meted out and trodden down, whose land the rivers have spoiled!
desc: An oracle against distant Nubian-Ethiopian power, predicting they would submit tribute to God on Zion.

sub: Egypt, Assyria, and Israel in worship
text: In that day shall Egypt be like unto women: and it shall be afraid and fear because of the shaking of the hand of the LORD of hosts, which he shaketh over it. And the land of Judah shall be a terror unto Egypt, every one that maketh mention thereof shall be afraid in himself, because of the counsel of the LORD of hosts, which he hath determined against it.
desc: Isaiah's remarkable oracle of Egypt's future turning to the LORD — an altar in Egypt, a highway joining Egypt, Assyria, and Israel in worship.

text: In the year that Tartan came unto Ashdod, (when Sargon the king of Assyria sent him,) and fought against Ashdod, and took it; At the same time spake the LORD by Isaiah the son of Amoz, saying, Go and loose the sackcloth from off thy loins, and put off thy shoe from thy foot. And he did so, walking naked and barefoot.
desc: Dated to 'the year that Tartan came unto Ashdod, when Sargon the king of Assyria sent him' — Isaiah walks stripped and barefoot three years as a sign that Egypt and Ethiopia, Judah's hoped-for allies, will be led away captive by Assyria.

text: The burden of the desert of the sea. As whirlwinds in the south pass through; so it cometh from the desert, from a terrible land. A grievous vision is declared unto me; the treacherous dealer dealeth treacherously, and the spoiler spoileth. Go up, O Elam: besiege, O Media; all the sighing thereof have I made to cease.
desc: Isaiah's night-vision of Babylon's fall — 'Babylon is fallen, is fallen' — the cry later echoed in Revelation.

text: The burden of Dumah. He calleth to me out of Seir, Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night? The watchman said, The morning cometh, and also the night: if ye will enquire, enquire ye: return, come.
desc: Oracle against Edom (Dumah) bringing watchman imagery of endless night and uncertain dawn.

text: The burden of the valley of vision. What aileth thee now, that thou art wholly gone up to the housetops? Thou that art full of stirs, a tumultuous city, a joyous city: thy slain men are not slain with the sword, nor dead in battle.
desc: A rare oracle against an individual: Shebna, the royal steward carving himself a cliff tomb, will be hurled away 'like a ball' into exile, and Eliakim will receive his robe, his authority, and 'the key of the house of David' — words Jesus later takes up for Himself (Rev. 3:7).

sub: The merchant city judged and restored
text: The burden of Tyre. Howl, ye ships of Tarshish; for it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in: from the land of Chittim it is revealed to them.
desc: Isaiah's burden against Tyre — the great merchant city laid waste, then after seventy years restored, her commerce ultimately consecrated to the LORD.

text: Behold, the LORD maketh the earth empty, and maketh it waste, and turneth it upside down, and scattereth abroad the inhabitants thereof. And it shall be, as with the people, so with the priest; as with the servant, so with his master; as with the maid, so with her mistress; as with the buyer, so with the seller; as with the lender, so with the borrower; as with the taker of usury, so with the giver of usury to him.
desc: The great eschatological judgment emptying the entire earth, an apocalyptic vision of the Day of the LORD.

sub: The feast for all nations; death abolished
text: And in this mountain shall the LORD of hosts make unto all people a feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees, of fat things full of marrow, of wines on the lees well refined.
desc: The LORD's feast for all peoples on His mountain, where death itself is swallowed up forever and every tear is wiped away — cited by Paul on the resurrection.

text: In that day shall this song be sung in the land of Judah; We have a strong city; salvation will God appoint for walls and bulwarks. Open ye the gates, that the righteous nation which keepeth the truth may enter in.
desc: Israel's future song of the strong city, where 'salvation will God appoint for walls and bulwarks', rising to the promise that the dead shall live.

sub: Israel — leviathan slain, the outcasts gathered
text: In that day the LORD with his sore and great and strong sword shall punish leviathan the piercing serpent, even leviathan that crooked serpent; and he shall slay the dragon that is in the sea.
desc: Isaiah's 'little apocalypse' closes with the LORD punishing leviathan with His 'sore and great and strong sword,' Israel blossoming to 'fill the face of the world with fruit,' and a great trumpet gathering the outcasts from Assyria and Egypt to worship 'in the holy mount at Jerusalem.'

text: Woe to the rebellious children, saith the LORD, that take counsel, but not of me; and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin:
desc: Woe against those seeking Egypt's help instead of God's, fulfilled when Jerusalem fell to Babylon after trusting Egypt.

text: Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek the LORD!
desc: God as a fierce lion protecting Jerusalem against Assyria, fulfilled when Sennacherib's army was destroyed.

text: Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in judgment. And a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest; as rivers of water in a dry place, as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land.
desc: The coming righteous King who is a refuge for his people, a portrait of Messiah's reign of justice and safety.

text: Woe to thee that spoilest, and thou wast not spoiled; and dealest treacherously, and they dealt not treacherously with thee! when thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled; and when thou shalt make an end to deal treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with thee.
desc: God rising to deliver and judge, a dramatic announcement of divine intervention that will ultimately be Christ's return.

text: Come near, ye nations, to hear; and hearken, ye people: let the earth hear, and all that is therein; the world, and all things that come forth of it. For the indignation of the LORD is upon all nations, and his fury upon all their armies: he hath utterly destroyed them, he hath delivered them to the slaughter.
desc: The day of vengeance on Edom as a type of the eschatological judgment of God's enemies around Zion.

text: And Isaiah said unto them, Thus shall ye say unto your master, Thus saith the LORD, Be not afraid of the words that thou hast heard, wherewith the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
desc: Isaiah's specific word that Sennacherib would not enter Jerusalem or shoot an arrow into it, fulfilled exactly.

text: Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent unto Hezekiah, saying, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Whereas thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria: This is the word which the LORD hath spoken concerning him; The virgin, the daughter of Zion, hath despised thee, and laughed thee to scorn; the daughter of Jerusalem hath shaken her head at thee.
desc: Hezekiah's recovery and fifteen additional years promised by God through Isaiah, both fulfilled exactly.

text: Then came the word of the LORD to Isaiah, saying, Go, and say to Hezekiah, Thus saith the LORD, the God of David thy father, I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tears: behold, I will add unto thy days fifteen years.
desc: God's personal response to Hezekiah's prayer, turning the death sentence to life plus 15 years.

text: Behold, the days come, that all that is in thine house, and that which thy fathers have laid up in store until this day, shall be carried to Babylon: nothing shall be left, saith the LORD.
desc: The Babylonian exile of Jerusalem's treasures predicted to Hezekiah, fulfilled a century later under Nebuchadnezzar.

sub: The voice in the wilderness; the Shepherd-God
text: Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God. Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem, and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned: for she hath received of the LORD'S hand double for all her sins.
desc: The opening of Isaiah's Book of Comfort — the herald's voice preparing the way of the LORD, the revelation of God's glory, and the Shepherd-God coming to His people.

text: Who hath measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and meted out heaven with the span, and comprehended the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance?
desc: God's eternal omnipotence declared as comfort to discouraged Israel, fulfilled in Christ's unceasing provision for believers.

text: Keep silence before me, O islands; and let the people renew their strength: let them come near; then let them speak: let us come near together to judgment. Who raised up the righteous man from the east, called him to his foot, gave the nations before him, and made him rule over kings? he gave them as the dust to his sword, and as driven stubble to his bow.
desc: God's call of Israel as his servant, with the covenant of Abraham reconfirmed, pointing to Israel's servant role in bringing the Messiah.

sub: Only God declares things to come
text: Produce your cause, saith the LORD; bring forth your strong reasons, saith the King of Jacob. Let them bring them forth, and shew us what shall happen: let them shew the former things, what they be, that we may consider them, and know the latter end of them; or declare us things for to come.
desc: God challenges the idols to prove their deity by foretelling the future — the very test of predictive prophecy on which this whole subject rests.

text: The LORD shall go forth as a mighty man, he shall stir up jealousy like a man of war: he shall cry, yea, roar; he shall prevail against his enemies. I have long time holden my peace; I have been still, and refrained myself: now will I cry like a travailing woman; I will destroy and devour at once.
desc: God as a warrior destroying his enemies and comforting his people, fulfilled at the Cross and Second Coming.

text: But now thus saith the LORD that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.
desc: God's promise of presence through every trial to his redeemed people, a comfort to exiles and all believers.

text: But thou hast not called upon me, O Jacob; but thou hast been weary of me, O Israel. Thou hast not brought me the small cattle of thy burnt offerings; neither hast thou honoured me with thy sacrifices. I have not caused thee to serve with an offering, nor wearied thee with incense.
desc: God's rebuke of Israel for neglecting prayer and worship, serving as a warning of the consequences of spiritual lethargy.

text: Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant; and Israel, whom I have chosen: Thus saith the LORD that made thee, and formed thee from the womb, which will help thee; Fear not, O Jacob, my servant; and thou, Jesurun, whom I have chosen.
desc: God's promise to pour his Spirit on Israel's descendants, fulfilled at Pentecost and ongoing in Spirit-filled believers.

text: They that make a graven image are all of them vanity; and their delectable things shall not profit; and they are their own witnesses; they see not, nor know; that they may be ashamed.
desc: The futility and shame of idol-making declared, fulfilled in the collapse of every civilization that trusted in idols.

text: Remember these, O Jacob and Israel; for thou art my servant: I have formed thee; thou art my servant: O Israel, thou shalt not be forgotten of me. I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions, and, as a cloud, thy sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed thee.
desc: God as Creator and Redeemer, who says of Cyrus he shall perform my pleasure, fulfilling the specific Cyrus prophecy.

text: Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me, Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure:
desc: The LORD's declaration of His sole deity and sovereign foreknowledge: 'I am God, and there is none else... declaring the end from the beginning' — the bedrock of biblical monotheism and of prophecy itself.

text: Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon, sit on the ground: there is no throne, O daughter of the Chaldeans: for thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate.
desc: Babylon commanded to step down from her throne into humiliation, fulfilled in Cyrus's conquest and Rome's later destruction of the system.

text: Hear ye this, O house of Jacob, which are called by the name of Israel, and are come forth out of the waters of Judah, which swear by the name of the LORD, and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth, nor in righteousness.
desc: God as the eternal First and Last speaking to his people, the title Christ claimed for himself in Revelation.

sub: Servant Song 2: salvation to the ends of the earth
text: Listen, O isles, unto me; and hearken, ye people, from far; The LORD hath called me from the womb; from the bowels of my mother hath he made mention of my name.
desc: The second Servant Song — the Servant called from the womb, named 'Israel,' yet sent to restore Israel and be a light of salvation to the ends of the earth.

text: But Zion said, The LORD hath forsaken me, and my Lord hath forgotten me. Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee.
desc: The acceptable time of salvation declared, quoted by Paul as the 'now' of the gospel age beginning with Christ.

sub: Servant Song 3: I gave my back to the smiters
text: Thus saith the LORD, Where is the bill of your mother's divorcement, whom I have put away? or which of my creditors is it to whom I have sold you? Behold, for your iniquities have ye sold yourselves, and for your transgressions is your mother put away.
desc: The third Servant Song — the obedient Servant who gives his back to those who beat him and his face to shame and spitting, yet trusts the Lord to vindicate him.

text: Who is among you that feareth the LORD, that obeyeth the voice of his servant, that walketh in darkness, and hath no light? let him trust in the name of the LORD, and stay upon his God.
desc: Warning to those who trust in their own wisdom and schemes rather than God, fulfilled in the consequences for those who reject God's light.

text: Hearken to me, ye that follow after righteousness, ye that seek the LORD: look unto the rock whence ye are hewn, and to the hole of the pit whence ye are digged.
desc: God calling his people to remember Abraham their father, encouraging trust in God's covenant faithfulness.

text: Awake, awake, stand up, O Jerusalem, which hast drunk at the hand of the LORD the cup of his fury; thou hast drunken the dregs of the cup of trembling, and wrung them out.
desc: Israel crying for God's arm (Messiah) to act as in the Exodus, pointing to the new and greater exodus through Christ.

text: Awake, awake; put on thy strength, O Zion; put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the unclean.
desc: Zion's glorious restoration to holiness, fulfilled spiritually in the new covenant church and ultimately in New Jerusalem.

text: Sing, O barren, thou that didst not bear; break forth into singing, and cry aloud, thou that didst not travail with child: for more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife, saith the LORD.
desc: The barren woman's children multiplying beyond the married wife's, quoted by Paul as the Gentile church surpassing Israel in numbers.

text: Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
desc: The messianic banquet offered freely to all who hunger and thirst, fulfilled in Christ's open invitation and the gospel's free offer.

text: Also the sons of the stranger, that join themselves to the LORD, to serve him, and to love the name of the LORD, to be his servants, every one that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and taketh hold of my covenant;
desc: Foreigners fully included in God's house of prayer, quoted by Jesus when cleansing the temple.

text: The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart: and merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come.
desc: God's mercy in taking the righteous before judgment falls, a pattern seen in Elijah, Josiah, and ultimately Christ's death before Jerusalem's doom.

text: Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins. Yet they seek me daily, and delight to know my ways, as a nation that did righteousness, and forsook not the ordinance of their God: they ask of me the ordinances of justice; they take delight in approaching to God.
desc: God's chosen fast as social justice and liberation, fulfilled in Christ's reading of this text as his mission statement.

text: Behold, the LORD'S hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear.
desc: Israel's separation from God through sin declared, with God's solution: his own arm bringing salvation.

text: Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee. For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the LORD shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.
desc: Jerusalem's glorious rising in God's light while darkness covers the earth, fulfilled in Christ the light and the ingathering of nations.

sub: The year of favor; garments of salvation
text: To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn; To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified.
desc: The anointed herald's commission — proclaiming the LORD's acceptable year and the day of vengeance, comfort for mourners, and the garments of salvation.

text: Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength? I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save.
desc: The divine warrior returning from judgment on Edom with blood-stained garments, a portrait of Christ's return at Armageddon.

text: I will mention the lovingkindnesses of the LORD, and the praises of the LORD, according to all that the LORD hath bestowed on us, and the great goodness toward the house of Israel, which he hath bestowed on them according to his mercies, and according to the multitude of his lovingkindnesses.
desc: God sharing Israel's affliction and carrying them, pointing to Christ who bore our griefs and the Spirit who carries believers.

text: Thus saith the LORD, The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool: where is the house that ye build unto me? and where is the place of my rest? For all those things hath mine hand made, and all those things have been, saith the LORD: but to this man will I look, even to him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembleth at my word.
desc: The promise of an entirely new cosmos replacing the present order, fulfilled in Revelation's new heaven and earth.

text: Then the LORD said unto me, Out of the north an evil shall break forth upon all the inhabitants of the land. For, lo, I will call all the families of the kingdoms of the north, saith the LORD; and they shall come, and they shall set every one his throne at the entering of the gates of Jerusalem, and against all the walls thereof round about, and against all the cities of Judah.
desc: Babylon coming from the north to devastate Judah, the opening of Jeremiah's ministry announcing the coming judgment.

text: At that time they shall call Jerusalem the throne of the LORD; and all the nations shall be gathered unto it, to the name of the LORD, to Jerusalem: neither shall they walk any more after the imagination of their evil heart.
desc: Jerusalem becoming the throne of the LORD with all nations gathered, pointing to the Millennial and eternal kingdom.

text: If thou wilt return, O Israel, saith the LORD, return unto me: and if thou wilt put away thine abominations out of my sight, then shalt thou not remove. And thou shalt swear, The LORD liveth, in truth, in judgment, and in righteousness; and the nations shall bless themselves in him, and in him shall they glory.
desc: The call to flee Jerusalem as Babylon approaches, fulfilled in Nebuchadnezzar's campaigns against Judah.

text: I beheld the earth, and, lo, it was without form, and void; and the heavens, and they had no light. I beheld the mountains, and, lo, they trembled, and all the hills moved lightly.
desc: Jeremiah's apocalyptic vision of de-creation language applied to Judah's judgment, debated as local vs. eschatological.

text: O ye children of Benjamin, gather yourselves to flee out of the midst of Jerusalem, and blow the trumpet in Tekoa, and set up a sign of fire in Bethhaccerem: for evil appeareth out of the north, and great destruction.
desc: The call to mourning for Jerusalem before Babylon's sudden attack, fulfilled in the siege and destruction of 586 BC.

text: Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that it shall no more be called Tophet, nor the valley of the son of Hinnom, but the valley of slaughter: for they shall bury in Tophet, till there be no place.
desc: Tophet/Hinnom becoming a valley of slaughter for Jerusalem's idolaters, fulfilled in the horrors of the Babylonian siege.

text: Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will punish all them which are circumcised with the uncircumcised; Egypt, and Judah, and Edom, and the children of Ammon, and Moab, and all that are in the utmost corners, that dwell in the wilderness: for all these nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in the heart.
desc: God's judgment on circumcised-but-uncircumcised-hearted Israel alongside Egypt, Edom, Ammon, Moab, and Babylon.

text: For thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will sling out the inhabitants of the land at this once, and will distress them, that they may find it so.
desc: God slinging Judah from the land like a stone from a sling, fulfilled in the Babylonian deportations.

text: Therefore thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will bring evil upon them, which they shall not be able to escape; and though they shall cry unto me, I will not hearken unto them.
desc: Judgment as the natural fruit of Israel's own rebellious thoughts and refusal of God's word.

text: Thus saith the LORD against all mine evil neighbours, that touch the inheritance which I have caused my people Israel to inherit; Behold, I will pluck them out of their land, and pluck out the house of Judah from among them.
desc: God restoring the neighboring nations after judgment if they learn from Israel's example and embrace his ways.

text: Therefore thou shalt speak unto them this word; Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Every bottle shall be filled with wine: and they shall say unto thee, Do we not certainly know that every bottle shall be filled with wine?
desc: Judah intoxicated with God's cup of wrath, smashing against each other in the chaos of Babylon's conquest.

text: The cities of the south shall be shut up, and none shall open them: Judah shall be carried away captive all of it, it shall be wholly carried away captive.
desc: The total captivity of Judah to Babylon specifically predicted, fulfilled in the three deportations of 605, 597, and 586 BC.

text: Then said the LORD unto me, Though Moses and Samuel stood before me, yet my mind could not be toward this people: cast them out of my sight, and let them go forth.
desc: Even the greatest intercessors cannot avert Judah's judgment, so completely has the nation exhausted God's patience.

text: Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that it shall no more be said, The LORD liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt;
desc: A second Exodus from the north to replace the Egyptian Exodus as the defining redemptive event, pointing to Israel's modern regathering.

text: But if ye will not hearken unto me to hallow the sabbath day, and not to bear a burden, even entering in at the gates of Jerusalem on the sabbath day; then will I kindle a fire in the gates thereof, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem, and it shall not be quenched.
desc: Jerusalem's gates and palaces threatened with an unquenchable fire for Sabbath violation, fulfilled in Babylon's burning.

text: And say, Hear ye the word of the LORD, O kings of Judah, and inhabitants of Jerusalem; Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will bring evil upon this place, the which whosoever heareth, his ears shall tingle.
desc: The ear-tingling judgment on Jerusalem for child sacrifice in Hinnom, fulfilled in the horrors of Babylon's siege.

text: For thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will make thee a terror to thyself, and to all thy friends: and they shall fall by the sword of their enemies, and thine eyes shall behold it: and I will give all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall carry them captive into Babylon, and shall slay them with the sword.
desc: Jeremiah's prediction of Jerusalem's burning specifically by Babylon's king, fulfilled exactly in 586 BC.

text: Then said Jeremiah unto them, Thus shall ye say to Zedekiah: Thus saith the LORD God of Israel; Behold, I will turn back the weapons of war that are in your hands, wherewith ye fight against the king of Babylon, and against the Chaldeans, which besiege you without the walls, and I will assemble them into the midst of this city.
desc: Jeremiah's controversial call to surrender to Babylon as the only path to life, fulfilled when resisters died and surrenderers lived.

text: But if ye will not hear these words, I swear by myself, saith the LORD, that this house shall become a desolation.
desc: The temple's desolation sworn by God himself for disobedience, fulfilled in Nebuzaradan's burning of the temple.

text: Weep ye not for the dead, neither bemoan him: but weep sore for him that goeth away: for he shall return no more, nor see his native country. For thus saith the LORD touching Shallum the son of Josiah king of Judah, which reigned instead of Josiah his father, which went forth out of this place; He shall not return thither any more:
desc: Jeremiah's instruction to mourn Jehoahaz's captivity rather than Josiah's death, fulfilled when Pharaoh Necho took Jehoahaz to Egypt.

text: Therefore thus saith the LORD concerning Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah; They shall not lament for him, saying, Ah my brother! or, Ah sister! they shall not lament for him, saying, Ah lord! or, Ah his glory!
desc: Jehoiakim predicted to have no burial rites, debated whether fulfilled as Jerusalem fell before his death or shortly after.

text: As I live, saith the LORD, though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah were the signet upon my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence; And I will give thee into the hand of them that seek thy life, and into the hand of them whose face thou fearest, even into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of the Chaldeans.
desc: Jeconiah (Coniah) cursed to be childless on the throne, a puzzle Matthew resolves by tracing Jesus through Joseph's legal line only.

text: Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith the LORD. Therefore thus saith the LORD God of Israel against the pastors that feed my people; Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away, and have not visited them: behold, I will visit upon you the evil of your doings, saith the LORD.
desc: God promising to give Israel faithful shepherds after the failures of past leaders, pointing to Christ the Good Shepherd.

text: Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that they shall no more say, The LORD liveth, which brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt;
desc: The new Exodus from all nations superseding the Egyptian Exodus as the defining event of Israel's history.

text: The LORD shewed me, and, behold, two baskets of figs were set before the temple of the LORD, after that Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon had carried away captive Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah, and the princes of Judah, with the carpenters and smiths, from Jerusalem, and had brought them to Babylon.
desc: The good and bad figs vision predicting the exiles' return and the remnant in Jerusalem's destruction.

text: Behold, I will send and take all the families of the north, saith the LORD, and Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon, my servant, and will bring them against this land, and against the inhabitants thereof, and against all these nations round about, and will utterly destroy them, and make them an astonishment, and an hissing, and perpetual desolations.
desc: Seventy years of Babylonian dominance predicted exactly, the foundational time prophecy confirmed by Daniel.

text: For thus saith the LORD God of Israel unto me; Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send thee, to drink it. And they shall drink, and be moved, and be mad, because of the sword that I will send among them.
desc: God's cup of judgment passed to all nations, a symbol cited in Revelation's bowls of wrath.

text: In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah came this word unto Jeremiah from the LORD, saying, Thus saith the LORD to me; Make thee bonds and yokes, and put them upon thy neck,
desc: Nebuchadnezzar as God's appointed instrument over all nations, resistance bringing divine punishment.

text: … Then said the prophet Jeremiah unto Hananiah the prophet, Hear now, Hananiah; The LORD hath not sent thee; but thou makest this people to trust in a lie. Therefore thus saith the LORD; Behold, I will cast thee from off the face of the earth: this year thou shalt die, because thou hast taught rebellion against the LORD.
desc: Jeremiah's prediction of Hananiah's death within the year for his false prophecy, fulfilled two months later.

text: For, lo, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah, saith the LORD: and I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.
desc: At the very moment Jeremiah announces the exile, he announces its reversal: 'the days come… that I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah… and they shall possess the land.' The prophet of doom is simultaneously the prophet of return — the Book of Consolation (Jer. 30-33) begins here.

text: Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob's trouble; but he shall be saved out of it.
desc: The unprecedented time of Jacob's trouble, identified with Daniel's 70th week and the Great Tribulation.

text: For it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD of hosts, that I will break his yoke from off thy neck, and will burst thy bonds, and strangers shall no more serve themselves of him:
desc: Israel freed from all foreign domination and serving their own Davidic King, to be fulfilled in the messianic kingdom.

text: Therefore fear thou not, O my servant Jacob, saith the LORD; neither be dismayed, O Israel: for, lo, I will save thee from afar, and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and shall be in rest, and be quiet, and none shall make him afraid.
desc: God's promise that regathered Israel will finally rest securely in peace, to be fulfilled in the messianic kingdom.

text: At the same time, saith the LORD, will I be the God of all the families of Israel, and they shall be my people. Thus saith the LORD, The people which were left of the sword found grace in the wilderness; even Israel, when I went to cause him to rest.
desc: The New Covenant formula 'I will be their God and they will be my people' applied to all Israel's families at the restoration.

text: Thus saith the LORD; Refrain thy voice from weeping, and thine eyes from tears: for thy work shall be rewarded, saith the LORD; and they shall come again from the land of the enemy.
desc: Rachel weeping for her children, fulfilled at Herod's massacre; the promise of their return from exile pointing to the resurrection.

text: Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; As yet they shall use this speech in the land of Judah and in the cities thereof, when I shall bring again their captivity; The LORD bless thee, O habitation of justice, and mountain of holiness.
desc: Israel's joyful restoration after desolation, the spiritual renewal of the nation under the New Covenant.

text: Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man, and with the seed of beast. And it shall come to pass, that like as I have watched over them, to pluck up, and to break down, and to throw down, and to destroy, and to afflict; so will I watch over them, to build, and to plant, saith the LORD.
desc: The God who 'watched over' Judah to pluck up and destroy pledges to watch just as vigilantly 'to build, and to plant' — and the proverb of inherited guilt ('the fathers have eaten a sour grape…') will be retired: each person answers for his own sin. Individual accountability enters covenant history on the eve of the new covenant passage (31:31-34).

text: Thus saith the LORD, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The LORD of hosts is his name:
desc: Israel's national existence as permanent as the cosmos itself, God's guarantee of Israel's eternal survival as a people.

text: Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that the city shall be built to the LORD from the tower of Hananeel unto the gate of the corner. And the measuring line shall yet go forth over against it upon the hill Gareb, and shall compass about to Goath.
desc: Jerusalem's future restoration with specific boundary points, the city rebuilt and consecrated to the LORD.

text: Behold, I will gather them out of all countries, whither I have driven them in mine anger, and in my fury, and in great wrath; and I will bring them again unto this place, and I will cause them to dwell safely:
desc: God's regathering of Israel from every nation of the Diaspora, progressively fulfilled in modern Jewish immigration.

text: Behold, I will bring it health and cure, and I will cure them, and will reveal unto them the abundance of peace and truth. And I will cause the captivity of Judah and the captivity of Israel to return, and will build them, as at the first.
desc: Spoken from prison while Babylon's siege ramps stood against the walls: God will bring 'health and cure,' return the captives of Judah and Israel, cleanse their iniquity — and ruined Jerusalem will become 'a name of joy, a praise and an honour before all the nations of the earth.'

text: Thus saith the LORD; Again there shall be heard in this place, which ye say shall be desolate without man and without beast, even in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem, that are desolate, without man, and without inhabitant, and without beast,
desc: In streets about to fall 'desolate, without man and without beast,' God promises the return of specific sounds: 'the voice of joy… the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride,' and of worshipers singing 'Praise the LORD of hosts: for the LORD is good; for his mercy endureth for ever.' Jewish weddings sing these very words over couples to this day — the prophecy is fulfilled again every week.

text: For thus saith the LORD; David shall never want a man to sit upon the throne of the house of Israel; Neither shall the priests the Levites want a man before me to offer burnt offerings, and to kindle meat offerings, and to do sacrifice continually.
desc: The righteous Branch of David who executes justice on earth, pointing directly to the messianic reign of Christ.

sub: Restoration — Davidic covenant as fixed as daylight
text: … Thus saith the LORD; If ye can break my covenant of the day, and my covenant of the night, and that there should not be day and night in their season;
desc: God stakes the Davidic and levitical covenants on the cosmos itself: only 'if ye can break my covenant of the day, and my covenant of the night' can David lack a son to reign. Answering those who said 'the two families… he hath even cast them off,' God declares Israel's rejection as impossible as cancelling sunrise.

text: The word which came unto Jeremiah from the LORD, when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and all his army, and all the kingdoms of the earth of his dominion, and all the people, fought against Jerusalem, and against all the cities thereof, saying,
desc: Jeremiah's repeated prediction of Jerusalem's burning by Babylon, fulfilled in 586 BC exactly as warned.

text: Therefore thus saith the LORD of Jehoiakim king of Judah; He shall have none to sit upon the throne of David: and his dead body shall be cast out in the day to the heat, and in the night to the frost.
desc: Jehoiakim's shameful unburied death predicted, disputed by scholars since 2 Kings says he slept with his fathers.

text: Then came the word of the LORD unto the prophet Jeremiah, saying, Thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel; Thus shall ye say to the king of Judah, that sent you unto me to enquire of me; Behold, Pharaoh's army, which is come forth to help you, shall return to Egypt into their own land.
desc: Jeremiah's unwavering prediction of Jerusalem's fall to Babylon, confirmed by the events of 586 BC.

text: Then said Jeremiah unto Zedekiah, Thus saith the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel; If thou wilt assuredly go forth unto the king of Babylon's princes, then thy soul shall live, and this city shall not be burned with fire; and thou shalt live, and thine house:
desc: God's merciful offer to Zedekiah to surrender and spare the city, rejected, leading to Jerusalem's destruction.

text: In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, came Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and all his army against Jerusalem, and they besieged it. And in the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, the ninth day of the month, the city was broken up.
desc: The precise date of Jerusalem's siege given to Ezekiel as a sign while he was in Babylon, confirmed in 2 Kings.

text: Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, saying; Ye and your wives have both spoken with your mouths, and fulfilled with your hand, saying, We will surely perform our vows that we have vowed, to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto her: ye will surely accomplish your vows, and surely perform your vows.
desc: God's declaration of Jerusalem's desolation for idolatry confirmed, with Pharaoh Hophra's death predicted and fulfilled.

text: The word of the LORD which came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Gentiles; Against Egypt, against the army of Pharaohnecho king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates in Carchemish, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon smote in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah.
desc: Dated 'against the army of Pharaohnecho... which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon smote in the fourth year of Jehoiakim': Jeremiah calls the battle of Carchemish (605 BC) and Egypt's long eclipse — 'yet afterward it shall be inhabited' (v.26), judged but never annihilated.

text: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Philistines, before that Pharaoh smote Gaza. Thus saith the LORD; Behold, waters rise up out of the north, and shall be an overflowing flood, and shall overflow the land, and all that is therein; the city, and them that dwell therein: then the men shall cry, and all the inhabitants of the land shall howl.
desc: 'Waters rise up out of the north... Baldness is come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is cut off.' In Kislev 604 BC, Nebuchadnezzar sacked Ashkelon so thoroughly that the Babylonian Chronicle boasts he 'turned the city into a mound and heaps of ruins' — the end of Philistine civilization.

sub: Moab and the shaming of Chemosh
text: Against Moab thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Woe unto Nebo! for it is spoiled: Kiriathaim is confounded and taken: Misgab is confounded and dismayed.
desc: Jeremiah's oracle against Moab — her cities destroyed, her god Chemosh shamed, with a closing promise to restore Moab's fortunes in the latter days.

text: Concerning the Ammonites, thus saith the LORD; Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir? why then doth their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities? Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will cause an alarm of war to be heard in Rabbah of the Ammonites; and it shall be a desolate heap, and her daughters shall be burned with fire: then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the LORD.
desc: Oracle against Ammon for occupying Israelite territory, predicting judgment and a later restoration.

sub: Edom in the clefts of the rock
text: Concerning Edom, thus saith the LORD of hosts; Is wisdom no more in Teman? is counsel perished from the prudent? is their wisdom vanished? Flee ye, turn back, dwell deep, O inhabitants of Dedan; for I will bring the calamity of Esau upon him, the time that I will visit him.
desc: Jeremiah's oracle against Edom in its rock fortress — pride humbled, the land made a perpetual desolation like Sodom.

sub: Damascus — fire in the wall of Ben-hadad
text: Concerning Damascus. Hamath is confounded, and Arpad: for they have heard evil tidings: they are fainthearted; there is sorrow on the sea; it cannot be quiet. Damascus is waxed feeble, and turneth herself to flee, and fear hath seized on her: anguish and sorrows have taken her, as a woman in travail.
desc: A century and a half after Isaiah, Jeremiah pronounces on a diminished Damascus: 'I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it shall consume the palaces of Benhadad' — the once-royal city now judged among the minor states swallowed by Babylon.

text: Concerning Kedar, and concerning the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon shall smite, thus saith the LORD; Arise ye, go up to Kedar, and spoil the men of the east.
desc: 'Concerning Kedar, and concerning the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadrezzar... shall smite': the desert tribes — tents, flocks, camels — will be scattered and Hazor become 'a dwelling for dragons... for ever.' An oracle against nomads, naming their conqueror in advance.

text: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet against Elam in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying, Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Behold, I will break the bow of Elam, the chief of their might.
desc: Oracle against Elam predicting scattering and judgment, with a later promise of restoration from captivity.

text: The word that the LORD spake against Babylon and against the land of the Chaldeans by Jeremiah the prophet. Declare ye among the nations, and publish, and set up a standard; publish, and conceal not: say, Babylon is taken, Bel is confounded, Merodach is broken in pieces; her idols are confounded, her images are broken in pieces.
desc: Jeremiah's vast oracle against Babylon — taken by a nation from the north, made a perpetual desolation; the empire that destroyed Jerusalem judged in turn.

text: Her adversaries are the chief, her enemies prosper; for the LORD hath afflicted her for the multitude of her transgressions: her children are gone into captivity before the enemy.
desc: Jerusalem confessing God's righteousness in the exile, a profound acknowledgment that the covenant curses were just.

text: The punishment of thine iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Zion; he will no more carry thee away into captivity: he will visit thine iniquity, O daughter of Edom; he will discover thy sins.
desc: Zion's punishment complete while Edom faces judgment, pointing to Israel's restoration and Edom's permanent desolation.

text: Thou also, son of man, take thee a tile, and lay it before thee, and pourtray upon it the city, even Jerusalem: And lay siege against it, and build a fort against it, and cast a mount against it; set the camp also against it, and set battering rams against it round about.
desc: Ezekiel's sign-prophecy enacting the siege of Jerusalem, the city surrounded and besieged by a miniature representation.

text: Thus saith the Lord GOD; This is Jerusalem: I have set it in the midst of the nations and countries that are round about her. And she hath changed my judgments into wickedness more than the nations, and my statutes more than the countries that are round about her: for they have refused my judgments and my statutes, they have not walked in them.
desc: Jerusalem made a waste and a reproach among the nations for its sins, fulfilled in the Babylonian destruction.

text: … And say, Ye mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD; Thus saith the Lord GOD to the mountains, and to the hills, to the rivers, and to the valleys; Behold, I, even I, will bring a sword upon you, and I will destroy your high places.
desc: Israel's idolatrous high places destroyed and their worshipers slain, that God's sovereignty might be acknowledged.

text: … Also, thou son of man, thus saith the Lord GOD unto the land of Israel; An end, the end is come upon the four corners of the land.
desc: The end declared for the land of Israel, God's anger poured out in final covenant judgment.

text: Again the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, Son of man, thy brethren, even thy brethren, the men of thy kindred, and all the house of Israel wholly, are they unto whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said, Get you far from the LORD: unto us is this land given in possession.
desc: God himself as a little sanctuary to the exiles, promising eventual regathering and a new heart and new spirit.

text: The word of the LORD also came unto me, saying, Son of man, thou dwellest in the midst of a rebellious house, which have eyes to see, and see not; they have ears to hear, and hear not: for they are a rebellious house.
desc: Ezekiel's acted prophecy of exile digging through a wall, illustrating Zedekiah's blinded flight, fulfilled in 586 BC.

text: … Son of man, eat thy bread with quaking, and drink thy water with trembling and with carefulness; And say unto the people of the land, Thus saith the Lord GOD of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and of the land of Israel; They shall eat their bread with carefulness, and drink their water with astonishment, that her land may be desolate from all that is therein, because of the violence of all them that dwell therein.
desc: Ezekiel demonstrating with his eating and drinking the terror Jerusalem would experience under siege.

text: The word of the LORD came again to me, saying, Son of man, when the land sinneth against me by trespassing grievously, then will I stretch out mine hand upon it, and will break the staff of the bread thereof, and will send famine upon it, and will cut off man and beast from it:
desc: Even the three greatest righteous men could not save a thoroughly corrupt generation, only themselves.

text: When I shall bring again their captivity, the captivity of Sodom and her daughters, and the captivity of Samaria and her daughters, then will I bring again the captivity of thy captives in the midst of them:
desc: God remembering his ancient covenant with Israel despite her unfaithfulness, the basis for the new everlasting covenant.

text: Thus saith the Lord GOD; I will also take of the highest branch of the high cedar, and will set it; I will crop off from the top of his young twigs a tender one, and will plant it upon an high mountain and eminent:
desc: God planting the messianic Branch from the Davidic cedar, a tender shoot from the top that becomes a mighty tree.

text: As I live, saith the Lord GOD, surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you: And I will bring you out from the people, and will gather you out of the countries wherein ye are scattered, with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out.
desc: The end-times regathering of Israel through a second Exodus with divine power, leading to the covenant relationship's restoration.

text: … And say to the land of Israel, Thus saith the LORD; Behold, I am against thee, and will draw forth my sword out of his sheath, and will cut off from thee the righteous and the wicked.
desc: Ezekiel's sword oracle against Jerusalem and Judah, the sword of God's judgment falling on his own people.

text: … Now, thou son of man, wilt thou judge, wilt thou judge the bloody city? yea, thou shalt shew her all her abominations. Then say thou, Thus saith the Lord GOD, The city sheddeth blood in the midst of it, that her time may come, and maketh idols against herself to defile herself.
desc: God addressing the wickedness of Israel's leadership, with the implication that only the rightful King (Christ) can bring order.

text: Again in the ninth year, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, Son of man, write thee the name of the day, even of this same day: the king of Babylon set himself against Jerusalem this same day.
desc: Ezekiel given the exact date of Jerusalem's siege while in Babylon, confirmed in 2 Kings as a supernatural sign.

sub: Four nations who cheered Jerusalem's fall
text: … Behold, therefore I will deliver thee to the men of the east for a possession, and they shall set their palaces in thee, and make their dwellings in thee: they shall eat thy fruit, and they shall drink thy milk.
desc: Four neighbors who applauded the temple's destruction receive matched sentences: Ammon given to 'the men of the east,' Moab opened, Edom laid desolate, the Philistine remnant cut off — 'and they shall know that I am the LORD.'

text: And it came to pass in the eleventh year, in the first day of the month, that the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, Son of man, because that Tyrus hath said against Jerusalem, Aha, she is broken that was the gates of the people: she is turned unto me: I shall be replenished, now she is laid waste:
desc: Ezekiel's oracle against Tyre — many nations against her, her stones and dust cast into the sea, left a bare rock for nets — the most debated fulfillment prophecy.

sub: Tyre — the shipwreck of a market-state
text: … Now, thou son of man, take up a lamentation for Tyrus; And say unto Tyrus, O thou that art situate at the entry of the sea, which art a merchant of the people for many isles, Thus saith the Lord GOD; O Tyrus, thou hast said, I am of perfect beauty.
desc: Tyre as a magnificent trading ship — cedar of Lebanon, oars of Bashan oak, sails of Egyptian linen, a cargo manifest naming more than thirty peoples and places — wrecked 'in the midst of the seas' while the merchants of the world hiss at her fall.

sub: The proud prince; the cherub in Eden
text: The word of the LORD came again unto me, saying, Son of man, say unto the prince of Tyrus, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because thine heart is lifted up, and thou hast said, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas; yet thou art a man, and not God, though thou set thine heart as the heart of God:
desc: The oracle against the self-deifying prince of Tyre, and the lament over the 'king of Tyre' whose Edenic, cherubic language has fueled the debate over a typological reference to Satan's fall.

text: … Speak, and say, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I am against thee, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon that lieth in the midst of his rivers, which hath said, My river is mine own, and I have made it for myself.
desc: Ezekiel's oracle against Pharaoh and Egypt — desolation, then a permanent reduction to a 'base kingdom' that would never again rule the nations.

sub: Egypt — the day of the LORD on the Nile
text: … For the day is near, even the day of the LORD is near, a cloudy day; it shall be the time of the heathen. And the sword shall come upon Egypt, and great pain shall be in Ethiopia, when the slain shall fall in Egypt, and they shall take away her multitude, and her foundations shall be broken down.
desc: Egypt and her helpers fall 'from the tower of Syene' — border to border; her idols cease from Noph (Memphis), her pride of power comes down, and 'there shall be no more a prince of the land of Egypt' — no more native pharaohs commanding empire.

text: … Son of man, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, and to his multitude; Whom art thou like in thy greatness? Behold, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon with fair branches, and with a shadowing shroud, and of an high stature; and his top was among the thick boughs.
desc: Pharaoh compared to a great cedar of Lebanon that falls, the pride of Egypt brought low by Assyrian-Babylonian power.

text: And it came to pass in the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, in the first day of the month, that the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, Son of man, take up a lamentation for Pharaoh king of Egypt, and say unto him, Thou art like a young lion of the nations, and thou art as a whale in the seas: and thou camest forth with thy rivers, and troubledst the waters with thy feet, and fouledst their rivers.
desc: A lament for Pharaoh and Egypt descending to Sheol, the dragon of the Nile caught in God's net.

text: Then the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, Son of man, they that inhabit those wastes of the land of Israel speak, saying, Abraham was one, and he inherited the land: but we are many; the land is given us for inheritance.
desc: The remnant left in Israel wrongly claiming the land while the faithful were in exile, bringing judgment on themselves.

text: And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel, prophesy, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD unto the shepherds; Woe be to the shepherds of Israel that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks? … Ye eat the fat, and ye clothe you with the wool, ye kill them that are fed: but ye feed not the flock. The diseased have ye not strengthened, neither have ye healed that which was sick, neither have ye bound up that which was broken, neither have ye brought again that which was driven away, neither have ye sought that which was lost; but with force and with cruelty have ye ruled them.
desc: Ezekiel's indictment of Israel's false shepherds and the promise that God Himself will shepherd His flock, setting over them 'my servant David' — read of the Messiah, the Good Shepherd.

text: … I will lay thy cities waste, and thou shalt be desolate, and thou shalt know that I am the LORD. Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end:
desc: Comprehensive judgment on Edom for perpetual hatred of Israel and seizing their land during the exile.

text: Also, thou son of man, prophesy unto the mountains of Israel, and say, Ye mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD: Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because the enemy hath said against you, Aha, even the ancient high places are ours in possession:
desc: The mountains of Israel promised restoration and fruitfulness after their desolation by enemies.

text: Moreover the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, Son of man, when the house of Israel dwelt in their own land, they defiled it by their own way and by their doings: their way was before me as the uncleanness of a removed woman.
desc: God's motivation for regathering Israel as his holy name's vindication before the nations, not for Israel's merit.

text: Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you. A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.
desc: God's new-covenant promise to cleanse with water, give a new heart, and put His Spirit within — a foundational text for regeneration, baptism, and the gift of the Spirit.

text: Thus saith the Lord GOD; In the day that I shall have cleansed you from all your iniquities I will also cause you to dwell in the cities, and the wastes shall be builded.
desc: Israel's agricultural restoration as a sign of divine blessing, nations acknowledging God when the land blooms.

sub: One nation, one King, an everlasting covenant
text: The word of the LORD came again unto me, saying, Moreover, thou son of man, take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions:
desc: The sign of the two sticks joined — Israel reunited under one Davidic king, an everlasting covenant of peace, and God's sanctuary in their midst forever.

sub: Gog defeated; the Spirit poured out
text: Therefore, thou son of man, prophesy against Gog, and say, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I am against thee, O Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal: And I will turn thee back, and leave but the sixth part of thee, and will cause thee to come up from the north parts, and will bring thee upon the mountains of Israel:
desc: The aftermath of Gog's invasion — the LORD's decisive victory, His glory revealed to the nations, and His Spirit poured out on a restored Israel.

sub: The measured temple; 'The LORD is there'
text: In the five and twentieth year of our captivity, in the beginning of the year, in the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after that the city was smitten, in the selfsame day the hand of the LORD was upon me, and brought me thither.
desc: Ezekiel's vast closing vision — a meticulously measured future temple, the return of God's glory, the river flowing from the sanctuary, the reapportioned land, and the city named 'The LORD is there' — one of the most debated passages in all eschatology.

text: And in the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams, wherewith his spirit was troubled, and his sleep brake from him. Then the king commanded to call the magicians, and the astrologers, and the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans, for to shew the king his dreams. So they came and stood before the king.
desc: Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the four-metal image — four successive kingdoms culminating in the stone, the everlasting kingdom of God.

text: The tree that thou sawest, which grew, and was strong, whose height reached unto the heaven, and the sight thereof to all the earth; Whose leaves were fair, and the fruit thereof much, and in it was meat for all; under which the beasts of the field dwelt, and upon whose branches the fowls of the heaven had their habitation:
desc: Daniel's prophecy of Nebuchadnezzar's seven-period madness and restoration, humbling the king until he confessed God's sovereignty over the kingdoms of men.

text: And this is the writing that was written, MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN. This is the interpretation of the thing: MENE; God hath numbered thy kingdom, and finished it.
desc: Daniel's reading of the handwriting on Belshazzar's wall, foretelling Babylon's fall to the Medes and Persians that very night.

text: I Daniel was grieved in my spirit in the midst of my body, and the visions of my head troubled me. I came near unto one of them that stood by, and asked him the truth of all this. So he told me, and made me know the interpretation of the things.
desc: The angel's interpretation of the four beasts and the little horn, ending in judgment and the everlasting kingdom given to the saints.

sub: Medo-Persia, Greece, and the little horn
text: In the third year of the reign of king Belshazzar a vision appeared unto me, even unto me Daniel, after that which appeared unto me at the first. And I saw in a vision; and it came to pass, when I saw, that I was at Shushan in the palace, which is in the province of Elam; and I saw in a vision, and I was by the river of Ulai.
desc: The vision of the ram (Medo-Persia) and goat (Greece) and the little horn, widely identified with Antiochus IV — the clearest named-empire sequence in Daniel.

text: In the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, which was made king over the realm of the Chaldeans; In the first year of his reign I Daniel understood by books the number of the years, whereof the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he would accomplish seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem. … And I set my face unto the Lord God, to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes: And I prayed unto the LORD my God, and made my confession, and said, O Lord, the great and dreadful God, keeping the covenant and mercy to them that love him, and to them that keep his commandments;
desc: Daniel's prayer of confession for Israel's sin, prompted by Jeremiah's seventy-years prophecy, leading into the revelation of the seventy weeks.

text: And whiles I was speaking, and praying, and confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and presenting my supplication before the LORD my God for the holy mountain of my God;
desc: Gabriel comes swiftly in answer to Daniel's prayer to unveil the seventy weeks — the prophecy pointing to the Messiah.

keywords: Daniel 9:25|Daniel 9:24|Daniel 9:26|Daniel 9:27|Seventy Weeks|70 weeks|seventy sevens|Messiah the Prince|cut off|confirm the covenant|Messianic timeline|abomination|desolation
text: Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.
desc: Gabriel's revelation of the seventy weeks (490 years) decreed on Israel — a timeline to the Messiah's coming and cutting off, the chronological backbone of biblical prophecy.
hebrewKey: מָשִׁיחַ נָגִיד (Mashiach Nagid) — Messiah the Prince; and שָׁבֻעִים שִׁבְעִים (shavuim shivim) — seventy sevens/weeks
archaeology: The decree to restore Jerusalem is anchored by the Persian-era commissions of Ezra 7 (Artaxerxes, 457 BC) and Nehemiah 2 (445 BC). Daniel fragments among the Dead Sea Scrolls (4QDan, 1st-2nd c. BC) confirm the text of this chapter circulated well before the Christian era.
trad_Jewish: Traditional rabbinic reading (Seder Olam, Rashi) runs the seventy sevens from the destruction of the First Temple to the fall of the Second, taking the anointed one who is cut off as a high priest or King Agrippa rather than the Messiah. The Talmud (Nazir 32b) wrestles with the chronology; the Messianic-date reading is generally avoided.
trad_Catholic: A Messianic timeline fulfilled in Christ. Counting from the Persian decree to the Anointed One, Christ is cut off (crucified) not for Himself but for many; the people of the coming prince are the Romans who destroyed the city and sanctuary in AD 70. Christ confirms the new covenant in His blood.
trad_Protestant: Two main camps. Historic and amillennial readers see the whole prophecy fulfilled at the first advent — the seventieth week is Christ's ministry and death, the covenant confirmed by the cross, sacrifice made to cease at Calvary. Dispensationalists insert a gap before a still-future seventieth week, a seven-year tribulation in which an antichrist confirms a covenant and breaks it at its midpoint.
trad_Oneness: Apostolics read the prophecy Christocentrically: the Messiah the Prince who is cut off is the Lord Jesus — God manifest in flesh (1 Tim 3:16) — whose once-for-all death caused the sacrifice and oblation to cease, rending the temple veil. The dating of the decree to the Anointed One is among the strongest evidences that Jesus is the promised Messiah. Apostolic eschatology divides on whether the seventieth week is wholly past or partly future, but agrees the covenant is confirmed in Christ alone.
trad_Academic: Critical scholarship dates the final form of Daniel to the Maccabean crisis (~165 BC) and reads the seventy sevens as schematic — from Jeremiah's word to Antiochus IV. The anointed one cut off is taken as the murdered high priest Onias III (171 BC) and the desolating prince as Antiochus, who desecrated the Temple in 167 BC (Montgomery; Collins, Hermeneia).

text: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia a thing was revealed unto Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar; and the thing was true, but the time appointed was long: and he understood the thing, and had understanding of the vision.
desc: Daniel's final vision: a time of trouble unmatched in history, the deliverance of God's people, and the resurrection of the dead to everlasting life or contempt.

text: Also I in the first year of Darius the Mede, even I, stood to confirm and to strengthen him. And now will I shew thee the truth. Behold, there shall stand up yet three kings in Persia; and the fourth shall be far richer than they all: and by his strength through his riches he shall stir up all against the realm of Grecia.
desc: Daniel 11's strikingly detailed account of the wars of the kings of the North and South — Ptolemies and Seleucids — climaxing in the desecrating ruler; the centerpiece of the predictive-vs-ex-eventu debate.

text: And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.
desc: The clearest OT statement of bodily resurrection to eternal life or eternal shame, foundational to the NT resurrection hope.

sub: Sealed till the time of the end
text: But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall be increased. Then I Daniel looked, and, behold, there stood other two, the one on this side of the bank of the river, and the other on that side of the bank of the river.
desc: Daniel is told to seal the prophecy until the time of the end, with the promise that he will rest and rise to his reward at the last day.

text: And the LORD said unto him, Call his name Jezreel; for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel.
desc: The blood of Jezreel to be avenged on Jehu's dynasty, fulfilled when Zechariah (4th generation) was assassinated.

text: Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.
desc: Israel's restoration and reidentification as sons of God, quoted by Paul as the basis for Gentile inclusion.

text: Therefore, behold, I will allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak comfortably unto her. And I will give her her vineyards from thence, and the valley of Achor for a door of hope: and she shall sing there, as in the days of her youth, and as in the day when she came up out of the land of Egypt.
desc: God wooing Israel back through the wilderness experience, and the restoration of covenant relationship.

text: For I will be unto Ephraim as a lion, and as a young lion to the house of Judah: I, even I, will tear and go away; I will take away, and none shall rescue him. I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.
desc: Israel's future return to the LORD after the time of trouble, with Hosea 6:2's resurrection pattern pointing to Christ.

text: They shall not dwell in the LORD'S land; but Ephraim shall return to Egypt, and they shall eat unclean things in Assyria. They shall not offer wine offerings to the LORD, neither shall they be pleasing unto him: their sacrifices shall be unto them as the bread of mourners; all that eat thereof shall be polluted: for their bread for their soul shall not come into the house of the LORD.
desc: Northern Israel's exile to Assyria and dispersion, fulfilled in 722 BC when Assyria deported the ten tribes.

text: It shall be also carried unto Assyria for a present to king Jareb: Ephraim shall receive shame, and Israel shall be ashamed of his own counsel.
desc: The golden calf idols of Samaria taken as plunder to Assyria, fulfilled when Sargon II carried off Israelite wealth.

text: Therefore shall a tumult arise among thy people, and all thy fortresses shall be spoiled, as Shalman spoiled Betharbel in the day of battle: the mother was dashed in pieces upon her children.
desc: Israel's sin reaching the depth of Gibeah's wickedness, bringing military disaster as in Benjamin's near-destruction.

text: O Israel, thou hast destroyed thyself; but in me is thine help. I will be thy king: where is any other that may save thee in all thy cities? and thy judges of whom thou saidst, Give me a king and princes?
desc: Israel's self-destruction and God alone as savior declared, the indictment before the final Assyrian judgment.

text: I will heal their backsliding, I will love them freely: for mine anger is turned away from him. I will be as the dew unto Israel: he shall grow as the lily, and cast forth his roots as Lebanon.
desc: God's unconditional love healing Israel's turning away, a portrait of the ultimate restoration in the messianic age.

text: The word of the LORD that came to Joel the son of Pethuel. Hear this, ye old men, and give ear, all ye inhabitants of the land. Hath this been in your days, or even in the days of your fathers?
desc: Joel's day-of-locust plague and call to repentance, used as a typological framework for the end-times Day of the LORD.

text: Blow ye the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain: let all the inhabitants of the land tremble: for the day of the LORD cometh, for it is nigh at hand;
desc: The Day of the LORD announced with trumpet alarm, the eschatological judgment described in apocalyptic imagery.

text: Therefore also now, saith the LORD, turn ye even to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning: And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the LORD your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil.
desc: Between devastation and outpouring stands the summons: 'Turn ye even to me with all your heart… and rend your heart, and not your garments.' Everything Joel promises after — restored years, poured Spirit, delivered remnant — hangs on this hinge. It is the Old Testament's altar call.

text: Then will the LORD be jealous for his land, and pity his people. Yea, the LORD will answer and say unto his people, Behold, I will send you corn, and wine, and oil, and ye shall be satisfied therewith: and I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen:
desc: After the locust devastation and the call to rend hearts, God answers: grain, wine, and oil again; the northern army removed; and the line generations have clung to — 'I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten.' The pledge stands one verse before the Spirit-outpouring promise of 2:28.

text: For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.
desc: All nations gathered for judgment in the valley of decision, the great end-times gathering before God's throne.

text: Proclaim ye this among the Gentiles; Prepare war, wake up the mighty men, let all the men of war draw near; let them come up: Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruninghooks into spears: let the weak say, I am strong.
desc: Joel's oracle of the nations gathered to the valley of Jehoshaphat for judgment on the Day of the LORD, followed by blessing for God's people.

text: Thus saith the LORD; For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron:
desc: God's judgment pattern on six pagan nations, then Judah, and finally Israel itself — eight oracles in the identical formula, the last one turning on the hearers; fulfilled in Assyrian and Babylonian conquests.

text: Hear ye, and testify in the house of Jacob, saith the Lord GOD, the God of hosts, That in the day that I shall visit the transgressions of Israel upon him I will also visit the altars of Bethel: and the horns of the altar shall be cut off, and fall to the ground.
desc: Amos pronouncing judgment on Israel's sins of exploitation and false worship, warning of the Assyrian exile.

text: The Lord GOD hath sworn by his holiness, that, lo, the days shall come upon you, that he will take you away with hooks, and your posterity with fishhooks. And ye shall go out at the breaches, every cow at that which is before her; and ye shall cast them into the palace, saith the LORD.
desc: Israel's wealthy women compared to cattle dragged away with hooks, the humiliation of Assyrian deportation.

text: Hear ye this word which I take up against you, even a lamentation, O house of Israel. The virgin of Israel is fallen; she shall no more rise: she is forsaken upon her land; there is none to raise her up.
desc: The virgin of Israel has fallen and will rise no more, the lament for the northern kingdom's irreversible fall.
