text: Therefore will I cause you to go into captivity beyond Damascus, saith the LORD, whose name is The God of hosts.
desc: Israel's captivity beyond Damascus (Assyria) predicted, fulfilled in 722 BC when Sargon II deported the ten tribes.

text: Therefore now shall they go captive with the first that go captive, and the banquet of them that stretched themselves shall be removed. The Lord GOD hath sworn by himself, saith the LORD the God of hosts, I abhor the excellency of Jacob, and hate his palaces: therefore will I deliver up the city with all that is therein.
desc: The luxurious elite of Israel going into exile first, fulfilled in Sargon's deportation of the ruling classes.

text: But, behold, I will raise up against you a nation, O house of Israel, saith the LORD the God of hosts; and they shall afflict you from the entering in of Hemath unto the river of the wilderness.
desc: Assyria raised up against Israel from north to south, fulfilled in the comprehensive Assyrian devastation.

text: And the high places of Isaac shall be desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste; and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.
desc: Israel's sanctuaries desolated and Jeroboam's dynasty ended by the sword, fulfilled in Zechariah's assassination.

text: Therefore thus saith the LORD; Thy wife shall be an harlot in the city, and thy sons and thy daughters shall fall by the sword, and thy land shall be divided by line; and thou shalt die in a polluted land: and Israel shall surely go into captivity forth of his land.
desc: Amos's judgment prophecy against the priest Amaziah who tried to silence him, all points fulfilled in the Assyrian conquest.

text: Behold, the eyes of the Lord GOD are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth; saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, saith the LORD.
desc: The sternest book in the prophets ends with a filter, not a furnace: 'I will destroy it from off the face of the earth; saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob… For, lo, I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.' Dispersion with preservation — stated as one act.

text: Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that the plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him that soweth seed; and the mountains shall drop sweet wine, and all the hills shall melt.
desc: The messianic age's superabundant harvest where sowing and reaping overlap, the fullness of covenant blessing.

text: The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord GOD concerning Edom; We have heard a rumour from the LORD, and an ambassador is sent among the heathen, Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle.
desc: Obadiah's vision against Edom — the proud nation in its rock fastness brought low for its violence against brother Jacob.

text: If thieves came to thee, if robbers by night, (how art thou cut off!) would they not have stolen till they had enough? if the grapegatherers came to thee, would they not leave some grapes?
desc: Edom's total devastation exceeding that of mere thieves — nothing left, completely exposed and cut off.

text: For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever. In the day that thou stoodest on the other side, in the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, even thou wast as one of them.
desc: For standing aloof, looting, and handing over Jacob's fugitives on the day Jerusalem fell, Esau's nation is sentenced: 'shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever' — the only nation in Scripture sentenced to total, permanent extinction.

text: For the day of the LORD is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head. For as ye have drunk upon my holy mountain, so shall all the heathen drink continually, yea, they shall drink, and they shall swallow down, and they shall be as though they had not been.
desc: The Day of the LORD's lex talionis principle applied to Edom and all nations, foreshadowing the final judgment.

text: And Jonah began to enter into the city a day's journey, and he cried, and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.
desc: Jonah's 40-day warning to Nineveh, conditionally fulfilled as Nineveh repented and God relented — demonstrating divine mercy.

sub: Samaria — stones poured into the valley
text: Therefore I will make Samaria as an heap of the field, and as plantings of a vineyard: and I will pour down the stones thereof into the valley, and I will discover the foundations thereof.
desc: 'I will make Samaria as an heap of the field, and as plantings of a vineyard: and I will pour down the stones thereof into the valley, and I will discover the foundations thereof' — spoken while Samaria was a fortified royal capital at its height.

text: For the inhabitant of Maroth waited carefully for good: but evil came down from the LORD unto the gate of Jerusalem. O thou inhabitant of Lachish, bind the chariot to the swift beast: she is the beginning of the sin to the daughter of Zion: for the transgressions of Israel were found in thee.
desc: Micah mourning Judah's coming catastrophe after Samaria's fall, pointing to Jerusalem itself being threatened.

text: I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of thee; I will surely gather the remnant of Israel; I will put them together as the sheep of Bozrah, as the flock in the midst of their fold: they shall make great noise by reason of the multitude of men.
desc: God gathering the remnant of Israel as a flock, the breaker (Christ) going before them.

sub: Zion plowed — the prophecy that saved Jeremiah
text: Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of the forest.
desc: 'Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of the forest.' A century later this exact verse is quoted in court to save Jeremiah's life (Jer. 26:18) — the Bible's own record of a prophecy being cited as precedent.

text: In that day, saith the LORD, will I assemble her that halteth, and I will gather her that is driven out, and her that I have afflicted; And I will make her that halted a remnant, and her that was cast far off a strong nation: and the LORD shall reign over them in mount Zion from henceforth, even for ever.
desc: The lame and outcaste remnant becoming a strong nation under the LORD's eternal reign from Zion.

text: Now why dost thou cry out aloud? is there no king in thee? is thy counsellor perished? for pangs have taken thee as a woman in travail. Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail: for now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go even to Babylon; there shalt thou be delivered; there the LORD shall redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies.
desc: Jerusalem going into Babylonian exile predicted by Micah, with redemption coming from that very captivity.

text: Now also many nations are gathered against thee, that say, Let her be defiled, and let our eye look upon Zion. But they know not the thoughts of the LORD, neither understand they his counsel: for he shall gather them as the sheaves into the floor.
desc: Nations gathered against Zion being threshed by daughter Zion, a pattern of end-times victory over Israel's enemies.

sub: He shall feed the flock; this man is the peace
text: Therefore will he give them up, until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth: then the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel.
desc: Following the Bethlehem prophecy (5:2), the Ruler who shepherds in the LORD's strength, is great to the ends of the earth, and is Himself 'the peace.'

text: And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD, that I will cut off thy horses out of the midst of thee, and I will destroy thy chariots: And I will cut off the cities of thy land, and throw down all thy strong holds:
desc: Israel's military fortifications and war horses removed in the messianic age when God alone is the source of security.

text: Therefore I will look unto the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation: my God will hear me. Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light unto me.
desc: Micah's personal declaration of hope in darkness, a model of faith leading to ultimate vindication.

text: Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity, and passeth by the transgression of the remnant of his heritage? he retaineth not his anger for ever, because he delighteth in mercy.
desc: God's final act of casting Israel's sins into the sea, the ultimate application of divine forgiveness.

sub: Nineveh — an utter end, not twice
text: The burden of Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite. God is jealous, and the LORD revengeth; the LORD revengeth, and is furious; the LORD will take vengeance on his adversaries, and he reserveth wrath for his enemies.
desc: Against the unconquerable capital of the world's superpower: 'He will make an utter end: affliction shall not rise up the second time.' In 612 BC the Medo-Babylonian coalition destroyed Nineveh so completely that within centuries its very location was forgotten.

text: He that dasheth in pieces is come up before thy face: keep the munition, watch the way, make thy loins strong, fortify thy power mightily. For the LORD hath turned away the excellency of Jacob, as the excellency of Israel: for the emptiers have emptied them out, and marred their vine branches.
desc: Nahum's vivid oracle of Nineveh's violent fall — the river-gates opened, the palace dissolved, the great Assyrian capital left empty and waste.

text: Behold ye among the heathen, and regard, and wonder marvellously: for I will work a work in your days, which ye will not believe, though it be told you. For, lo, I raise up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation, which shall march through the breadth of the land, to possess the dwellingplaces that are not theirs.
desc: God raising up Babylon as his instrument of judgment against Judah, Habakkuk's great theological puzzle.

text: And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it. For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.
desc: God's assurance that the vision of judgment will certainly come at the appointed time, quoted in Hebrews about Christ's return.

sub: God goes forth with His anointed
text: God came from Teman, and the Holy One from mount Paran. Selah. His glory covered the heavens, and the earth was full of his praise. And his brightness was as the light; he had horns coming out of his hand: and there was the hiding of his power.
desc: Habakkuk's theophany — God marching forth in radiant glory for the salvation of His people 'with thine anointed' — a vision of divine deliverance.

text: The word of the LORD which came unto Zephaniah the son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah, the son of Amariah, the son of Hizkiah, in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah.
desc: Comprehensive judgment on all of creation in the Day of the LORD as declared by Zephaniah.

sub: Judgment on the nations round about
text: Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired; Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the LORD come upon you, before the day of the LORD'S anger come upon you.
desc: Zephaniah's sweeping oracle against the nations around Judah — Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Cush, and Assyria/Nineveh — on the Day of the LORD.

text: Woe to her that is filthy and polluted, to the oppressing city! She obeyed not the voice; she received not correction; she trusted not in the LORD; she drew not near to her God.
desc: Jerusalem indicted for four failures, facing the same judgment pronounced on the nations.

text: Sing, O daughter of Zion; shout, O Israel; be glad and rejoice with all the heart, O daughter of Jerusalem. The LORD hath taken away thy judgments, he hath cast out thine enemy: the king of Israel, even the LORD, is in the midst of thee: thou shalt not see evil any more.
desc: The joyful song of Zion's final restoration with God himself dwelling in their midst, awaiting complete fulfillment.

text: Ye looked for much, and, lo, it came to little; and when ye brought it home, I did blow upon it. Why? saith the LORD of hosts. Because of mine house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house.
desc: God blowing away Israel's harvest for neglecting the temple, a call to prioritize God's house.

sub: The latter glory; the desire of all nations
text: For thus saith the LORD of hosts; Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land; And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory, saith the LORD of hosts.
desc: God will shake the nations and 'the desire of all nations' will come, filling the temple with a glory greater than the former — read of the Messiah entering the Second Temple.

sub: The chosen signet; the Davidic line preserved
text: … Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, saying, I will shake the heavens and the earth; And I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms, and I will destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the heathen; and I will overthrow the chariots, and those that ride in them; and the horses and their riders shall come down, every one by the sword of his brother.
desc: God's promise to make Zerubbabel His signet ring, reversing the curse on Jehoiachin — preserving the Messianic Davidic line.

text: So the angel that communed with me said unto me, Cry thou, saying, Thus saith the LORD of hosts; I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy. And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction.
desc: God returning to Jerusalem with mercy and the temple to be rebuilt, followed by the golden age of the rebuilt city.

sub: A wall of fire; nations joined to the LORD
text: I lifted up mine eyes again, and looked, and behold a man with a measuring line in his hand. Then said I, Whither goest thou? And he said unto me, To measure Jerusalem, to see what is the breadth thereof, and what is the length thereof.
desc: Zechariah's vision of a Jerusalem without walls, the LORD Himself her wall of fire and glory, with many nations joined to Him and God dwelling in her midst.

text: And he shewed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD, and Satan standing at his right hand to resist him. And the LORD said unto Satan, The LORD rebuke thee, O Satan; even the LORD that hath chosen Jerusalem rebuke thee: is not this a brand plucked out of the fire?
desc: The vision of Joshua the high priest accused by Satan, cleansed and reclothed, and the promise of God's servant the BRANCH who removes iniquity 'in one day.'

sub: By my Spirit; the day of small things
text: Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the LORD unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts.
desc: The word to Zerubbabel — the temple will be finished 'not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit' — and the call not to despise the day of small things.

text: … And speak unto him, saying, Thus speaketh the LORD of hosts, saying, Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the LORD: Even he shall build the temple of the LORD; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both.
desc: The symbolic crowning of Joshua, pointing to the BRANCH who will build the LORD's temple and uniquely be 'a priest upon his throne' — king and priest in one.

text: … Thus speaketh the LORD of hosts, saying, Execute true judgment, and shew mercy and compassions every man to his brother: And oppress not the widow, nor the fatherless, the stranger, nor the poor; and let none of you imagine evil against his brother in your heart.
desc: God questioning Israel's fasting and challenging them to true justice and mercy rather than ritual observance.

sub: Restored Jerusalem; the nations seek the LORD
text: Again the word of the LORD of hosts came to me, saying, Thus saith the LORD of hosts; I was jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and I was jealous for her with great fury.
desc: God's promise to return and dwell in Jerusalem, restoring its peace, with the nations seeking the LORD through His people.

text: And I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem, and the battle bow shall be cut off: and he shall speak peace unto the heathen: and his dominion shall be from sea even to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the earth.
desc: Following the lowly king on the donkey (9:9), the LORD disarms war and the King speaks peace to the nations, His dominion reaching to the ends of the earth.

text: As for thee also, by the blood of thy covenant I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water. Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope: even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee;
desc: Prisoners freed from the waterless pit by the blood of the covenant, pointing to Christ's blood releasing captives.

text: Mine anger was kindled against the shepherds, and I punished the goats: for the LORD of hosts hath visited his flock the house of Judah, and hath made them as his goodly horse in the battle.
desc: Israel to ask God for the latter rain of blessing in the messianic era, a spiritual promise of revival.

text: Thus saith the LORD my God; Feed the flock of the slaughter; Whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty: and they that sell them say, Blessed be the LORD; for I am rich: and their own shepherds pity them not.
desc: Zechariah's enacted prophecy of the good shepherd and the thirty pieces of silver, remarkably fulfilled in Judas's betrayal.

text: In that day shall there be a great mourning in Jerusalem, as the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon. And the land shall mourn, every family apart; the family of the house of David apart, and their wives apart; the family of the house of Nathan apart, and their wives apart;
desc: Israel mourning family by family for the one they pierced, the national repentance at the Second Coming.

text: In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and for uncleanness. And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD of hosts, that I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land, and they shall no more be remembered: and also I will cause the prophets and the unclean spirit to pass out of the land.
desc: The fountain of cleansing opened for Jerusalem, fulfilled in Christ's blood and the Spirit poured out at Pentecost.

text: And one shall say unto him, What are these wounds in thine hands? Then he shall answer, Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends.
desc: The pierced hands of the rejected shepherd acknowledged, a vivid portrait of Christ showing his wounds after resurrection.

sub: The Day of the LORD over Jerusalem
text: Behold, the day of the LORD cometh, and thy spoil shall be divided in the midst of thee. For I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle; and the city shall be taken, and the houses rifled, and the women ravished; and half of the city shall go forth into captivity, and the residue of the people shall not be cut off from the city.
desc: Zechariah foresees all nations gathered against Jerusalem on the Day of the LORD, and the LORD Himself going forth to fight for His city.

sub: One LORD, and His name one
text: And ye shall flee to the valley of the mountains; for the valley of the mountains shall reach unto Azal: yea, ye shall flee, like as ye fled from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah: and the LORD my God shall come, and all the saints with thee.
desc: The climax of Zechariah — the LORD comes with His saints, living waters flow from Jerusalem, and He is King over all the earth: 'one LORD, and his name one.'

sub: The King reigns; holiness fills the kingdom
text: And this shall be the plague wherewith the LORD will smite all the people that have fought against Jerusalem; Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth.
desc: The plague on the nations that warred against Jerusalem, and the survivors going up year by year to worship the King and keep the Feast of Tabernacles — the holiness of the kingdom age.

text: I have loved you, saith the LORD. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the LORD: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.
desc: God's elective love for Jacob over Esau declared, quoted by Paul as the foundational example of divine election.

text: And now, O ye priests, this commandment is for you. If ye will not hear, and if ye will not lay it to heart, to give glory unto my name, saith the LORD of hosts, I will even send a curse upon you, and I will curse your blessings: yea, I have cursed them already, because ye do not lay it to heart.
desc: Judgment on corrupt priests who dishonored God's name, pointing to the need for the perfect High Priest.

text: For I am the LORD, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed. Even from the days of your fathers ye are gone away from mine ordinances, and have not kept them. Return unto me, and I will return unto you, saith the LORD of hosts. But ye said, Wherein shall we return?
desc: God's challenge to test him with tithes and experience his overflowing blessing, the promise of covenant faithfulness.

text: Your words have been stout against me, saith the LORD. Yet ye say, What have we spoken so much against thee? Ye have said, It is vain to serve God: and what profit is it that we have kept his ordinance, and that we have walked mournfully before the LORD of hosts?
desc: God keeping a book of remembrance for those who fear him, an anticipation of the Lamb's Book of Life.

text: For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the LORD of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.
desc: The Day of the LORD burning the wicked like stubble in an oven, the great eschatological fire of judgment.

text: Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments. Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD:
desc: The closing of the Old Testament — the promise of 'Elijah' before the Day of the LORD, fulfilled (in part) in John the Baptist.

text: Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil. For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.
desc: Jesus declaring he came to fulfill the Law and Prophets, every detail secured until all is accomplished.

sub: A debated saying on His coming
text: But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.
desc: Jesus' debated saying that the disciples would not finish the cities of Israel before the Son of Man comes — a crux in the timing of His coming.

text: And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.
desc: Jesus's promise to build his church on the apostolic confession of faith, which hell's powers cannot overcome.

text: Verily I say unto you, There be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.
desc: Jesus' debated promise that some standing there would not die before seeing the Son of Man coming in His kingdom.

sub: Signs of the end of the age
text: And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?
desc: Jesus' answer to the disciples on the Mount of Olives, listing the signs preceding the end and promising the worldwide preaching of the gospel before the end comes.

sub: The abomination of desolation; great tribulation
text: When ye therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:) Then let them which be in Judaea flee into the mountains:
desc: Jesus' warning of the abomination of desolation in the holy place, the call to flee Judea, and the great tribulation — unequalled and, for the elect's sake, shortened.

text: Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Christ, or there; believe it not. For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect.
desc: Jesus warns against false christs and describes His own coming as unmistakable as lightning — visible, glorious, gathering the elect.

sub: Know that it is near, at the doors
text: Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh: So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.
desc: The parable of the fig tree — when its signs appear, the end is near, 'at the doors'; and the saying that 'this generation shall not pass' till all is fulfilled.

text: But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only. But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.
desc: Jesus declares the timing of His coming unknown and commands constant readiness, comparing the day to the suddenness of Noah's flood.

text: When the Son of man shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory: And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats:
desc: The final judgment of all nations at the Son of Man's glorious throne, separating sheep and goats.

text: Then saith Jesus unto them, All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad.
desc: Jesus predicting the disciples' desertion quoting Zechariah, fulfilled when all fled in Gethsemane.

text: Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, That this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.
desc: Jesus's specific prediction of Peter's three denials before cockcrow that very night, fulfilled exactly.

text: And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That there be some of them that stand here, which shall not taste of death, till they have seen the kingdom of God come with power.
desc: Mark's form of the saying: some would not die before seeing the kingdom of God come with power.

text: And as he went out of the temple, one of his disciples saith unto him, Master, see what manner of stones and what buildings are here! And Jesus answering said unto him, Seest thou these great buildings? there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.
desc: Mark's Olivet Discourse: the Temple's fall and the Son of Man's coming, closing with the charge to watch since the hour is unknown.

text: And Jesus saith unto them, All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered. But after that I am risen, I will go before you into Galilee.
desc: A double prediction on the way to Gethsemane: all the disciples will scatter that night, fulfilling Zechariah 13:7 ('smite the shepherd'), and after rising He will meet them in Galilee. Both happened exactly (Mk. 14:50; 16:7; Mt. 28:16).

text: And Jesus saith unto him, Verily I say unto thee, That this day, even in this night, before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice.
desc: Jesus predicts that before the rooster crows twice that same night, Peter will deny Him three times — fulfilled to the letter within hours (Mk. 14:66-72), against Peter's own vehement protest.

text: And the angel said unto her, Fear not, Mary: for thou hast found favour with God. And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS.
desc: Gabriel announcing to Mary the virgin conception and birth of Jesus, naming him and declaring his eternal kingdom.

text: Blessed are those servants, whom the lord when he cometh shall find watching: verily I say unto you, that he shall gird himself, and make them to sit down to meat, and will come forth and serve them.
desc: Jesus' parable of the watchful servants awaiting their returning master, calling for readiness and faithful stewardship since the hour is unknown.

sub: Sudden as lightning; as the days of Noah
text: And he said unto the disciples, The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see it. And they shall say to you, See here; or, see there: go not after them, nor follow them.
desc: Jesus describes His day as sudden and universally visible like lightning, coming upon an unprepared world as in the days of Noah and Lot.

text: For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side, And shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.
desc: Jesus predicting Jerusalem's encirclement by Roman armies with a wall, fulfilled by Titus's circumvallation wall in 70 AD.

text: And as some spake of the temple, how it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts, he said, As for these things which ye behold, the days will come, in the which there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.
desc: Luke's Olivet Discourse uniquely notes Jerusalem trodden by Gentiles 'until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled,' before the Son of Man's coming.

text: And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh. Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto.
desc: The military encirclement of Jerusalem as the signal to flee, fulfilled in 70 AD when Titus besieged the city.

text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live. For as the Father hath life in himself; so hath he given to the Son to have life in himself;
desc: The universal resurrection of both righteous and wicked at the voice of the Son of God, the final judgment.

text: And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day. And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.
desc: Jesus's promise to lose none of those given by the Father but raise them all at the last day.

text: In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.
desc: Jesus' promise to prepare a place in the Father's house and to return personally to receive His own to Himself.

text: And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.
desc: The promise of the Paraclete Spirit who would permanently indwell believers, fulfilled at Pentecost.

text: But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.
desc: The Holy Spirit as teacher and remembrancer of all Jesus's words, enabling the apostles to write the NT.

text: But when the Comforter is come, whom I will send unto you from the Father, even the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father, he shall testify of me: And ye also shall bear witness, because ye have been with me from the beginning.
desc: The Spirit proceeding from the Father sent by the Son to testify of Christ, central to the pneumatological controversy.

text: Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you.
desc: Jesus explaining the necessity of his departure for the Spirit's coming, the foundational logic of the Day of Pentecost.

text: Behold, the hour cometh, yea, is now come, that ye shall be scattered, every man to his own, and shall leave me alone: and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
desc: Jesus predicting the disciples' scattering, fulfilled in Gethsemane, with his assurance of the Father's presence.

text: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not.
desc: Jesus predicting Peter's death by crucifixion in old age, with his hands stretched out — fulfilled in Peter's inverted crucifixion under Nero.

text: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.
desc: The geographical expansion of the gospel from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth, the program of Acts fulfilled.

text: But this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel; And it shall come to pass in the last days, saith God, I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams:
desc: Peter applying Joel's Pentecost prophecy to the outpouring of the Spirit, declaring its fulfillment in Acts 2.

text: Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
desc: Peter's gospel proclamation at Pentecost citing Joel and Psalm 16, calling for repentance, baptism, and Spirit-reception.

text: For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope,
desc: Paul's vision of all creation groaning for liberation, tied to the believers' bodily resurrection and the renewal of the cosmos.

text: Esaias also crieth concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved: For he will finish the work, and cut it short in righteousness: because a short work will the Lord make upon the earth.
desc: Paul cites Isaiah 10:22-23 and 1:9: though Israel be as the sand of the sea, 'a remnant shall be saved' — and except the Lord had left a seed, 'we had been as Sodoma.' Israel's story is never total apostasy nor total preservation, but always a preserved core through judgment.

text: But I say, Did not Israel know? First Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people, and by a foolish nation I will anger you. But Esaias is very bold, and saith, I was found of them that sought me not; I was made manifest unto them that asked not after me.
desc: The Gentiles provoking Israel to jealousy, Paul's strategy in Romans to explain Israel's partial hardening and future restoration.

text: I say then, Have they stumbled that they should fall? God forbid: but rather through their fall salvation is come unto the Gentiles, for to provoke them to jealousy.
desc: 'Have they stumbled that they should fall? God forbid.' Israel's lapse became 'the riches of the Gentiles' — and their future fullness will be 'life from the dead.' Paul reads Israel's unbelief as a hinge in the plan, not its wreckage, and stakes a future reversal on it.

text: For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.
desc: Paul unveils 'this mystery': hardening has come on Israel in part, until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in — 'and so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer' (Isa. 59:20). A two-phase program with a stated sequence and a scriptural warrant.

text: Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power. For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet.
desc: Christ's mediatorial kingdom delivered to the Father after all enemies are subdued, the final act of eschatological history.

text: Behold, I shew you a mystery; We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed, In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.
desc: The mystery of the instant transformation of believers at the resurrection, Paul's most detailed rapture/resurrection passage.

text: But if the ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away:
desc: The greater glory of the New Covenant Spirit over the fading glory of the Old Covenant, fulfilled in Christ's ministry.

text: Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.
desc: Paul's argument that the Abrahamic seed promise was singular, pointing to Christ as the one in whom all nations are blessed.

text: Having made known unto us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure which he hath purposed in himself: That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth; even in him:
desc: God's ultimate purpose to sum up all things in Christ, the cosmic reconciliation and unification of creation.

text: Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth;
desc: Universal acknowledgment of Christ's Lordship by all creation, fulfilling Isaiah 45:23's worship of the one God.

text: For it pleased the Father that in him should all fulness dwell; And, having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things unto himself; by him, I say, whether they be things in earth, or things in heaven.
desc: Christ's blood making peace and reconciling all things to God, the cosmic scope of the atonement's ultimate effect.

sub: Day of the Lord; children of light
text: But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you. For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night.
desc: Paul teaches that the Day of the Lord comes unexpectedly like a thief, but believers, as children of light, are to watch and be sober.

text: And to you who are troubled rest with us, when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels, In flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God, and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ:
desc: Christ revealed from heaven in flaming fire executing vengeance on the ungodly, the eschatological judgment.

sub: Consumed by the brightness of His coming
text: And then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming:
desc: The lawless one, once revealed, is consumed by the breath of the Lord's mouth and destroyed by the splendor of His coming — the Antichrist's certain doom.

text: Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils; Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron;
desc: The Holy Spirit's explicit warning of apostasy in the last times, forbidding marriage and foods.

text: This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy,
desc: Paul's catalog of last-days character deterioration, a pattern increasingly evident in every generation.

text: I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom;
desc: Paul's solemn charge invoking the coming judgment of the living and dead at Christ's appearing and kingdom.

text: God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds;
desc: The Son as God's final and supreme word surpassing all prophetic revelation, the beginning of the last days age.

text: For unto the angels hath he not put in subjection the world to come, whereof we speak. But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him?
desc: Psalm 8's human destiny fulfilled in Jesus who was briefly lowered then exalted, tasting death as the representative man.

text: For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah:
desc: Hebrews quoting Jeremiah 31's New Covenant as making the Old obsolete, established in Christ's blood.

text: But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool.
desc: Christ reigning until the last enemy death is destroyed, the Millennium ending when death is cast into the lake of fire.

text: Whose voice then shook the earth: but now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven. And this word, Yet once more, signifieth the removing of those things that are shaken, as of things that are made, that those things which cannot be shaken may remain.
desc: The final cosmic shaking leaving only the unshakeable kingdom, Hebrews applying Haggai 2:6 to the eschatological transformation.

text: Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you. Your riches are corrupted, and your garments are motheaten.
desc: James's warning to the exploiting rich of coming misery, fulfilled in Jerusalem's fall and the eschatological judgment.

sub: Salvation revealed in the last time
text: Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
desc: Peter assures believers they are guarded by God's power for a salvation ready to be revealed at the last time — the unveiling at Christ's coming.

text: But the end of all things is at hand: be ye therefore sober, and watch unto prayer.
desc: Peter's announcement that the end of all things is near, grounding a call to sober, prayerful, watchful living.

text: For the time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God: and if it first begin at us, what shall the end be of them that obey not the gospel of God? And if the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?
desc: Divine judgment beginning with God's own household first, the principle fulfilled in every persecution and ultimately the last judgment.

text: Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts, And saying, Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.
desc: End-times scoffers mocking the Second Coming promise, Paul and Peter both identifying this as a sign of the last days.

text: But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night; in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up.
desc: After the dissolution of the present order by fire, Peter directs hope to the promised new heavens and new earth in which righteousness dwells.

text: Little children, it is the last time: and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists; whereby we know that it is the last time.
desc: John identifying the spirit of antichrist already at work, with the final Antichrist yet to come.

sub: Abide, that we may have confidence
text: And now, little children, abide in him; that, when he shall appear, we may have confidence, and not be ashamed before him at his coming.
desc: John's pastoral charge to abide in Christ so that believers may have confidence, not shame, at His appearing.

text: Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.
desc: John's promise that at Christ's appearing believers will be transformed to be like Him, seeing Him as He is.

sub: The Lord comes with His saints
text: And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.
desc: Jude cites Enoch's ancient prophecy of the Lord coming with His holy myriads to execute judgment on the ungodly.

text: Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him. Even so, Amen.
desc: John's keynote promise that Christ will return visibly and universally, seen by all, including those who pierced Him.

text: He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God.
desc: The promise to the overcomer at Ephesus — to eat of the tree of life in the paradise of God, the Eden lost now restored.

text: He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it.
desc: The promise to the overcomer at Pergamos — the hidden manna, a white stone, and a new name known only to the one who receives it.

text: And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers: even as I received of my Father.
desc: The promise to the overcomer at Thyatira — to share Christ's rule over the nations (Psalm 2) and to receive the morning star, Christ Himself.

text: He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.
desc: The promise to the overcomer at Sardis — white raiment, his name kept in the book of life, and confessed by Christ before the Father.

text: Because thou hast kept the word of my patience, I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world, to try them that dwell upon the earth.
desc: The promise to faithful Philadelphia — to be kept from the hour of trial coming on all the world — a key text in the rapture-timing discussion.

text: Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven from my God: and I will write upon him my new name.
desc: The promise to the overcomer — made a permanent pillar in God's temple, inscribed with the name of God, of the New Jerusalem, and Christ's new name.

text: To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne.
desc: The climactic overcomer promise — to sit with Christ on His throne, as He overcame and sat down with the Father.

text: And I saw when the Lamb opened one of the seals, and I heard, as it were the noise of thunder, one of the four beasts saying, Come and see. And I saw, and behold a white horse: and he that sat on him had a bow; and a crown was given unto him: and he went forth conquering, and to conquer.
desc: The Lamb opens the seven seals, loosing the four horsemen (conquest, war, famine, death), the martyrs' cry, and cosmic upheaval — the opening movement of Revelation's judgments.

text: And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree.
desc: Between the sixth and seventh seals, the sealing of the 144,000 from the tribes of Israel — held back from the four winds of judgment until the servants of God are marked.

sub: Escalating judgments on an unrepentant world
text: And when he had opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven about the space of half an hour. And I saw the seven angels which stood before God; and to them were given seven trumpets.
desc: Six of the seven trumpets — hail and fire, the burning mountain, Wormwood, darkened lights, the demonic locusts, and the army from the Euphrates — escalating judgments that still leave humanity unrepentant. The seventh sounds at Revelation 11:15, a separate entry here.

sub: The two witnesses and the seventh trumpet
text: And I saw another mighty angel come down from heaven, clothed with a cloud: and a rainbow was upon his head, and his face was as it were the sun, and his feet as pillars of fire:
desc: The mighty angel and the little scroll, the measuring of the temple, the two witnesses who prophesy, are killed, and rise, and the seventh trumpet announcing the kingdom.

text: And there appeared a great wonder in heaven; a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars: And she being with child cried, travailing in birth, and pained to be delivered.
desc: The cosmic sign — the woman, the male child caught up to God, the dragon (Satan) cast down, and his war on the woman's offspring — the conflict behind history.

sub: The beast from the sea and the false prophet
text: And saw a beast rise up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns, and upon his heads the name of blasphemy. And the beast which I saw was like unto a leopard, and his feet were as the feet of a bear, and his mouth as the mouth of a lion: and the dragon gave him his power, and his seat, and great authority.
desc: The beast from the sea (the blasphemous world-power) and the beast from the earth (the false prophet) who enforces its worship and mark — 666.

sub: The Lamb on Zion; the grain and grape harvest
text: And I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father's name written in their foreheads. And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps:
desc: The Lamb and the 144,000 on Mount Zion, the three angels' messages, the blessing on those who die in the Lord, and the twin harvest — the grain and the winepress of wrath.

text: And I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvellous, seven angels having the seven last plagues; for in them is filled up the wrath of God. And I saw as it were a sea of glass mingled with fire: and them that had gotten the victory over the beast, and over his image, and over his mark, and over the number of his name, stand on the sea of glass, having the harps of God.
desc: The seven last plagues — the bowls of God's wrath poured on the earth, sea, rivers, sun, the beast's throne, the Euphrates (Armageddon), and the air — completing God's judgment.

sub: The harlot on the scarlet beast
text: And there came one of the seven angels which had the seven vials, and talked with me, saying unto me, Come hither; I will shew unto thee the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters:
desc: Babylon the great — the harlot on the seven-headed beast, drunk with the blood of the saints — and the angel's interpretation of the heads and horns.

sub: Come out of her, my people
text: And after these things I saw another angel come down from heaven, having great power; and the earth was lightened with his glory. And he cried mightily with a strong voice, saying, Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird.
desc: The fall of Babylon the great — the call to God's people to come out of her, and the lament of kings, merchants, and sailors over the city's sudden ruin.

text: And after these things I heard a great voice of much people in heaven, saying, Alleluia; Salvation, and glory, and honour, and power, unto the Lord our God: For true and righteous are his judgments: for he hath judged the great whore, which did corrupt the earth with her fornication, and hath avenged the blood of his servants at her hand.
desc: John's vision of the heavenly Bridegroom returning as the conquering King of kings to judge and to reign, following the marriage supper of the Lamb.

text: And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.
desc: John pronounces blessed those in the first resurrection, who escape the second death and reign as priests with Christ a thousand years.

text: And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison, And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea.
desc: After the thousand years, Satan is loosed, gathers Gog and Magog against the saints, and is cast forever into the lake of fire — the final defeat of evil.

text: And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them. And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.
desc: The final judgment — the dead raised before the great white throne, judged by their works from the books, with the book of life decisive — and death itself cast into the lake of fire.  This is the judgment of the unsaved dead; the redeemed are judged separately — at the judgment seat of Christ (the bema), for reward, not condemnation (2 Cor. 5:10; 1 Cor. 3:11-15). See “Two judgments, one Judge” on the Eschatology page.

text: And there came unto me one of the seven angels which had the seven vials full of the seven last plagues, and talked with me, saying, Come hither, I will shew thee the bride, the Lamb's wife.
desc: John's vision of the New Jerusalem descending from God — the eternal dwelling of God with His people, lit by the glory of God and the Lamb.

sub: River of life; the curse undone
text: And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb. In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.
desc: The river and tree of life in the New Jerusalem, where the curse is undone and God's servants behold His face and reign forever.

sub: I come quickly; the First and the Last
text: And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be. I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last.
desc: Christ's closing promise of imminent return with recompense, declaring Himself Alpha and Omega — the very title YHWH claims in Isaiah.

text: For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet.
desc: Psalm 22's description of hands and feet pierced, directly prefiguring the wounds of crucifixion.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture.
desc: The gambling for Jesus's garments fulfilled at the crucifixion exactly as written in Psalm 22.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive: thou hast received gifts for men; yea, for the rebellious also, that the LORD God might dwell among them.
desc: Christ's ascension and leading captivity captive, cited by Paul in Ephesians 4:8 as fulfilled in the ascension.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: Reproach hath broken my heart; and I am full of heaviness: and I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; and for comforters, but I found none. They gave me also gall for my meat; and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
desc: The gall and vinegar given to the Suffering Servant, fulfilled at the cross when soldiers offered Jesus vinegar and gall.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: He shall cry unto me, Thou art my father, my God, and the rock of my salvation. Also I will make him my firstborn, higher than the kings of the earth.
desc: The Davidic Son crying 'My Father' and set as firstborn over all kings, fulfilled in Christ's exaltation.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: The LORD hath sworn, and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.
desc: The eternal priesthood after Melchizedek's order, the anchor of Hebrews' argument for Christ's superior high priesthood.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: And he shall pass through Judah; he shall overflow and go over, he shall reach even to the neck; and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel.
desc: Amid the Assyrian threat, the land is addressed as belonging to 'Immanuel' — tying the chapter to the Immanuel prophecy of 7:14.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

sub: The people in darkness see a great light
text: Nevertheless the dimness shall not be such as was in her vexation, when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.
desc: The light dawning in 'Galilee of the nations' on a people in darkness — which Matthew applies directly to Jesus' Galilean ministry.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

sub: Servant Song 1: justice to the nations
text: He shall not cry, nor lift up, nor cause his voice to be heard in the street. A bruised reed shall he not break, and the smoking flax shall he not quench: he shall bring forth judgment unto truth.
desc: The first Servant Song — the gentle, Spirit-endowed Servant who brings justice to the nations without breaking the bruised reed, applied by Matthew directly to Jesus.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: I have sworn by myself, the word is gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and shall not return, That unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear.
desc: The LORD's oath that to Him alone every knee will bow and every tongue confess — applied by Paul directly to Jesus (Philippians 2:10; Romans 14:11).
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

sub: Despised by the nation; honored by kings
text: Thus saith the LORD, the Redeemer of Israel, and his Holy One, to him whom man despiseth, to him whom the nation abhorreth, to a servant of rulers, Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship, because of the LORD that is faithful, and the Holy One of Israel, and he shall choose thee.
desc: The Servant despised and abhorred by the nation, before whom kings will yet rise and princes worship — humiliation reversed into honor.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

sub: Servant Song 4: high and lifted up, visage marred
text: Behold, my servant shall deal prudently, he shall be exalted and extolled, and be very high. As many were astonied at thee; his visage was so marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men:
desc: The prologue of the fourth Servant Song — the Servant exalted yet whose appearance is marred beyond recognition, who sprinkles many nations and silences kings.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground: he hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him.
desc: The Servant's humble, unattractive appearance with no royal form — the incarnate Christ's unimpressive humanity.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted. But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.
desc: Vicarious suffering bearing our griefs and wounds, the cornerstone of Isaiah 53's substitutionary atonement theology.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.
desc: Universal human straying and collective sin laid on the Servant, the breadth of vicarious substitution.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth.
desc: The Suffering Servant silent before His oppressors, led 'as a lamb to the slaughter' — the very text the Ethiopian was reading when Philip preached Jesus.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: He was taken from prison and from judgment: and who shall declare his generation? for he was cut off out of the land of the living: for the transgression of my people was he stricken.
desc: The Servant cut off from the land of the living for the people's transgression, the death of Christ for sin.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: Yet it pleased the LORD to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the LORD shall prosper in his hand.
desc: The Father's purpose in the Servant's sin offering, followed by resurrection life ('prolong his days') and spiritual offspring.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied: by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities.
desc: The Servant satisfied seeing the fruit of his suffering, justifying many by bearing their iniquities.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

sub: He bare the sin of many and interceded
text: Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he hath poured out his soul unto death: and he was numbered with the transgressors; and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.
desc: The Servant's vindication and the reason — He poured out His soul to death, was numbered with transgressors, bore many's sin, and interceded — words Jesus claimed at the Last Supper.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

sub: The Redeemer and the covenant of the Spirit
text: And the Redeemer shall come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob, saith the LORD. As for me, this is my covenant with them, saith the LORD; My spirit that is upon thee, and my words which I have put in thy mouth, shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of thy seed's seed, saith the LORD, from henceforth and for ever.
desc: The Redeemer coming to Zion and God's covenant of Spirit and word — which Paul cites of the salvation of Israel (Rom. 11:26-27).
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: And David my servant shall be king over them; and they all shall have one shepherd: they shall also walk in my judgments, and observe my statutes, and do them. And they shall dwell in the land that I have given unto Jacob my servant, wherein your fathers have dwelt; and they shall dwell therein, even they, and their children, and their children's children for ever: and my servant David shall be their prince for ever.
desc: David's servant-king (Christ) over the unified nation with one shepherd, fulfilled in the millennial kingdom.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

sub: Cosmic signs; the Day of the LORD
text: And I will shew wonders in the heavens and in the earth, blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and the terrible day of the LORD come.
desc: Joel's signs in heaven and earth heralding the great Day of the LORD — the oracle Peter cites at Pentecost as the dawn of the last days.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

sub: The Judge struck on the cheek
text: Now gather thyself in troops, O daughter of troops: he hath laid siege against us: they shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek.
desc: Immediately before the Bethlehem prophecy, the 'judge of Israel' struck on the cheek with a rod — read of the smiting of the Messiah.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: And speak unto him, saying, Thus speaketh the LORD of hosts, saying, Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the LORD:
desc: The Branch who is both king and priest, building the eschatological temple — a dual office fulfilled in Christ.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: Then certain of the scribes and of the Pharisees answered, saying, Master, we would see a sign from thee. But he answered and said unto them, An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas:
desc: Jesus citing Jonah as the sign of his burial and resurrection on the third day.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: From that time forth began Jesus to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.
desc: Immediately after Peter's confession, a program change: 'From that time forth began Jesus to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer… and be killed, and be raised again the third day.' Location, actors (elders, chief priests, scribes), outcome, and timetable — announced months in advance.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: And while they abode in Galilee, Jesus said unto them, The Son of man shall be betrayed into the hands of men: And they shall kill him, and the third day he shall be raised again. And they were exceeding sorry.
desc: The second passion prediction — betrayal, death, and third-day resurrection — all fulfilled exactly.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man shall be betrayed unto the chief priests and unto the scribes, and they shall condemn him to death, And shall deliver him to the Gentiles to mock, and to scourge, and to crucify him: and the third day he shall rise again.
desc: The third prediction adds granular detail on the road up to Jerusalem: betrayed to the chief priests; condemned; delivered to the Gentiles; mocked, scourged, crucified; raised the third day. Six specific stages, every one fulfilled within weeks — including the transfer to Rome, which Jewish condemnation alone would not have entailed.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: And when they drew nigh unto Jerusalem, and were come to Bethphage, unto the mount of Olives, then sent Jesus two disciples, Saying unto them, Go into the village over against you, and straightway ye shall find an ass tied, and a colt with her: loose them, and bring them unto me.
desc: Jesus deliberately sends for the donkey and colt so that Zechariah 9:9 — 'thy King cometh unto thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass' — is fulfilled in public view at the exact Passover of His death. Matthew cites the prophecy verbatim.
trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

text: Jesus saith unto them, Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner: this is the Lord's doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?
desc: Jesus applying Psalm 118:22 to himself — the stone the Jewish leaders rejected would become the cornerstone.

trad_Oneness: Oneness Pentecostal reading: this passage, read through the lens of absolute monotheism (Col. 2:9), points to the one God fully revealed in Jesus Christ. See the Oneness tab for full Name Theology framework.

desc: Stephen, before the Sanhedrin, cites Moses' own prophecy: 'A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me' (Deut. 18:15) — the raised-up Prophet whom Peter (Acts 3:22) and the crowds (Jn. 6:14) identify as Jesus.

text: After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up: That the residue of men might seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called, saith the Lord, who doeth all these things.

keywords: John 5:39|John 5:46|search the scriptures|they testify of me|Moses wrote of me|all scripture points to Jesus|John 5:18|John 5:16
text: Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.
desc: Search the scriptures... they are they which testify of me — Jesus' own claim that the Hebrew Scriptures point to him.
trad_Jewish: John 5 records sharp conflict; the claim that all the Hebrew Scriptures 'testify' of Jesus is the fundamental Christian-Jewish divide. Judaism reads the Tanakh as God's covenant with Israel, not as pointing to Jesus.
trad_Catholic: Christ is the key to all the Scriptures, which find their meaning in Him (Luke 24:27); the Old Testament is read in light of the New (cf. the Catechism).
trad_Protestant: A foundational text for Christ-centered interpretation — the Scriptures testify of Jesus; to search them apart from Him misses their goal (cf. Luke 24:44).
trad_Oneness: This is the keystone of the apostolic reading: Jesus declares that all the Scriptures 'testify of me' (v. 39), and 'had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me' (v. 46). The Law, the Prophets, and the Psalms point to one Person — the Lord Jesus. John 5 also shows what it cost: from here 'the Jews sought the more to kill him... because he... said also that God was his Father, making himself equal with God' (5:16-18). But Jesus' own answer is that 'the Son can do nothing of himself' — the Father dwelling in Him does the works (5:19, 30; 14:10): not a second God beside the Father, but the Father's Son, God manifest in flesh. The One of whom all Scripture testifies is the one God come as Saviour.
trad_Academic: John 5 is pivotal in the Gospel's structure — the first major controversy and the unfolding of Jesus' relation to the Father; v. 39 (indicative vs. imperative 'search') and the scripture-witness theme are much discussed.
